its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿يَنْفَعُهُمْ إِيمانُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and its mafʿūl bihi, and إيمانهم is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of يك, and the clause لم يك is resumptive. ﴿لَمَّا﴾ adverbial, meaning "when" (ḥīna). ﴿رَأَوْا بَأْسَنا﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿سُنَّتَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of سنة. ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). ﴿خَلَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿فِي عِبادِهِ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَخَسِرَ﴾ a resumptive particle, and a past verb. ﴿هُنالِكَ﴾ a demonstrative in the position of accusative as an adverb of place. ﴿الْكافِرُونَ﴾ fāʿil, nominative by the wāw; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:1-5.t: ﴿حم﴾ letters with no grammatical position. ﴿تَنْزِيلُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْكِتابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿الْعَزِيزِ﴾ badal (substitute). ﴿الْعَلِيمِ﴾ a second badal. ﴿غافِرِ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty. ﴿الذَّنْبِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَقابِلِ﴾ conjoined to غافر. ﴿التَّوْبِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿شَدِيدِ﴾ also an adjective. ﴿الْعِقابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ذِي﴾ an adjective, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ. ﴿الطَّوْلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation, operating like inna. ﴿إِلهَ﴾ its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and its khabar is omitted. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿هُوَ﴾ badal of the pronoun latent (mustatir) in the omitted khabar. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar. ﴿الْمَصِيرُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause لا إله إلّا هو is resumptive, and the second nominal clause is also resumptive. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿يُجادِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿فِي آياتِ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a postponed fāʿil (agent). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its agent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause يجادل is resumptive. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ of the implied condition), and lā is of prohibition. ﴿يَغْرُرْكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lā, and the kāf is its object. ﴿تَقَلُّبُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿فِي الْبِلادِ﴾ the two are attached to تقلبهم; the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿كَذَّبَتْ﴾ a past verb. ﴿قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿قَوْمُ﴾ a postponed agent. ﴿نُوحٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَحْزابُ﴾ conjoined to قوم. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَهَمَّتْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb conjoined to كذبت. ﴿كُلُّ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿أُمَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِرَسُولِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to همت. ﴿لِيَأْخُذُوهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of causation (lām al-taʿlīl); the wāw is its agent and the hāʾ its object; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and the verb is in the position of genitive by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to همت. ﴿وَجادَلُوا﴾ a past verb and its agent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِالْباطِلِ﴾ the two are attached to جادلوا. ﴿لِيُدْحِضُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied an after the lām of causation. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَأَخَذْتُهُمْ﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb, its agent and its object. ﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾ a resumptive particle, and كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a fronted khabar. ﴿كانَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿عِقابِ﴾ the postponed noun of kāna; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-8.t: ﴿وَكَذلِكَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the kāf is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "والأمر كذلك" (and the matter is thus). ﴿حَقَّتْ﴾ a past verb. ﴿كَلِمَةُ﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its agent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿أَصْحابُ﴾ its khabar. ﴿النَّارِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from anna and what follows it is a badal (substitute) of كلمة. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَحْمِلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its agent. ﴿الْعَرْشَ﴾ its object; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a relative noun conjoined to الذين. ﴿حَوْلَهُ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿يُسَبِّحُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its agent; the clause is the khabar of الذين. ﴿بِحَمْدِ﴾ the two are attached to يسبحون. ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَيُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ conjoined to يسبحون. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to يؤمنون. ﴿وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ the two are attached to يستغفرون. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its agent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ a munādā (the one addressed) that is muḍāf; the vocative clause is the object of an omitted verb of saying. ﴿وَسِعْتَ﴾ a past verb and its agent. ﴿كُلَّ﴾ its object. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿وَعِلْماً﴾ conjoined to رحمة. ﴿فَاغْفِرْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ of the implied condition), and a verb of supplication, its agent latent (mustatir). ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ the two are attached to اغفر. ﴿تابُوا﴾ a past verb and its agent; the clause is the ṣila, and the clause اغفر is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا﴾ conjoined to تابوا. ﴿سَبِيلَكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَقِهِمْ﴾ a conjunction, and a verb of supplication, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; the agent is latent and the hāʾ is the first object. ﴿عَذابَ﴾ second object. ﴿الْجَحِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ a munādā that is muḍāf, and nā is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَأَدْخِلْهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a verb of supplication and its first object, the agent latent. ﴿جَنَّاتِ﴾ its second object. ﴿عَدْنٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ an adjective. ﴿وَعَدْتَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its agent and its object; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a conjunction, and مَن is a relative noun conjoined to the object of وعدتهم. ﴿صَلَحَ﴾ a past verb, its agent latent. ﴿مِنْ آبائِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَأَزْواجِهِمْ وَذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ﴾ conjoined. ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ two khabars; the nominal clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause of inna gives the reason (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:9-12.t: ﴿وَقِهِمُ﴾ a conjunction, and a verb of supplication, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir) and the hāʾ is its first object. ﴿السَّيِّئاتِ﴾ its second object. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and مَن is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿تَقِ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the weak letter. ﴿السَّيِّئاتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb of time annexed to one like it. ﴿فَقَدْ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and qad is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of مَن. ﴿رَحِمْتَهُ﴾ a past verb, its agent and its object; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. ﴿وَذلِكَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْفَوْزُ﴾ khabar. ﴿الْعَظِيمُ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of الفوز; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its agent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause of inna is resumptive. ﴿يُنادَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿لَمَقْتُ﴾ the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), and مقت is mubtadaʾ. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَكْبَرُ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is the object of ينادون. ﴿مِنْ مَقْتِكُمْ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to أكبر. ﴿أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi of مقتكم. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿تُدْعَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿إِلَى الْإِيمانِ﴾ the two are attached to تدعون. ﴿فَتَكْفُرُونَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its agent; the clause is conjoined to تدعون. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its agent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ a munādā (the one addressed) that is muḍāf; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying). ﴿أَمَتَّنَا﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿اثْنَتَيْنِ﴾ a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq). ﴿وَأَحْيَيْتَنَا اثْنَتَيْنِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَاعْتَرَفْنا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِذُنُوبِنا﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and هل is interrogative. ﴿إِلى خُرُوجٍ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿سَبِيلٍ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ, genitive in form; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ذلِكُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِأَنَّهُ﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition, anna is a particle resembling the verb, and the hāʾ is its noun. ﴿إِذا﴾ adverbial, conditional. ﴿دُعِيَ اللَّهُ﴾ a passive past verb and nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿وَحْدَهُ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿كَفَرْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its agent; the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position. The conditional clause and its apodosis are the khabar of anna; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from anna and what follows it is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar of ذلكم; the clause ذلكم is resumptive. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ a jussive conditional particle. ﴿يُشْرَكْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿تُؤْمِنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis, and the wāw is its agent; the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position, and the clause يشرك is initial, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَالْحُكْمُ﴾ a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿الْعَلِيِّ الْكَبِيرِ﴾ two badals (substitutes) of the Name of Majesty.

daas-irab:13-16.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿يُرِيكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the kāf is its first object. ﴿آياتِهِ﴾ its second object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَيُنَزِّلُ﴾ conjoined to يريكم. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ the two are also attached to the verb. ﴿رِزْقاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and mā is negative. ﴿يَتَذَكَّرُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿مِنَ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil (agent) «[Translator's note: the word is مَنْ in the ayah.]». ﴿يُنِيبُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila, and the clause ما يتذكر is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَادْعُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ of the implied condition), and an imperative verb and its agent. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its object. ﴿مُخْلِصِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two are attached to the ḥāl. ﴿الدِّينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi of مخلصين. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is of the ḥāl and law is connective (waṣliyya). ﴿كَرِهَ الْكافِرُونَ﴾ a past verb and its agent, nominative by the wāw; the clause is a ḥāl, and the clause ادعوا is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿رَفِيعُ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿الدَّرَجاتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ذُو﴾ a second khabar of the omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْعَرْشِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يُلْقِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent latent. ﴿الرُّوحَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a third khabar. ﴿مِنْ أَمْرِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb before them. ﴿عَلى مَنْ﴾ the two are also attached to the verb. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its agent latent. ﴿مِنْ عِبادِهِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied an after the lām of causation (lām al-taʿlīl); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of genitive by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to يلقى; the agent of ينذر is omitted. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿التَّلاقِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal (substitute) of the preceding يوم. ﴿هُمْ بارِزُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَخْفى﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative. ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿شَيْءٌ﴾ the agent of يخفى. ﴿لِمَنِ﴾ the two are attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿الْمُلْكُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ the two are attached to the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "الملك كائن" (the dominion is…). ﴿الْواحِدِ﴾ badal of الله. ﴿الْقَهَّارِ﴾ an adjective.

daas-irab:17-20.t: ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿تُجْزى﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿كُلُّ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿نَفْسٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿كَسَبَتْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لا ظُلْمَ﴾ lā is the lā of generic negation, and its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and its khabar (predicate) is omitted. ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time; the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya). ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ﴾ inna, the Name of Majesty its noun and سريع its khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿الْحِسابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَأَنْذِرْهُمْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and an imperative verb, its agent latent, and the hāʾ is its first object. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ its second object. ﴿الْآزِفَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِذِ﴾ badal (substitute) of يوم. ﴿الْقُلُوبُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لَدَى﴾ an adverb of place attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿الْحَناجِرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿كاظِمِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb); the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿لِلظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿حَمِيمٍ﴾ genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَلا شَفِيعٍ﴾ conjoined to من حميم; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يُطاعُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb with a latent nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of شفيع. ﴿يَعْلَمُ خائِنَةَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, the agent latent. ﴿الْأَعْيُنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَما﴾ a conjunction, and mā is a relative noun conjoined to خائنة. ﴿تُخْفِي الصُّدُورُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَقْضِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its agent latent; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its agent. ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَقْضُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause is the khabar of الذين. ﴿بِشَيْءٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ﴾ the two khabars of inna; the nominal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:21-22.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī) and the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿يَسِيرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿فَيَنْظُرُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and ينظروا is conjoined to يسيروا. ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of kāna. ﴿عاقِبَةُ﴾ its noun; the clause كيف كان is in the position of accusative as the object of ينظروا. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar of كانوا. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿هُمْ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿أَشَدَّ﴾ its khabar. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to أشد. ﴿قُوَّةً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿وَآثاراً﴾ conjoined to قوة. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ the two are attached to آثارا. ﴿فَأَخَذَهُمُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its object. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿بِذُنُوبِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is of the ḥāl (circumstantial) and mā is negative. ﴿كانَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to its fronted khabar. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ the two are attached to واق. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿واقٍ﴾ a noun genitive in form, nominative in position, the postponed noun of kāna; the verbal clause ما كان is a ḥāl. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition, and anna and its noun. ﴿كانَتْ﴾ an incomplete past verb, its noun latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar of anna; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from anna and what follows it is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, the two being attached to the omitted khabar of ذلك, and the clause ذلك is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿تَأْتِيهِمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object. ﴿رُسُلُهُمْ﴾ its agent; the clause is the khabar of كانت. ﴿بِالْبَيِّناتِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿فَكَفَرُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَأَخَذَهُمُ﴾ conjoined to فكفروا. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿إِنَّهُ قَوِيٌّ﴾ inna, its noun and its first khabar. ﴿شَدِيدُ﴾ a second khabar. ﴿الْعِقابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:23-25.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and a preposition, the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and qad is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿أَرْسَلْنا مُوسى﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to أرسلنا; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying) «[Translator's note: so in the source; no verb of saying precedes here.]». ﴿وَسُلْطانٍ﴾ conjoined to آياتنا. ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ a naʿt (adjective); the clause أرسلنا is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أرسلنا. ﴿وَهامانَ﴾ ﴿وَقارُونَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿فَقالُوا﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its agent; the clause is conjoined to أرسلنا. ﴿ساحِرٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَذَّابٌ﴾ a second khabar; the nominal clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and lammā is an adverbial, non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object, its agent latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِنا﴾ the two are also attached to the verb. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its agent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿اقْتُلُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its agent. ﴿أَبْناءَ﴾ its object. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its agent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿مَعَهُ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿وَاسْتَحْيُوا نِساءَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle and mā is negative. ﴿كَيْدُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْكافِرِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿فِي ضَلالٍ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted khabar; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:26-28.t: ﴿وَقالَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿فِرْعَوْنُ﴾ its fāʿil (agent). ﴿ذَرُونِي﴾ an imperative verb; the wāw is its agent, the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya) and the yāʾ is its object; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying). ﴿أَقْتُلْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), its agent latent (mustatir). ﴿مُوسى﴾ its object. ﴿وَلْيَدْعُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām of command, its agent latent. ﴿رَبَّهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it, and the clause أقتل is also the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿أَخافُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its agent latent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause gives the reason for the command. ﴿أَنْ يُبَدِّلَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, its agent latent. ﴿دِينَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿أَنْ يُظْهِرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an, its agent latent. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿الْفَسادَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَقالَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿مُوسى﴾ its agent. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿عُذْتُ﴾ a past verb and its agent; the nominal clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿بِرَبِّي﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَرَبِّكُمْ﴾ conjoined to بربي; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مُتَكَبِّرٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُؤْمِنُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent latent; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of متكبر. ﴿بِيَوْمِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿الْحِسابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَقالَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a past verb. ﴿رَجُلٌ﴾ its agent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مُؤْمِنٌ﴾ an adjective. ﴿مِنْ آلِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted second adjective of رجل. ﴿فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَكْتُمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent latent. ﴿إِيمانَهُ﴾ its object; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَتَقْتُلُونَ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its agent; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿رَجُلًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنْ يَقُولَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative, its agent latent. ﴿رَبِّيَ اللَّهُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar; the nominal clause is the maqūl al-qawl, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and what follows it is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is of the ḥāl and qad is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿جاءَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object, the agent latent; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿بِالْبَيِّناتِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ the two are also attached to the verb. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and in is conditional. ﴿يَكُ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn implied on the nūn, which is omitted for lightness; its noun is latent. ﴿كاذِباً﴾ its khabar. ﴿فَعَلَيْهِ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿كَذِبُهُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the clause يك is initial. ﴿وَإِنْ يَكُ صادِقاً يُصِبْكُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بَعْضُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَعِدُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, the agent latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent latent; the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and khabar. ﴿كَذَّابٌ﴾ a second khabar; the nominal clause is the ṣila of مَن.

dervis-irab:47-52.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَتَحاجُّونَ): they dispute with one another. One says: حاجّه حجاجا ومحاجّة ومحاجة, meaning he disputed with him; and المحجاج is one who disputes a great deal.
(تَبَعاً): plural of تابع (follower), like خدم, plural of خادم; or it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description.
(جَهَنَّمَ): discussion of it will come in the section on rhetoric.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ يَتَحاجُّونَ فِي النَّارِ فَيَقُولُ الضُّعَفاءُ لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا): the wāw is resumptive, and إذ is an adverb of past time attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "Mention, O Muhammad, to your people"; the clause يتحاجون is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) because the adverb is annexed to it; في النار is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يتحاجون; the fāʾ is of ramification (tafrīʿiyya), detailing the mutual disputing and quarrelling; يقول الضعفاء is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); للذين is attached to يقول; and the clause استكبروا is the ṣila (relative clause).
(إِنَّا كُنَّا لَكُمْ تَبَعاً فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُغْنُونَ عَنَّا نَصِيباً مِنَ النَّارِ): إنّ and its noun, and the clause كنا is its khabar (predicate), and the whole clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); كان and its noun; لكم is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of تبعا, or attached to تبعا itself if it is regarded as a maṣdar; فهل: the fāʾ is a conjunction and هل is an interrogative particle; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and مغنون its khabar; عنا is attached to مغنون; نصيبا is the object of مغنون, i.e. "warding off from us a portion of the Fire". The wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ: «نصيبا is accusative by a verb indicated by مغنون, its implied form being: "Will you ward off from us, or hold back…"; and it may be in the position of the maṣdar, just as شيء is likewise — do you not see the saying of Allah the Exalted: «لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا»? شيئا there is in the position of غنى (an availing), and so likewise نصيبا». من النار is a naʿt of نصيبا.
(قالَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا إِنَّا كُلٌّ فِيها إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ حَكَمَ بَيْنَ الْعِبادِ): قال الذين is a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause استكبروا is the ṣila of الذين; إنا is إنّ and its noun; كلّ is a mubtadaʾ, permitted to begin the sentence because of the sense of generality in it; فيها is the khabar of كل, and the clause is the khabar of إنّ; إنّ and its noun, and the clause قد حكم is the khabar of إنّ; بين العباد is an adverb attached to حكم.
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ فِي النَّارِ لِخَزَنَةِ جَهَنَّمَ ادْعُوا رَبَّكُمْ يُخَفِّفْ عَنَّا يَوْماً مِنَ الْعَذابِ): the wāw is a conjunction; قال الذين is a past verb and its fāʿil; في النار is attached to an omitted ṣila of الذين; لخزنة جهنم is attached to قال, and جهنم is placed in the position of the pronoun to evoke terror — more of this discussion will come in the section on rhetoric; ادعوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; ربكم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the object of the saying; يخفف is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab); عنا is attached to يخفف; يوما is an adverb also attached to يخفف; and من العذاب is a naʿt of an omitted noun which is the object of يخفف, i.e. "that He lighten for us something of the punishment on one day".
(قالُوا أَوَلَمْ تَكُ تَأْتِيكُمْ رُسُلُكُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ؟): قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil, the pronoun referring to the keepers of Jahannam; the hamza is for disapproving, rebuking interrogation; the wāw conjoins to something implied, i.e. "Did you not desist from this, and did not … come to you?"; لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to past) and jussive; تك is an imperfect verb in the jussive, the sign of its jussive being the implied sukūn on the nūn that was dropped for lightness; the noun of تك is latent (mustatir), and the clause تأتيكم is its khabar; رسلكم is the fāʿil of تأتيكم — both تك and تأتيكم contend for it (tanāzuʿ), so it was given as fāʿil to the second and a pronoun was implied in the first, and the reverse is also permissible; بالبينات is attached to تأتيكم.
(قالُوا بَلى قالُوا فَادْعُوا وَما دُعاءُ الْكافِرِينَ إِلَّا فِي ضَلالٍ): قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil; بلى is a particle of answer affirming what was negated; قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil as well; فادعوا: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and ادعوا is an imperative verb, mabnī on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the wāw is circumstantial (of ḥāl); ما is negating; دعاء is a mubtadaʾ and الكافرين a muḍāf ilayhi; إلا is a particle of restriction; and في ضلال is the khabar of دعاء.
(إِنَّا لَنَنْصُرُ رُسُلَنا وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَيَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْأَشْهادُ): this gives the reason why their supplication goes to waste, since it is stripped of any argument. إنّ and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause ننصر رسلنا is the khabar of إنا; الذين is conjoined to رسلنا, and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila; في الحياة الدنيا is attached to ننصر. This emphasis is not impaired by what appears — that they are sometimes overcome, as a trial and a test — for what counts is the outcomes, and matters are judged by their endings. ويوم يقوم الاشهاد is conjoined to في الحياة الدنيا, i.e. "We shall surely help them in the life of this world and on the Day of Resurrection"; the clause يقوم الاشهاد is in the position of the genitive because the adverb is annexed to it; and الأشهاد is the plural of شاهد (witness), like صاحب and أصحاب.
(يَوْمَ لا يَنْفَعُ الظَّالِمِينَ مَعْذِرَتُهُمْ وَلَهُمُ اللَّعْنَةُ وَلَهُمْ سُوءُ الدَّارِ): يوم is a badal (substitute) of the يوم before it; the clause لا ينفع is in the position of the genitive because the adverb is annexed to it; الظالمين is a mafʿūl bihi and معذرتهم is the fāʿil; the wāw is a conjunction; لهم is a fronted khabar and اللعنة a postponed mubtadaʾ; and لهم سوء الدار is conjoined to لهم اللعنة.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «لخزنة جهنم» there is — as we said — the placing of the overt noun in the position of the pronoun, to evoke terror. It is also possible that جهنم is the part of the Fire deepest in its pit, from their saying بئر جهنام, i.e. a well of great depth; al-Nābigha used to be called al-Jihinnām because of the depth of his poetry. The first view is more apparent, and the magnification in it comes from two aspects: first, placing the overt noun in the position of the pronoun; and second, mentioning it — while it is one and the same thing — by an overt noun other than the first and more terrible than it, for جهنم is more terrible than النار, since النار is general while جهنم is its most severe part. Moreover, the following is stated in al-Qāmūs: «A well جهنّام — with the jīm pronounced with any of the three vowels — and جهنم on the pattern of عملّس, means one of great depth; and from this Jahannam was named, may Allah the Exalted protect us from it». Its commentator said: «His saying "from this Jahannam was named" proceeds on the view that it is Arabic and is not declined (lam tujra) because of femininity and definiteness; whereas Yūnus and others held that it is a foreign word, not declined because of definiteness and foreignness». His expression "lam tujra" means "is not fully declined" (lam tanṣarif). The expression المنصرف and غير المنصرف (declinable and indeclinable / diptote) is the terminology of Sībawayh and of the Basrans, while المجري and غير المجري is the terminology of the Kufans.

dervis-irab:53-59.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْهُدى وَأَوْرَثْنا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ الْكِتابَ): a resumptive statement, brought to present a great example among the examples of the help which Allah promised His prophets and His friends in this world. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); آتينا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); موسى is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and الهدى a second mafʿūl bihi; أورثنا is conjoined to آتينا and is a verb and its fāʿil; بني إسرائيل is a first mafʿūl bihi and الكتاب a second mafʿūl bihi.
(هُدىً وَذِكْرى لِأُولِي الْأَلْبابِ): هدى and ذكرى are accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of guidance and reminder; or as two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial). لأولي الألباب is a naʿt (adjective) of ذكرى, or it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ذكرى.
(فَاصْبِرْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لِذَنْبِكَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you have come to know this established truth — that Allah helps His messengers and His friends — then be patient, O Muhammad, with the harm of your people"; إنّ, its noun and its khabar (predicate); واستغفر لذنبك is conjoined to فاصبر, i.e. "and make up for the shortcomings (al-mufraṭāt) by [seeking forgiveness for] your sin". It has been said that the expression involves the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "for the sin of your community".
(وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ بِالْعَشِيِّ وَالْإِبْكارِ): also conjoined; بحمد ربك is a ḥāl; بالعشي والإبكار is attached to سبح.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُجادِلُونَ فِي آياتِ اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ سُلْطانٍ أَتاهُمْ): إنّ and its noun, and the clause يجادلون is the khabar of إنّ; في آيات الله is attached to يجادلون; بغير سلطان is a ḥāl, i.e. while they rely in their disputing on no proof except obstinacy and contentiousness — and these are two fettered weapons; the clause أتاهم is a naʿt of سلطان.
(إِنْ فِي صُدُورِهِمْ إِلَّا كِبْرٌ ما هُمْ بِبالِغِيهِ): إن is negating; في صدورهم is a fronted khabar; إلا is a particle of restriction; كبر is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is the khabar of إنّ [Translator's note: so in the source; إنّ الذين is meant]; ما is the Ḥijāzī negating ما, and هم is its noun; ببالغيه: the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and بالغيه is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of ما; the clause is a naʿt of كبر, i.e. "they will not attain what their pride requires", which is self-aggrandisement.
(فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; استعذ is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; بالله is attached to استعذ; إنّ and its noun; هو is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; and السميع البصير is the khabar of إنّ.
(لَخَلْقُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ خَلْقِ النَّاسِ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); خلق السموات والأرض is a mubtadaʾ and أكبر its khabar; من خلق الناس is attached to أكبر; ولكن: the wāw is circumstantial (of ḥāl), and لكنّ and its noun, with the clause لا يعلمون as its khabar. The secret of how this statement coheres with what precedes it will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَما يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمى وَالْبَصِيرُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ وَلَا الْمُسِيءُ قَلِيلًا ما تَتَذَكَّرُونَ): the wāw conjoins to what preceded; ما is negating; يستوي الأعمى is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; البصير is conjoined to الأعمى; الذين آمنوا is conjoined to الأعمى and البصير, and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); عملوا الصالحات is a conjoined clause falling within the scope of the ṣila; ولا المسيء: the wāw is a conjunction, لا is redundant for emphasis, and المسيء is conjoined to what precedes it. The ordering of these conjoined items will come in the section on rhetoric. قليلا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or an adverb of time; ما is redundant; and تتذكرون is a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb with its fāʿil.
(إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ لَآتِيَةٌ لا رَيْبَ فِيها وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ): إنّ and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and آتية is its khabar; لا is the lā of generic negation, ريب its noun and فيها its khabar, and the clause is a second khabar of إنّ. ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون: the i'rab of this clause preceded a little earlier, so refresh your memory of it.

* Rhetoric:
1- The device of compelling (fann al-iljāʾ):
In His saying «لخلق السموات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس» there is a lofty device among the devices of rhetoric, namely the device of compelling (al-iljāʾ): the speaker confronts his opponent at once with what compels him to acknowledge its truth. By this its cohesion with the preceding speech is sound. For their disputing about the signs of Allah comprised many matters of argument, fallacy, contentiousness and sophistry, foremost among them the denial of the resurrection, which is in fact the root of the dispute and the axis on which it turns. So He, glory be to Him, hastened to confront them with what would leave them confounded and cut off from them the paths of obstinacy and stubbornness: namely the creation of the heavens and the earth. They acknowledged that Allah was their Creator and that they were a mighty creation; so the creation of people, by comparison, is an easy thing, and whoever is able to create them despite their vastness is without doubt more able to create weak man and more fit for it. Moreover, the a fortiori force (al-awlawiyya) in this argument is of two degrees: first, that the one able to do the mighty thing is more able to do the lowly thing; and second, that their dispute was about the resurrection, which is re-creation, and there is no doubt that the initial creation is mightier and more dazzling than re-creation.
2- The device of good arrangement (fann ḥusn al-nasaq):
In His saying «وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير» (the verse) there is the device of good arrangement. In ordering the arrangement there are three methods. The first is that a thing is placed next to what corresponds to it, as in this verse: the blind is placed next to the seeing — these two descriptions are borrowed for one who is heedless of knowing the truth about his origin and his return — and the blind is put first in negating equality because it comes after the description of blame in His saying «ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون»; and «الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات», i.e. the doer of good, is placed next to the evil-doer, and الذين آمنوا is put first because of its adjacency to البصير — and that adjacency is honour enough for the believer. The second of the two methods [Translator's note: so in the source, «وثاني الطريقتين», although three methods are listed] is that the two contrasting items are both postponed, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «مثل الفريقين كالأعمى والأصم والبصير والسميع». The third of them is that the counterpart of the first is put first and the counterpart of the last is put last, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير ولا الظلمات ولا النور». The speaker chooses among these three methods in presenting them according to what the situation requires and in accordance with the laws and ways of rhetoric; and Allah knows best.

* Benefits:
The lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ):
It conveys two things. The first is emphasising the content of the sentence; for this reason, in the chapter of inna they shifted it away from the head of the sentence, disliking to begin speech with two emphasisers. The second is restricting the imperfect to the present. By agreement it enters in two places:
1- On the mubtadaʾ, e.g.: «لأنتم أشد رهبة في صدورهم من الله ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون».
2- After إنّ. In this chapter it enters by agreement on three things: the noun, e.g. «إن ربي لسميع الدعاء»; the imperfect verb, because of its resemblance to the noun, e.g. «وإن ربك ليحكم بينهم»; and the adverbial phrase, e.g. «وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم». And it enters on three with disagreement: the non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb, e.g. (إن زيدا لعسى أن يقوم); the past verb accompanied by قد; and the inflecting past verb free of قد.
Among the [kinds of] lām of inception is the lām of the oath, e.g. «لينبذن في الحطمة» and «ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى».

dervis-irab:60-63.t:
* Vocabulary:
(داخِرِينَ): humbled, abased. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «دخر الشخص يدخر, with two fatḥas, دخورا: he was abased and humiliated; and أدخرته, with the alif, for transitivity».

* I'rab:
(وَقالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ): a resumptive statement brought to show the merit of supplication, i.e. worship; the figurative usage (majāz) in this word will come in the section on rhetoric. قال ربكم is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ادعوني is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). أستجب is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), and لكم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أستجب.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبادَتِي سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ داخِرِينَ): إنّ and its noun; the clause يستكبرون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين; عن عبادتي is attached to يستكبرون; the clause سيدخلون is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; جهنم is a mafʿūl bihi by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa); and داخرين is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(اللَّهُ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ وَالنَّهارَ مُبْصِراً): الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and الذي its khabar; the clause جعل is the ṣila; لكم is attached to جعل, because it means "created"; الليل is a mafʿūl bihi; لتسكنوا: the lām is causal, and تسكنوا is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and the wāw is the fāʿil; فيه is attached to تسكنوا; النهار is conjoined to الليل; and مبصرا is a ḥāl.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَشْكُرُونَ): إنّ and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ذو فضل is the khabar of إنّ; على الناس is attached to فضل; ولكن: the wāw is a conjunction, and لكنّ and its noun, with the clause لا يشكرون as the khabar of لكنّ.
(ذلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ خالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the One who is known and distinguished by the acts that require His lordship; الله is a first khabar, ربكم a second khabar and خالق كل شيء a third khabar.
(لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَأَنَّى تُؤْفَكُونَ): the i'rab of the word of testimony (kalimat al-shahāda) has preceded in detail, so refresh your memory of it; the clause is a fourth khabar. The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; أنى is an interrogative noun meaning "how", in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; تؤفكون, i.e. "you are turned away", is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), i.e. "How then are you turned away from faith after the proofs of His lordship have been established?"
(كَذلِكَ يُؤْفَكُ الَّذِينَ كانُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ): the kāf is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "like the turning-away of these is the turning-away of those who used to deny the signs of Allah"; الذين is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause كانوا is the ṣila of the relative noun; كان and its noun; بآيات الله is attached to يجحدون; and the clause يجحدون is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- Figurative usage (al-majāz) and verbal correspondence (al-mushākala):
In His saying «وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم» there is a majāz mursal (metonymic figure) whose relation is causality, because supplication is a cause of worship; and in His saying «أستجب لكم» there is mushākala (verbal correspondence), because the rewarding follows upon it. We have only taken the expression as figurative because of the contextual indication in His saying after that «إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي». This figurative reading is supported by the ḥadīth of al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: «Supplication is worship», and he recited this verse; and by the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās: "The best worship is supplication". Nevertheless, some took the verse in its apparent sense and said that supplication is asking and humble entreaty. More discussion on this point will come in the section on benefits.
2- Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī):
In His saying «الله الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا» there is a figurative attribution: seeing is attributed to the day because one sees in it, whereas seeing in reality belongs to the people of the day. The night is coupled with the object of purpose and the day with the ḥāl, because each of them conveys what the other conveys; for if it had been said «لتبصروا فيه», the eloquence latent in the figurative attribution would have been lost; and if it had been said «ساكنا» — while the night may be described as still in a literal sense — the literal would not have been distinguished from the figurative.
3- Placing the overt noun in the position of the pronoun:
In His saying «ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون» there is the placing [Translator's note: the source has «وسع», evidently a misprint for «وضع»] of the overt noun in the position of the pronoun. The context required Him to say «ولكن أكثرهم لا يشكرون», so that the mention of الناس would not be repeated; but in this repetition there is a singling out of them for ingratitude for blessings, and that they are the ones distinguished by this trait, which is ingrained in [human] natures: blessings follow upon them in succession and favours come one after another, and everything of life's comforts that they long for is made ready for them, yet they persist in denial and disavowal. Is this not the mark of people in various circumstances and conditions? He, glory be to Him, has repeatedly affirmed this, saying: «إن الإنسان لربه لكنود» and saying «إن الإنسان لظلوم كفار».

* Benefits:
1- Imam Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī said in his Risāla: «People have differed as to which is better: supplication, or silence and contentment? Some of them said: supplication is worship, because of the ḥadīth "Supplication is indeed worship", and because supplication is a display of one's need of Allah the Exalted. A group said: silence and stillness under the course of [divine] decree is more complete, and contentment with what destiny has already decreed is more fitting. And some people said: one should be a person of supplication with his tongue and of contentment with his heart, so as to combine both matters». Al-Qushayrī said: «It is more fitting to say that times differ: in some states supplication is better than silence, and that is the proper conduct (adab); and in some states silence is better than supplication, and that is the proper conduct. This is only known by the moment: if he finds in his heart an indication towards supplication, then supplication is more fitting for him; and if he finds an indication towards silence, then silence is more complete».
If it is said: how did Allah the Exalted say «ادعوني أستجب لكم», when a person may supplicate a great deal and not be answered? It has been said in reply: «Supplication has conditions, among them: sincerity in supplication; that one not supplicate while his heart is distracted and occupied with something other than the supplication; that what is sought by the supplication be in the person's interest; and that it involve no severing of family ties. If the supplication meets these conditions, it is worthy of being answered: either He hastens it for him or He defers it for him. This is indicated by what is narrated from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no man who supplicates Allah the Exalted with a supplication but he is answered: either it is hastened for him in this world, or it is deferred for him in the Hereafter, or some of his sins are expiated for him to the extent of what he supplicated — so long as he does not supplicate for a sin or for the severing of family ties, or become impatient." They said: O Messenger of Allah, and how does he become impatient? He said: "He says: I supplicated, but He did not answer me."»
Al-Ghazālī brought up another question. He said: «If it is said: what is the benefit of supplication when the decree cannot be turned back? Then know that part of the decree is the repelling of affliction by supplication. Supplication is a cause for repelling affliction and for the bringing of mercy, just as the shield is a cause for warding off weapons and water is a cause for plants coming out of the earth. Just as the shield repels the arrow and the two push against each other, so too do supplication and affliction. It is not a condition of acknowledging the decree that one not bear arms; Allah the Exalted has said: "وليأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم". So Allah the Exalted decreed the matter and decreed its cause».
This is a question whose answer may come before it. We have narrated in the book of al-Tirmidhī, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Whoever would be pleased that Allah the Exalted answer him in hardships, let him supplicate much in times of ease». The meaning of سره is: it delighted him and made him glad and happy. «أن يستجيب الله» is the fāʿil of سره, and the object of يستجيب is omitted, i.e. his supplication. His saying «عند الشدائد» is an adverb for the answering, i.e. the occurrence of severe matters among disliked things; and الكرب, with ḍamma then fatḥa, is the plural of كربة, which is the grief that seizes the soul [Translator's note: the word الكرب does not occur in the ḥadīth as quoted here; the commentary appears to follow a version with «عند الشدائد والكرب»]. His saying «فليكثر الدعاء…» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). And الرخاء [Translator's note: the source has «ولرخاء»], with fatḥa on the rāʾ, is ease of living and good circumstance. It is so only because supplicating much in times of ease indicates the servant's sincerity in his servanthood and his resorting to his Lord in all his states, and that he thanks Him in ease as he thanks Him in hardship, and turns to Him with his whole being, so that it may be a provision for him.
Imam Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī said in al-Iḥyāʾ: «The etiquettes of supplication are ten:
The first: that one watch for the noble times, such as the Day of ʿArafa, the month of Ramaḍān, Friday, the last third of the night and the time before dawn. The second: that one seize the noble states, such as the state of prostration, the meeting of armies, the coming down of rain, and at the establishing of the prayer and after it. The third: facing the qibla and raising the hands, and wiping the face with them at the end. The fourth: lowering the voice between a whisper and loudness. The fifth: that one not strain after rhymed prose (sajʿ). The sixth: humble entreaty, submissiveness and awe. The seventh: that one be resolute in asking and certain of the answer. The eighth: that one be insistent in supplication, repeat it three times, and not consider the answer slow. The ninth: that one open the supplication with the remembrance of Allah the Exalted. The tenth is the root of the answer: it is repentance, restoring what was wrongfully taken, and turning to Allah the Exalted».
2- A glimpse of al-Qushayrī:
In this section we have taken a spark from al-Risāla al-Qushayriyya. To complete the benefit, it is good for us to present a brief glimpse of it and of its author, for it furnishes us with a complete picture of Sufism and its men from the emergence of Sufism in the second half of the second century AH down to the author's age; and, despite its relatively small size, it is regarded as the best scholarly and historical document on its subject. Before summarising the Risāla, its author must be mentioned. He is the Shaykh ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn Hawāzin, known as Zayn al-Islām Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī, born in 376 AH. He was born in a purely Arab household: his father was a Qushayrī from the tribe of Qushayr ibn Kaʿb, which entered Khurāsān in the time of the Umayyads; his mother was of Sulaym, and his maternal uncle Abū ʿAqīl al-Sulamī was one of the notable landowners (dahāqīn) of the district of Ustuwā near Nīsābūr; in this region his nearer ancestors lived. We know only a little about his early childhood, but we know that his father died when he was young, and the matter of his upbringing was entrusted to Abū al-Qāsim al-Yamānī, who was a friend of the Qushayrī family; he studied literature and Arabic with him. Then he moved to Nīsābūr, where he took knowledge from some of the eminent scholars there, and attended the circle of the famous master Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Daqqāq, who was one of the great Sufi shaykhs of his time. Al-Qushayrī admired him, found his words excellent and followed his path; the shaykh accepted him and advised him to learn [religious] knowledge. So he attended the lessons of Shaykh Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Bakr al-Ṭūsī, then of the master Abū Bakr ibn Nūrak, who died in 406 AH and was a great scholar of uṣūl. After his death he frequented the master Abū Isḥāq al-Isfarāyīnī and combined his method with that of Ibn Nūrak. After that he studied the books of al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr al-Bāqillānī, who died in 403 AH. Throughout all this he kept attending the circle of Abū ʿAlī al-Daqqāq, until the latter chose him for his companionship and married him to his daughter. When the master Abū ʿAlī died, he accompanied Shaykh Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, the great Sufi historian, and became the undisputed shaykh of Khurāsān in jurisprudence according to the school of Imam al-Shāfiʿī and in theology (kalām) according to the school of Imam Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī; he also held the foremost place in ḥadīth, literature and language. Al-Bākharzī, who died in 467, described his ability at moving exhortation by saying: «Were the rock struck with the whips of his warning it would melt, and were Iblīs tied up in the gathering of his admonition he would repent; and he possesses decisive speech (faṣl al-khiṭāb) in the excellence of pleasing discourse».
It seems that the wide fame al-Qushayrī enjoyed in Nīsābūr stirred rancour and envy in the souls of the jurists of that city, and they began to make preparations to lower his standing by fabricating accusations and spreading lies about him. They succeeded in their endeavour, and a severe ordeal befell al-Qushayrī, in which he met various kinds of hardship, pain and displacement. We refer the reader to the Ṭabaqāt of al-Subkī to read the details of that ordeal, which lasted five years, until ʿAḍud al-Dawla restored his honour to him and his circle came together again as it had been.
Summary of al-Risāla al-Qushayriyya:
The Risāla consists of the following main sections:
1- An introduction in which he explains the motive for composing the Risāla. He had noticed that some Sufis of his time had strayed from the paths of right guidance, so he resolved to compose a book in which he would return Sufism to its first way of life and free it from the innovations that had crept into it. Here are his words, which we quote verbatim because of the splendour with which they depict this tragedy. He says: «Know — may Allah have mercy on you — that most of the true realisers (al-muḥaqqiqūn) of this group have passed away, and nothing remains of this group in this time of ours except their traces, as it was said:
أما الخيام فإنها كخيامهم ... وأرى نساء الحي غير نسائها
(As for the tents, they are like their tents, but I see the women of the encampment are not its [former] women.)
In this introduction al-Qushayrī also gives an exposition of the fundamentals of the articles of faith which the early Sufis professed and on which they built the foundations of their affair on the Path; then he summarises his point of view in nine questions, to which whoever wishes may refer in his Risāla.
2- A section in which he gives biographies of a group of Sufis, beginning with Ibrāhīm ibn Adham and ending with Aḥmad ibn ʿAṭāʾ.
3- An explanation of terms current among the Sufis, and a clarification of what is obscure in them.
4- On the etiquette of the Path and the obstacles that confront the wayfarer on his journey to Allah.
5- A conclusion containing his counsel to the disciples (murīdīn).
Moreover, the Risāla has been the object of scholars' attention, and several commentaries have been written on it, the most famous being the commentary of Shaykh Zakariyyā al-Anṣārī.

dervis-irab:64-68.t:
* I'rab:
(اللَّهُ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ قَراراً وَالسَّماءَ بِناءً وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ): a resumptive statement brought to show His favour, exalted is He, relating to place, after showing His favour relating to time. الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and الذي its khabar (predicate); the clause جعل is the ṣila (relative clause); لكم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); الأرض is a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and قرارا a second mafʿūl bihi, because جعل here means "to make into"; if you regard it as meaning "to create", then قرارا is a ḥāl meaning "settled". السماء بناء is conjoined to what precedes. صوركم is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi; فأحسن is conjoined to صوركم, and صوركم is a mafʿūl bihi. The meaning of the sky being a بناء is that it is built like a dome pitched [over us] to the eye's view.
(وَرَزَقَكُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّباتِ ذلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ): رزقكم is conjoined to what precedes; من الطيبات is attached to رزقكم; ذلكم is a mubtadaʾ, الله a khabar and ربكم a second khabar.
(فَتَبارَكَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعالَمِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; تبارك is a past verb, الله its fāʿil, and رب العالمين a naʿt (adjective) of الله.
(هُوَ الْحَيُّ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَادْعُوهُ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ): هو is a mubtadaʾ and الحي a khabar; the word of testimony, whose i'rab has preceded, is a second khabar. فادعوه: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and ادعوه is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; مخلصين is a ḥāl; له is attached to مخلصين; and الدين is the object of مخلصين.
(الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ): its i'rab preceded at the opening of the book. The clause is the object of an omitted saying, which is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of فادعوه, i.e. "saying: الحمد لله…". The clause may also be resumptive, as being from the speech of Him Himself, glory be to Him.
(قُلْ إِنِّي نُهِيتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ لَمَّا جاءَنِي الْبَيِّناتُ مِنْ رَبِّي): إنّ, its noun and its khabar are the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the clause نهيت is the khabar of إنّ, and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); أن أعبد: the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "from worshipping those whom you call upon"; the clause تدعون is the ṣila; من دون الله is a ḥāl; لما is an adverb meaning "when", or a linking particle (rābiṭa); جاءني البينات is a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi and a postponed fāʿil; and the clause جاءني is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) because the adverb is annexed to it.
(وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ): conjoined to نهيت; أن and what falls within its scope are accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "to submit"; لرب العالمين is attached to أسلم.
(هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ تُرابٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ): هو is a mubtadaʾ and الذي a khabar; the clause خلقكم is the ṣila; من تراب is attached to خلقكم. The statement is resumptive, brought to show how the body comes into being, and what follows is conjoined to it.
(ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلًا): also conjoined; يخرجكم is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; and طفلا is a ḥāl of the kāf in يخرجكم.
(ثُمَّ لِتَبْلُغُوا أَشُدَّكُمْ ثُمَّ لِتَكُونُوا شُيُوخاً): also conjoined; the lām is causal, and تبلغوا is accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "then He keeps you alive"; likewise لتكونوا شيوخا, and شيوخا is the khabar of كان. It has been read with ḍamma and with kasra on the shīn.
(وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُتَوَفَّى مِنْ قَبْلُ): the clause is resumptive; منكم is attached to an omitted khabar of «من»; and من قبل is attached to يتوفى.
(وَلِتَبْلُغُوا أَجَلًا مُسَمًّى وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; لتبلغوا: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted as well, its implied form being "and We do that and the like"; أجلا is a mafʿūl bihi and مسمى a naʿt; and لعلكم تعقلون is conjoined to His saying لتبلغوا أشدكم.
(هُوَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ فَإِذا قَضى أَمْراً فَإِنَّما يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ): هو is a mubtadaʾ and الذي its khabar; the clause يحيي ويميت is the ṣila. فإذا: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; the clause قضى is in the position of the genitive because the adverb is annexed to it; أمرا is a mafʿūl bihi. فإنما: the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa), and إنما is a restraining particle with what it restrains (kāffa wa-makfūfa); يقول is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "He"; له is attached to يقول; كن is a complete (tāmm) imperative verb with a latent fāʿil, its implied form being "you"; the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause يكون is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "so it is". It has been read فيكونَ with fatḥa, on the view that the fāʾ is causal (sababiyya), the fāʿil being a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it".

* Benefits:
كائنا ما كان ("whatever it may be"):
There is disagreement about كان and كائنا in your saying لأضربنه كائنا ما كان ("I shall surely strike him, whoever he may be"). Al-Fārisī said: both are complete (tāmm) in the two places, and ما is maṣdariyya; it together with what follows it is the fāʿil of كائنا, i.e. "its being". It has been said that both are incomplete (nāqiṣ) in the two places: in كائنا there is a pronoun which is its noun, and its khabar is ما, which is a relative, and its ṣila is كان with its noun and its khabar; its noun is a pronoun latent in it, and its khabar is omitted, its implied form being إياه. The noun of كائن latent in it and the khabar of كان both refer back to the person struck. The implied form of the expression is then: لأضربنه كائنا الذي كان إياه, and كائنا is a ḥāl of the object of لأضربنه. This involves applying ما to a rational being, which is permissible. ما may also be an indefinite noun qualified by a description. One may also say «من كان», and then the expression runs on its proper course.

dervis-irab:69-76.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السَّلاسِلُ): plural of سلسلة (chain), which is a ring of iron or the like whose parts or links are joined to one another. From it come سلاسل البرق, i.e. the elongated streaks of lightning across the breadth of the cloud, and سلاسل الكتاب: its lines. Al-Rāghib said: تسلسل الشيء means the thing quivered, as if a repeated chaining was imagined in it, so the repetition in its wording draws attention to the repetition in its meaning; and ماء سلسل is water that moves to and fro in its resting place.
(يُسْجَرُونَ): they are kindled, from سجر التنور, when he fills the oven with fuel.

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يُجادِلُونَ فِي آياتِ اللَّهِ أَنَّى يُصْرَفُونَ): the hamza is for interrogation of affirmation (taqrīr) and wonder; لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to past) and jussive; تر is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by إلى [Translator's note: so in the source; it is jussive by لم], and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; إلى الذين is attached to (mutaʿalliq) تر, i.e. "look"; the clause يجادلون بآيات الله is the ṣila (relative clause); أنى is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); يصرفون is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); what it is attached to is omitted, i.e. "they are turned away from faith altogether".
(الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِالْكِتابِ وَبِما أَرْسَلْنا بِهِ رُسُلَنا فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ): الذين is a badal (substitute) of the first الذين; كذبوا is the ṣila; بالكتاب is attached to كذبوا; بما is conjoined to بالكتاب; the clause أرسلنا is the ṣila; به is attached to أرسلنا; رسلنا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ is resumptive; سوف is a particle of the future; يعلمون is a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the clause is resumptive, brought for threat. Moreover, الذين may be parsed as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), so that its position is nominative; or as accusative by way of blame; or it may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is فسوف يعلمون, the fāʾ being linking (rābiṭa) because of the scent of condition in the relative noun.
(إِذِ الْأَغْلالُ فِي أَعْناقِهِمْ وَالسَّلاسِلُ يُسْحَبُونَ): إذ is an adverb of past time attached to يعلمون, or it is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi of يعلمون. There is no contradiction in the adverb being past while «سوف يعلمون» is future, for in making it a mafʿūl bihi one avoids the impossibility of a future [verb] governing past time. You may also say there is no contradiction because future matters, since they are certain and definite in the reports of Allah the Exalted, are expressed by the wording of what has happened and come to be, while the meaning is future.
The wording of al-Samīn: «There is no need to take إذ out of its proper meaning; rather it remains indicating the past, and it is accusative by His saying فسوف يعلمون as a mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "they will know on the Day of Resurrection the time of the fetters being on their necks", i.e. the time of the cause of the fetters, which is the sins they used to commit in this world — as if it were said: "they will come to know the time of their sins which put the fetters on their necks". This is a sound view; the most it involves is dealing freely with إذ by making it a mafʿūl bihi, and that does us no harm, for the parsers most of the time say "accusative by an implied اذكر", and it is then nothing but a mafʿūl bihi, because of the impossibility of a future [verb] governing past time. They also allowed it to be accusative by an implied اذكر, i.e. "mention to them the time of the fetters, so that they may fear and be deterred". So these are three views, the best of which is the middle one».
The wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ: إذ is an adverb of past time, and what is meant by it here is the future, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: فسوف يعلمون. الأغلال is a mubtadaʾ and في أعناقهم a khabar; السلاسل is conjoined to الأغلال, and the adverbial phrase is intended to come after both of them, so it is a khabar for both together; the clause يسحبون is a ḥāl. Or [السلاسل] is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause يسحبون, the binding element being implied, its implied form being بها. It has been read with السلاسلَ in the accusative and يَسحبون with fatḥa on the yāʾ, so it is a fronted object of يسحبون.
The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «From Ibn ʿAbbās: والسلاسلَ يَسحبون, in the accusative and with fatḥa on the yāʾ, conjoining the verbal clause to the nominal one; and from him also: والسلاسلِ يُسحبون, with السلاسل in the genitive. Its justification is that if it had been said إذ أعناقهم في الأغلال in place of His saying إذ الأغلال في أعناقهم, it would have been correct and sound; so since they are two expressions that succeed one another, His saying والسلاسل was construed on the other expression. Its parallel is:
مشائيم ليسوا مصلحين عشيرة ... ولا ناعب إلا ببين غرابها
(Ill-omened men, they do not set a tribe aright, nor does their crow croak except at a parting.)
as if it had been said بمصلحين. And it has been read وبالسلاسل يسحبون». So on the reading in the genitive it belongs to the category of conjunction by supposition (ʿaṭf al-tawahhum), whose discussion has preceded. In that case it contains the device of inversion (fann al-qalb), which is frequent and widespread in their speech and whose discussion has preceded, and after that it contains conjunction by supposition.
[Translator's note: the source prints the verse's hemistich as «ولا ناعب إلا بين غرابها»; the well-known form is «إلا ببين», which is translated here.]
(فِي الْحَمِيمِ ثُمَّ فِي النَّارِ يُسْجَرُونَ): في الحميم is attached to يسحبون; ثم is a conjunction for delay; في النار is attached to يسجرون; and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.
(ثُمَّ قِيلَ لَهُمْ أَيْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تُشْرِكُونَ): ثم قيل, i.e. "then it will be said", or "they will say"; the past form is because the occurrence of the saying is certain; لهم is attached to قيل; أين is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, and the adverb is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ما is a relative noun, a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause كنتم is the ṣila; and the clause تشركون is the khabar of كنتم.
(مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ قالُوا ضَلُّوا عَنَّا): من دون الله is a ḥāl; قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil; and the clause ضلوا عنا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(بَلْ لَمْ نَكُنْ نَدْعُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ شَيْئاً كَذلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ الْكافِرِينَ): بل is a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī); لم is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; نكن is an incomplete imperfect verb, jussive by لم, its noun latent, its implied form being "we", and the clause ندعو is its khabar; من قبل is a ḥāl; شيئا is a mafʿūl bihi; كذلك is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); and يضل الله الكافرين is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi.
(ذلِكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَفْرَحُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the leading astray or to the punishment; بما is a khabar; the clause كنتم is the ṣila; the clause تفرحون is the khabar of كنتم; في الأرض is attached to تفرحون; and بغير الحق is a ḥāl.
(وَبِما كُنْتُمْ تَمْرَحُونَ): conjoined to His saying كنتم تفرحون. المرح is joy, or the most intense of it, as in al-Miṣbāḥ.
(ادْخُلُوا أَبْوابَ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدِينَ فِيها فَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ): ادخلوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the object of an omitted saying; أبواب جهنم is a mafʿūl bihi by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa); خالدين is a ḥāl; فيها is attached to خالدين; the fāʾ is a conjunction; بئس is a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; مثوى المتكبرين is the fāʿil of بئس; and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "it". He did not say مدخل المتكبرين ("the entrance of the arrogant"), in order to convey permanence and eternity by the word الثواء (abiding).

* Benefits:
«أين» is written separately from «ما» in the Muṣḥaf [here], while it is joined in other places. The wording of Ibn al-Jazarī: («فأينما كالنحل صل», i.e. join «أين» with «ما» in the saying of Allah the Exalted «أينما تولوا فثم وجه الله» in al-Baqara, like al-Naḥl, i.e. as you join it with it in His saying «أينما يوجهه لا يأت بخير» in al-Naḥl; «ومختلف في الأحزاب والنساء وصف», i.e. the disagreement about «أين ما كنتم تعبدون» in al-Shuʿarāʾ, «أينما ثقفوا» in al-Aḥzāb and «أينما تكونوا يدرككم الموت» in al-Nisāʾ has been described, i.e. mentioned — the scholars of orthography have mentioned it; and apart from these three, e.g. «فاستبقوا الخيرات أين ما تكونوا», «أين ما كنتم تدعون من دون الله» in al-Aʿrāf, «أين ما كنتم تشركون» in Ghāfir and «أين ما كانوا» in al-Mujādila, it is written separately).

dervis-irab:77-78.t:
* I'rab:
(فَاصْبِرْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if there appears to you from them whatever obstruction and turning away appears, then do not grieve, and be patient, for We shall take vengeance on them for you".
اصبر is an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; إنّ, its noun and its khabar (predicate) give the reason for the command to be patient.
(فَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِلَيْنا يُرْجَعُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; the conditional إن is assimilated into the redundant (zāʾida) ما; نرينك is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, in the position of the jussive (majzūm); its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "We"; the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and بعض الذي a second mafʿūl bihi; the clause نعدهم is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي; أو نتوفينك is conjoined to نرينك; the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa); فإلينا يرجعون: إلينا is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يرجعون, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the second condition, which is نتوفينك; and the apodosis of the first condition [Translator's note: the word "is omitted" is evidently missing in the source] — the implied form being: "Either We show you part of what We promise them of punishment, namely killing and captivity on the day of Badr — then that is that; or We take you in death before the day of Badr — then to Us they will be returned on the Day of Resurrection, and We shall take the severest vengeance on them".
The apodosis of the first was omitted, rather than that of the second, only because if the first happens, that is the utmost hope in afflicting them; so what holds on the supposition of its occurrence is known, namely the complete attainment of what is desired. But if it does not happen and the second happens — namely his being taken in death before the requital comes upon them — then this is what needs to be mentioned, for consolation and reassurance of the soul that, even if their requital is delayed beyond this world, it is inevitable in the Hereafter and must come.
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا رُسُلًا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَصَصْنا عَلَيْكَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ لَمْ نَقْصُصْ عَلَيْكَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); أرسلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; رسلا is a mafʿūl bihi; من قبلك is a naʿt (adjective) of رسلك [Translator's note: so in the source; رسلا is meant], or it is attached to أرسلنا; منهم is a fronted khabar and من a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause قصصنا is the ṣila; عليك is attached to قصصنا; and منهم من لم نقصص عليك is conjoined to the first clause, which is a naʿt of رسلا or resumptive.
(وَما كانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِآيَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negating; كان is an incomplete past verb; لرسول is the fronted khabar of كان; أن and what falls within its scope are its postponed noun; بآية is attached to يأتي; إلا is a particle of restriction; and بإذن الله is an exception from the most general of states.
(فَإِذا جاءَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ قُضِيَ بِالْحَقِّ وَخَسِرَ هُنالِكَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; the clause جاء أمر الله is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) because the adverb is annexed to it; the clause قضي بالحق has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of قضي is latent, its implied form being "it", i.e. the matter; بالحق is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "bound up with the truth"; خسر is a past verb; هنالك is a demonstrative in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to خسر; and المبطلون is the fāʿil of خسر.

* Benefits:
Is the pronoun of an indefinite noun indefinite or definite?
Someone asked about the pronoun in His saying «منهم من قصصنا», which refers back to His saying «رسلا»: is it indefinite or definite? He answered that it is indefinite, because its referent is like the referent of what it refers back to, which is indefinite; so what refers back must also be indefinite, since indefiniteness and definiteness are by consideration of meaning. The correct view is that it is definite, because the hāʾ in your saying «جاءني رجل وضربته» ("a man came to me and I struck him") is not general in the way رجل is general, for it indicates specifically the man who came, not "a man". What confirms this is that you say «جاءني رجل» and then say «أكرمني الرجل», meaning by الرجل nothing but the one who came; and there is no disagreement that الرجل is definite. So the pronoun must also be definite, because it has its meaning.

dervis-irab:79-85.t:
* I'rab:
(اللَّهُ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَنْعامَ لِتَرْكَبُوا مِنْها وَمِنْها تَأْكُلُونَ): a resumptive statement brought to enumerate some of His favours, glory be to Him. الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and الذي its khabar (predicate); the clause جعل is the ṣila (relative clause); لكم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) جعل, because it means "created"; الأنعام is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) — its explanation has preceded in Sūrat al-Anʿām, and there is no sense in restricting it to camels alone. لتركبوا: the lām is causal, and تركبوا is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جعل, because it is the reason for the creating. منها is attached to تركبوا, i.e. "some of them", so من is partitive, and there is no sense in making it of beginning (ibtidāʾiyya). ومنها تأكلون is conjoined to what precedes.
(وَلَكُمْ فِيها مَنافِعُ وَلِتَبْلُغُوا عَلَيْها حاجَةً فِي صُدُورِكُمْ): the clause is conjoined.
(وَعَلَيْها وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ): عليها is attached to تحملون, and على الفلك is conjoined to عليها.
(وَيُرِيكُمْ آياتِهِ فَأَيَّ آياتِ اللَّهِ تُنْكِرُونَ): [Translator's note: the opening of this heading is damaged in the source and has been restored from the verse.] ويريكم آياته is conjoined to جعل لكم الأنعام, and آياته is a second mafʿūl bihi. فأي: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and أي is a fronted object of تنكرون, put first necessarily because interrogative nouns have the right to head the sentence (al-ṣadāra); تنكرون is a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb; and the interrogation is for rebuke. Al-Zamakhsharī said:
«It has come according to the widespread usage; your saying فأية آيات الله is rare, because distinguishing masculine and feminine in nouns that are not adjectives, like حمار and حمارة, is unusual, and in أي it is more unusual». I say: its feminine form has occurred frequently, and among it is the saying of al-Kumayt:
بأي كتاب أم بأية سنة ... ترى حبهم عارا علي وتحسب
(By what book, or by what sunna, do you see and reckon love of them a disgrace upon me?)
(أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): a resumptive statement brought to begin rebuking them. The hamza is for disapproving, rebuking interrogation; the fāʾ conjoins to something implied, i.e. "Were they unable, so that they did not travel in the land?", i.e. in its regions and its extremities. The fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (sababiyya), and ينظروا is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ of causation, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as the fronted khabar of كان, and عاقبة is its postponed noun; من قبلهم is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun.
(كانُوا أَكْثَرَ مِنْهُمْ وَأَشَدَّ قُوَّةً وَآثاراً فِي الْأَرْضِ): a resumptive statement brought to show the beginning of their conditions and their outcomes. كان and its noun, and أكثر is its khabar; منهم is attached to أكثر; قوة is a tamyīz (specification); آثارا is conjoined to قوة; and في الأرض is a naʿt (adjective) of آثارا.
