(فَما أَغْنى عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; ما is negating, or interrogative in the position of the accusative as the fronted object of أغنى; أغنى is a past verb; عنهم is attached to أغنى; the second ما is relative or maṣdariyya, and its position is nominative as the fāʿil, i.e. "what they earned / their earning did not avail them", or "what did what they earned / their earning avail them?"
(فَلَمَّا جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ فَرِحُوا بِما عِنْدَهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ): this fāʾ is the second of four successive fāʾs. The first is for conjunction, as we said, and showed the outcome of their great numbers and the intensity of their strength. The second is also conjunctive, pointing to the detailing of what was left vague about the not availing. لما is an adverb meaning "when", or a linking particle (rābiṭa); جاءتهم رسلهم is a past verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi and a fāʿil; بالبينات is attached to جاءتهم; the clause فرحوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; عندهم is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; and من العلم is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَحاقَ بِهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ): حاق is conjoined to فرحوا; بهم is attached to حاق; ما is a relative noun, the fāʿil; the clause كانوا is the ṣila; كان and its noun; به is attached to يستهزئون; and the clause يستهزئون is the khabar of كانوا. The meaning of this statement will come in the section on rhetoric.
(فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنا قالُوا آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ): this is the third fāʾ, and it is for mere conjunction and succession, i.e. the one that makes what follows it subordinate to what precedes it, occurring right after it. لما is temporal (ḥīniyya); رأوا is a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) because the adverb is annexed to it; بأسنا is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the clause آمنا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); بالله is attached to آمنا; and وحده is a ḥāl.
(وَكَفَرْنا بِما كُنَّا بِهِ مُشْرِكِينَ): كفرنا is conjoined to آمنا; بما is attached to كفرنا; the clause كنا is the ṣila of ما; كان and its noun; به is attached to مشركين; and مشركين is the khabar of كنا.
(فَلَمْ يَكُ يَنْفَعُهُمْ إِيمانُهُمْ لَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنا): this is the fourth fāʾ, and it is for conjunction; the clause يك is conjoined to آمنّا, as if it were said "so they believed, but their faith did not benefit them"; it has conveyed conjunction together with explanation. يك is an incomplete imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the implied sukūn on the nūn that was dropped for lightness; its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it", i.e. the matter (al-shaʾn); the clause ينفعهم is its khabar; and إيمانهم is the fāʿil of ينفعهم. It is also permissible to make إيمانهم nominative as the noun of كان, the clause ينفعهم being its fronted khabar; the case does not belong to the chapter of contention (al-tanāzuʿ). لما is temporal, and the clause رأوا بأسنا is in the position of the genitive because the adverb is annexed to it.
(سُنَّتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ فِي عِبادِهِ وَخَسِرَ هُنالِكَ الْكافِرُونَ): سنة الله is a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising an implied verb from its own root, i.e. "the Exalted One established with them the practice of those before them"; it may also be accusative by way of warning (taḥdhīr), i.e. "beware of Allah's practice regarding those who deny". التي is a naʿt of سنة; the clause قد خلت is the ṣila; في عباده is attached to خلت, i.e. "it has passed among His servants". The wāw is resumptive; خسر is a past verb; هنالك is a demonstrative in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to خسر; and الكافرون is the fāʿil of خسر. The adverb of place has been borrowed for time, i.e. "they lost at the time of seeing the despair (al-yaʾs)" [Translator's note: so in the source, «اليأس»; evidently «البأس», "the might", is meant]; it may also be kept to its original sense.

* Rhetoric:
The device of mockery (fann al-tahakkum):
In His saying «فلما جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فرحوا بما عندهم من العلم» (the verse) there is the device of mockery. Originally تهكّم is the collapse of a building — one says تهكمت البئر when the well collapsed — and also intense anger and regret over a matter that has passed. In the terminology of the rhetoricians it is ridicule and derision of the arrogant, by addressing them with the expression of honour in the place of contempt, good tidings in the place of warning, promise in the place of threat, and knowledge in the place of ignorance, out of the speaker's disdain for the one addressed and ridicule of him. Reference to this device has been made frequently in our book. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «He meant the "knowledge" that occurs by way of mockery in the saying of Allah the Exalted: بل ادّارك علمهم في الآخرة. Their knowledge regarding the Hereafter was that they used to say: "We shall not be resurrected and we shall not be punished", "وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رجعت إلى ربي إن لي عنده للحسنى", "وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رددت إلى ربي لأجدن خيرا منها منقلبا". They used to rejoice in that and repel with it the clear proofs and the knowledge of the prophets, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون». How beautiful is the saying of the poet of the Ḥamāsa:
أتاني من أبي أنس وعيد ... فثل تغيظ الضحاك جسمي
(A threat reached me from Abū Anas, and the rage of al-Ḍaḥḥāk wasted my body.)
ثلّ means "destroyed"; التغيظ means rage; and Abū Anas is alluded to as al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who was a king, by way of ridicule.

* Benefits:
Dropping the nūn of the jussive imperfect of كان:
The discussion has preceded on dropping the nūn of the jussive imperfect of كان, on condition that it is jussive with sukūn and not joined to an accusative pronoun or to a vowelless letter. This has occurred in the Revelation in eighteen places. Dropping it when followed by a vowelless letter has been heard in poetry; al-Khanjar ibn Ṣakhr al-Asadī said:
فإن لم تك المرآة أبدت وسامة ... فقد أبدت المرآة جبهة ضيغم
(If the mirror has not shown handsomeness, the mirror has shown the brow of a lion.)
He dropped the nūn despite meeting a vowelless letter. المرآة, with kasra on the mīm and a long hamza, is the instrument of seeing: it is as if he looked at his face in it and did not find it handsome, so he consoled himself that it resembled a ضيغم, which is the lion. الوسامة, with fatḥa on the wāw, is beauty and comeliness. The majority of grammarians took it as poetic necessity (ḍarūra), and cited as evidence the saying of al-Najāshī:
فلست يأتيه ولا أستطيعه ... ولاك اسقني إن كان ماؤك ذا فضل
(I am not one to come to it, nor am I able to; but give me to drink, if your water has any surplus.)
[Translator's note: the source prints «يأتيه»; the commentary below shows «بآتيه» is meant.]
So he dropped the nūn of لكن by poetic necessity. Al-Farrāʾ cited this verse as evidence that the doubled لكنّ is compound, its origin being لكن إنّ: the hamza was dropped for lightness, and the nūn of لكن because of the two vowelless letters. Among the curious things related about this verse is that a wolf came upon al-Najāshī the poet on his journey; he related that he invited the wolf to food and said to it: "Have you a brother" — meaning himself — "who will share his food with you without reproach or stinginess?" The wolf said to him: "You have invited me to something the beasts of prey before me have not done — eating together with the sons of Adam; I am not one to come to it, nor am I able to; but if there is, in the water you have with you, a surplus over what you need, then give me to drink of it".

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿غَافِرِ ٱلذَّنبِ وَقَابِلِ ٱلتَّوْبِ شَدِيدِ ٱلْعِقَابِ﴾.
He made them like an adjective (naʿt) of a definite noun, though they are indefinite; do you not see that you say: marartu bi-rajulin shadīdi al-qalbi ("I passed by a man strong of heart")? Except that together with them came His words ﴿ذى الطول﴾, which is definite, so they were made to run in its course. Their genitive may also be by repetition (takrīr, i.e. as a badal (substitute)), in which case definite and indefinite are the same. Similar are His words: ﴿وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الوَدُودُ، ذُو العرشِ المجيدُ، فعَّالٌ لما يريدُ﴾: this is by repetition, [163/ا] because faʿʿāl is purely indefinite. Similar are His words: ﴿رفيعُ الدرجاتِ ذو العرشِ﴾: rafīʿ is indefinite, and it was made to run as a fresh start (istiʾnāf), or on the explanation of the first case.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words: ﴿وَهَمَّتْ كُـلُّ أُمَّةٍ بِرَسُولِهِمْ﴾.
He referred it to the men. In the reading (ḥarf) of ʿAbdallāh it is "bi-rasūlihā" ("its messenger"), and all is correct.

farraa:8-8.t:
His words: ﴿وَأَدْخِلْهُمْ جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾.
Some read "jannata ʿadnin" in the singular, and so it is in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: singular.
His words: ﴿وَمَن صَـلَحَ مِنْ آبَآئِهِمْ﴾.
man is accusative from two possible places: if you wish you may make (wa-man) refer back to the hāʾ and mīm in "wa-adkhilhum", and if you wish to the hāʾ and mīm in "waʿadtahum".

farraa:10-10.t:
His words: ﴿يُنَادَوْنَ لَمَقْتُ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
The meaning in it is: they will be called out to that Allah's loathing of you is greater than your loathing of yourselves on the Day of Resurrection; for they loathed themselves since they had abandoned faith. But the lām suffices instead of saying, in speech: nādaytu anna Zaydan qāʾimun ("I proclaimed that Zayd is standing"), and nādaytu la-Zaydun qāʾimun. Similar is: ﴿ثم بَدا لهم من بعدِ ما رَأوا الآياتِ﴾ (the verse). The lām is equivalent to anna in every expression resembling "saying", such as "they are called out to", "they are told", and the like.

farraa:15-15.t:
His words: ﴿يُلْقِي ٱلرُّوحَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ﴾.
"The Spirit" in this place is prophethood: so that the one upon whom He casts the Spirit may warn of the Day of Meeting. It is called "the Meeting" (al-talāq) only because the people of heaven and the people of earth meet in it.

farraa:16-16.t:
His words: ﴿يَوْمَ هُم بَارِزُونَ﴾.
hum is in the position of a nominative by its predicate after it, and [it is] like your saying: ātīka yawma anta fārighun lī ("I will come to you on the day you are free for me").

farraa:18-18.t:
His words: ﴿ٱلأَزِفَةِ﴾.
It is the Resurrection.
His words: ﴿كَاظِمِينَ﴾.
It is accusative by qaṭʿ (detachment) from the meaning that refers back to them in "the hearts" and "the throats"; the meaning is: when their hearts are at their throats, suppressing [their grief]. If you wish you may make its detachment from the hāʾ in His words "wa-andhirhum"; the first is better in Arabic.
Had it been "kāẓimūna", nominative, on your saying: "when the hearts are at the throats, when they are suppressing", or as a fresh start, it would have been correct.
His words: ﴿مَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ وَلاَ شَفِيعٍ يُطَاعُ﴾:
whose intercession is accepted. Then He said: ﴿يَعْلَمُ خَآئِنَةَ ٱلأَعْيُنِ﴾, meaning Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is said: a man has two glances: the first is permitted to him and the second is forbidden to him. So His words ﴿يعلم خائنة﴾ al-aʿyun refer to the second glance, and "what the breasts conceal" to the first glance. If the first glance was deliberate, there is sin in it too; and if he did not intend it, it is forgiven.

farraa:26-26.t:
His words: ﴿أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim made (al-fasād) nominative, making the verb belong to it [yaẓhara al-fasādu, "that corruption appear"]. The people of Medina and al-Sulamī read: [wa-an] yuẓhira fī al-arḍi al-fasāda, making "corruption" accusative and making yuẓhira [the act] of Moses. The people of Medina drop the first alif, saying: wa-an yuẓhira, and so [it is] in their codices; while in the codices of the people of Iraq: "aw an yaẓhara". [The meaning] is that he said: I fear a change [163/ب] to your religion, or that people will hear [of it] and believe him, so that there will be corruption to your religion in it.

farraa:32-32.t:
His words: ﴿[وَ] يٰقَوْمِ إِنِّيۤ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلتَّنَادِ﴾.
The common people read it al-tanādi, light [without doubling]; al-Ḥasan alone kept the yāʾ [in it]. It is from tanādā al-qawm ("the people called out to one another"). [Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us:] al-Farrāʾ related to us; he said: Ḥibbān related to me from al-Ajlaḥ, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim, that he said: The angels will descend from the heavens and surround the regions of the earth, and Hell will be brought; when they see it, it will terrify them, and they will flee (nadda) in the earth as camels flee, but they will not head for any region without seeing angels, so they will return to where they came from. That is His words: ﴿يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ والإِنْسِ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تنفذوا من أقطار السماواتِ والأرضِ﴾, and that is His words: ﴿وجَاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا، وَجِىءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ﴾, and that is His words: ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ السَّمَاءُ بِالْغَمَامِ وَنُزِّلَ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ تَنْزِيلاً﴾. Al-Ajlaḥ said: and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read it "al-tanādd" with the dāl doubled. Ḥibbān said: and so al-Kalbī explained it, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
Al-Farrāʾ said: And whoever reads it "al-tanād" [light] means the day when the people of Paradise call out to the people of the Fire, and the people of the Fire to the people of Paradise, and the people of the Heights to men whom they recognize.

farraa:35-35.t:
His words: ﴿كَبُرَ مَقْتاً عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is: that disputing is grievous as an object of loathing [tamyīz (specification)]. Similar is: ﴿كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾: in kaburat their saying ﴿اتَّخَذَ اللّهُ وَلَداً﴾ is implied. Whoever makes "word" nominative implies nothing; al-Ḥasan read it so, with "word" nominative: ﴿كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةٌ تَخْرُجُ﴾.
His words: ﴿عَلَىٰ كُـلِّ قَلْبِ مُتَكَبِّرٍ جَبَّارٍ﴾: He puts "heart" in iḍāfa to "the arrogant one". Whoever uses tanwīn makes the heart itself the arrogant tyrant. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: "kadhālika yaṭbaʿu Allāhu ʿalā qalbi kulli mutakabbirin jabbārin" ("on the heart of every arrogant tyrant"); this is a witness for whoever reads with iḍāfa. The meaning, whether "heart" comes first or later, is the same, and Allah knows best.
He said: I heard one of the Arabs [say]: "He combs his hair on the day of every Friday", meaning "every Friday day"; and the meaning is the same.

farraa:36-37.t:
His words: ﴿لَّعَـلِّيۤ أَبْلُغُ ٱلأَسْبَابَ (أَسْبَابَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ) فَأَطَّلِعُ﴾.
With the nominative [fa-aṭṭaliʿu], referring it back to His words "ablughu". Whoever makes it an answer to laʿallī makes it accusative [fa-aṭṭaliʿa], and some readers read it so. He said: and one of the Arabs recited to me:
علَّ صروفَ الدَّهر أو دولاتها * يدللنا اللَّمَّةَ من لَمَّاتها * فتستريحَ النفسُ من زَفْراتها *
(Perhaps the turns of fortune or its changes will bring us round to one of its visitations, so that the soul may rest from its sighs.)
He used the accusative as the answer to laʿalla.

farraa:46-46.t:
His words: ﴿ٱلنَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا﴾.
You make (al-nār) nominative by what refers back to it in ʿalayhā. Had you made it nominative by what makes ﴿سُوءَ الْعَذَاب﴾ (45) nominative [i.e. as a badal (substitute) of it], it would have been correct. And had you made it accusative, on the ground that it falls [164/ا] between something referring back to it and speech connected with what precedes it, it would have been correct. Similar is: ﴿قُلْ أَفَأُنَبِّئكُمْ بِشَرٍّ مِنْ ذَلِكُم النارُ وَعَدهَا﴾.
His words: ﴿غُدُوًّا وَعَشِيًّا﴾.
In the Hereafter there is neither morning nor evening; rather, it is the measures of the evenings and mornings of this world.
His words: ﴿[وَ] يَوْمَ تَقُومُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدْخِلُوۤاْ آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and the people of the Hijaz pronounced the alif with hamza [adkhilū], while ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan made it light, reading "wa-yawma taqūmu al-sāʿatu udkhulū āla Firʿawna"; here "the family of Pharaoh" is accusative as a vocative: "Enter, O family of Pharaoh, the severest punishment". In the first case "adkhilū" falls upon them [as its object].

farraa:48-48.t:
His words: ﴿إِنَّا كُلٌّ فِيهَآ﴾.
You make (kull) nominative by fīhā, and do not make it an adjective of innā. And if you made it accusative on that basis [as tawkīd (emphasis)], making [fīhā] the predicate of innā «[Translator's note: the apodosis is missing in the source; presumably "it would be correct"]». Similar is: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ الأَمْرَ كُلَّهُ لِلّهِ﴾: you make ﴿كلّه لله﴾ nominative, and you make it accusative on this explanation.

farraa:51-51.t:
His words: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلأَشْهَادُ﴾.
The readers read with yāʾ, meaning yaqūmu in the masculine. Had a reader read "wa-yawma taqūmu", it would have been correct [Translator's note: the source prints «صوبا», a misprint for «صوابا»], because al-ashhād is a plural, and a plural of a masculine may have its verb feminine or masculine when the verb comes first. The Arabs say: dhahabat al-rijāl and dhahaba al-rijāl ("the men went").

farraa:56-56.t:
His words: ﴿إِلاَّ كِبْرٌ مَّـا هُم بِبَالِغِيهِ﴾.
He means: they were too proud to believe in what Muḥammad, Allah bless him, brought; they will not attain that, i.e. they will not obtain what they wanted.

farraa:67-67.t:
His words: ﴿ثُمَّ لِتَكُـونُواْ شُيُوخاً﴾.
In the reading (ḥarf) of ʿAbdallāh: "wa-minkum man yakūnu shuyūkhan" ("and among you are those who become old men"): He made the verb of man singular, then returned to "old men", intending the plural by man. Had He said "shaykhan" (singular), because man is singular in wording, it would have been correct.

farraa:71-71.t:
His words: ﴿إِذِ ٱلأَغْلاَلُ فِيۤ أَعْنَاقِهِمْ وٱلسَّلاَسِلُ﴾.
[You make "the chains" and "the shackles" nominative. And had you made "the chains" accusative and said: "yusḥabūna" (active: yasḥabūna), you would mean] they drag their chains in Hell.
Al-Kalbī mentioned from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: "[and they] are dragged in the chains". The genitive of "the chains" is not permissible, since the preposition would be implied; but had someone imagining it said: "the meaning is only: when their necks are in the shackles, and in the chains they are dragged", the genitive in "the chains" would be permissible on this approach. Similar, among what was referred back to the meaning, is the poet's saying:
قد سالم الحياتِ منه القدَما * الأُفعوانَ والشُّجاعَ الشجعما
(His foot has made peace with the snakes — the viper and the bold, fierce serpent.)
He made "the serpent" (al-shujāʿ) accusative, while "the snakes" before it are nominative «[Translator's note: the verse as printed in the source vowels الحياتِ with kasra, i.e. accusative]», because the meaning is: his foot made peace with the snakes and they made peace with it; when he needed the rhyme to be accusative, he made the verb of the foot fall upon the snakes.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «تنزيل» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); its khabar (predicate) is what the preposition phrase «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «غافر» is a badal (substitute), and likewise what follows it; the clause of transcendence [«لا إله إلا هو»] is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause, and the clause «إليه المصير» is a ḥāl clause.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «الذين» is the fāʿil (agent); the clause «فلا يغررك» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «في البلاد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) (تَقَلُّبهم).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «فأخذتهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «جادلوا», and the clause «فكيف كان عقاب» is conjoined to the clause «فأخذتهم»; «كيف» is an interrogative noun, the khabar of kāna; and «عقاب» is the noun of kāna, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ that was omitted for lightness.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The wāw is resumptive; the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: it came true with a coming-true like that coming-true; the clause «حَقَّتْ» is resumptive; and the interpreted maṣdar «أنهم أصحاب» is a badal (substitute) from «كلمت», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl).

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «الذين» is resumptive [i.e. begins a resumptive clause]; the preposition phrase «بحمد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يسبحون»; the vocative clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied (muqaddar) saying, and the implied clause of saying is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «يستغفرون», i.e.: saying: «ربنا وسعت»; «رحمة» is tamyīz (specification); the clause «فاغفر» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «وسعت»; «عذاب» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «ربنا» is parenthetical; the clause «وأَدْخِلهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the earlier clause «قِهِمْ»; «جنات» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «التي» is a naʿt (adjective); «مَنْ» is a relative noun conjoined to the hāʾ in «وعدتهم»; the preposition phrase «من آبائهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «صَلَح»; «أنت» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the kāf; and the clause «إنك أنت العزيز» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «السيئات» is a second object; the clause «وقهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَأَدْخِلْهُمْ}; the clause «ومن تق» is resumptive; «من» is a conditional noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «وذلك هو الفوز» is resumptive; and «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «لمقت الله أكبر» explains the calling; the lām in «لمقت» is of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); the preposition phrase «من مقتكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أكبر»; «أنفسكم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the maṣdar (verbal noun) «مقتكم»; «إذ» is an adverb of time attached to an implied (muqaddar) «مَقَتَكم». It is not attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the first «مقت», because the maṣdar and what it governs are not separated by the khabar (predicate); nor is it attached to the second, because the loathing is on the Day of Resurrection, not at the time they were called to faith.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «اثنتين» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose number stands in for it; the interrogative clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «اعترفنا»; the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «سبيل», and «من» is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «أنَّ» and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar in the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the conditional clause is the khabar of «أنَّ»; «وحده» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «يشرك» is a pronoun referring to a partner (sharīk), indicated by the context; the clause «فالحكم لله» is resumptive; «العلي الكبير» are two naʿts (adjectives) of the name of Majesty.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The two preposition phrases «لكم من السماء» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينزل», and the clause «وما يتذكر» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «فادعوا» is resumptive; «مخلصين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw; the preposition phrase «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مخلصين»; «الدين» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle «مخلصين»; the clause «ولو كره الكافرون» is a ḥāl clause, and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), conjoining to an implied (muqaddar) ḥāl for comprehensiveness, the implied form being: so call upon Allah, sincere in every state, even in this state; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: «رفيع» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: He is exalted; the clause "هو رفيع" is resumptive; «ذو» is a second khabar; the clause «يُلْقي» is a third khabar; the preposition phrase «من عباده» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «مَنْ»; the interpreted maṣdar in the genitive «لينذر» is attached to «يُلْقي»; «يوم» is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the first object is implied (muqaddar), i.e.: the people.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «يوم» is a badal (substitute) from {يَوْمَ التَّلاقِ}; the clause «هم بارزون» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause «لا يخفى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «بارزون»; the preposition phrase «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl of «شيء»; the clause «لمن الملك» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied (muqaddar) saying, i.e.: Allah says: «لمن الملك»; the clause «لله الواحد» is the object of the saying of an implied saying; the two implied clauses of saying are resumptive; «اليوم» is an adverb attached to a ḥāl of «الملك»; «الواحد القهار» are two naʿts (adjectives).

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The adverb «اليوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تجزى»; the clause «تجزى» is resumptive within the scope of the saying; «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar in the genitive is attached to «تجزى»; the clause «لا ظلم اليوم» is resumptive within the scope of the saying.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «يوم» is a second object, not an adverb, because the warning does not take place on the Day of the Approaching [Hour]; «إذ» is an adverbial noun, a badal (substitute) from «يوم»; «لدى» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); «كاظمين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «القلوب»; the clause «ما للظالمين حميم» is a ḥāl of «يوم الآزفة», the link being implied (muqaddar), i.e.: in it. «كاظمين» was given the plural of rational beings because there was attributed to them what is attributed to rational beings. «مِنْ» in «من حميم» is redundant (zāʾida), and the clause «يطاع» is a naʿt (adjective) of «شفيع».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: (يعلم خائنة الأعين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause «يعلم» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «والله يقضي بالحق» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «من دونه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الذين»; the clause «لا يقضون» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين»; «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); «البصير» is a second khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «أولم يسيروا» is resumptive; the clause «كيف كان» is the object of the looking, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative, [the looking] carrying the meaning of knowing; «كيف» is the khabar of kāna; the second clause «كانوا» is a badal (substitute) from the first; «هم» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the wāw in «كانوا»; the preposition phrase «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أشد»; «قوة» is tamyīz (specification); the preposition phrase «في الأرض» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «آثارًا»; the clause «فأخذهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «كانوا»; the clause «وما كان لهم واق» is conjoined to the clause «أخذهم»; «واق» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida); the preposition phrase «لهم» is attached to the khabar (predicate); and the preposition phrase «من الله» is attached to «واق».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The maṣdar from «أنَّ» and what follows it is in the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the noun of kāna is the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa), and the clause «تأتيهم» is its khabar. It is weak that it be the pronoun «هم», because He expressed the earlier peoples by the pronoun «هم»; and it is weak that «رسلهم» be its noun with the clause «تأتيهم» as its khabar, because the khabar of a mubtadaʾ (subject), if it is a verbal clause, does not come first. «رسلهم» is the fāʿil (agent) of «تأتيهم»; «شديد» is a second khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The preposition phrase «بآياتنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «موسى», i.e.: accompanied by Our signs.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أرسلنا»; the clause «فقالوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أرسلنا»; «ساحر» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: he is a sorcerer; «كذَّاب» is a second khabar; and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {أَرْسَلْنَا}; the preposition phrase «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جاءهم»; the preposition phrase «من عندنا» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الحق»; the adverb «معه» is attached to «آمنوا»; the clause «وما كيد الكافرين ...» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The clause «وقال فرعون» is resumptive; the clause «أقتل» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; the clause «وليدع» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ذروني»; the clause «إني أخاف» is resumptive within the scope of the saying; the interpreted maṣdar «أن يبدل» is the object of «أخاف»; the preposition phrase «في الأرض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الفساد».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «وقال موسى» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «من كل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عُذْت»; and the clause «لا يؤمن» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كل متكبر».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «وقال رجل» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «من آل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second naʿt (adjective); the clause «يكتم» is a third naʿt of «رجل»; the maṣdar «أن يقول» is accusative by removal of the preposition (al-lām), i.e.: for saying; the clause «وقد جاءكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «رجلا», and what permitted the owner of the ḥāl to be indefinite is the preceding interrogative; the preposition phrase «بالبينات» is attached to «جاء»; the preposition phrase «من ربكم» is attached to a ḥāl of «البينات»; the clause «وإن يك كاذبًا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أتقتلون»; «يكُ» is an abrogating (nāsikh) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) with the sukūn implied (muqaddar) on the nūn that was omitted for lightness.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: «اليوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being-settled (istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached; «ظاهرين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «لكم»; the preposition phrase «في الأرض» is attached to «ظاهرين»; the clause «فمن ينصرنا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition, i.e.: if this is your situation; the clause «إن جاءنا» is resumptive, and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. His saying «ما أرى»: a relative noun, the second object of «أريكم»; «سبيل» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: (إني أخاف عليكم مثل يوم الأحزاب) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «مثل» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: «مثل» is a badal (substitute) from the first; the clause «وما الله يريد» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items; the preposition phrase «للعباد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ظلمًا»; the clause «يريد..» is the khabar (predicate) of «ما» that operates like laysa.

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The clause «يا قوم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {يَا قَوْمِ} in verse (30).

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: «يوم» is a badal (substitute) from {يَوْمَ التَّنَادِ}; the clause «تُوَلُّون» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «مدبرين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «تولُّون»; the clause «ما لكم..عاصم» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «تولون»; «عاصم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida); the preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the preposition phrase «من الله» is attached to «عاصم»; the conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause answering the vocative, «إني أخاف»; «من» is a conditional noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and «هاد» is a mubtadaʾ, and «من» is redundant.

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The wāw is resumptive, and the lām occurs in the answer to an implied (muqaddar) oath; the preposition phrase «بالبينات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جاءكم»; «قبل» is indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation; the clause «فما زلتم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لقد جاءكم»; the preposition phrase «مما» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «شك»; «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya), and the clause after it is resumptive; the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: Allah leads astray with a leading-astray like that leading-astray; the clause «يضل» is resumptive; «مرتاب» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition phrase «بغير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يجادلون»; the clause «أتاهم» is a naʿt (adjective); the fāʿil of «كبر» is a pronoun referring to their disputing, understood from the context, and the clause «كبر جدالهم» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين»; «مقتًا» is tamyīz (specification) converted from the fāʿil, i.e.: the loathing of their state is great; the adverb «عند الله» is attached to (كَبُر); the clause «يطبع» is resumptive; and the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: Allah seals with a sealing like that sealing.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The clause «وقال فرعون» is resumptive, and the clause «لعلي أبلغ» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: «أسباب» is a badal (substitute); the fāʾ in «فأطلع» is causal (sababiyya), and the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e.: there is a hoping for reaching the means, and then a looking; «فأطلع» is accusative as the answer to the hoping in «لعل»; the clause «وإني لأظنه» is conjoined to the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The clause «زُيِّن» is resumptive, and the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: it was made fair-seeming to Pharaoh with a making-fair like that making-fair; the clause «وما كيد فرعون ...» is conjoined to the clause «صُدَّ»; «ما» is inoperative because its negation is broken by «إلا»; the preposition phrase «في تباب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «كيد».

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The clause «وقال» is resumptive; «اتبعون» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the nūn is of protection (nūn al-wiqāya); the clause «أَهْدِكم» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; «سبيل» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The clause «يا قوم» is resumptive within the scope of the saying; «إنما» is the restraining [mā] together with what it restrains (kāffa wa-makfūfa), having no governing effect.

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The conditional clause is resumptive within the scope of the saying; the clause «لا يُجزى» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: he is not recompensed, and the nominal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause «وهو مؤمن» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; the preposition phrase «من ذكر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «عمل»; the clause «يرزقون» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «يدخلون»; the preposition phrase «بغير» is attached to a ḥāl of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), the wāw.

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The clause «ويا قوم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to its like in verse (39); «ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition phrase «لي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the clause «أدعوكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «لي»; the clause «وتدعونني» is a ḥāl of the kāf implied (muqaddar) in (وما لكم تدعونني), and the implied clause is conjoined to the clause «ما لي».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: The clause «تدعونني» is a badal (substitute) from «تدعونني» before it; «ما» is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «ليس لي به علم» is the ṣila (relative clause); the preposition phrase «به» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «علم»; and the clause «وأنا أدعوكم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «تدعونني».

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: «لا جرم»: the lā of generic negation and its noun; «أن» is abrogating (nāsikha), «ما» is its noun, and the clause «ليس له دعوة» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن»; the interpreted maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition (في), attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar of «لا»; the preposition phrase «في الدنيا» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «دعوة»; the interpreted maṣdar «وأنَّ مردَّنا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding maṣdar; «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The clause «فستذكرون» is resumptive; «ما» is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «وأفَوِّض» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «إلى الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أفوض»; the preposition phrase «بالعباد» is attached to «بصير».

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The clause «فوقاه» is resumptive; «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause «وحاق» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «وقاه الله».

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: «النار» is a badal (substitute) from {سُوءُ الْعَذَابِ}; the clause «يُعْرضون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «النار»; «غُدُوًّا» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يُعرضون». His saying «ويوم تقوم»: the wāw is conjunctive; «يوم» is an adverb of time attached to a verb implied (muqaddar) as "it will be said"; «أشد» is a second object; the clause of the implied verb is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يُعرضون»; and the clause «أدخلوا» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of the implied [verb].

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The wāw is resumptive; «إذ» is an adverbial noun, the object of an implied (muqaddar) "remember"; the preposition phrase «في النار» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «يتحاجُّون»; the clause «فيقول» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يتحاجون»; the preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «تبعًا»; the clause «فهل أنتم مغنون» is conjoined to the clause «إنا كنا تبعًا»; the preposition phrase «عنا» is attached to «مغنون»; «نصيبًا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «مُغْنون», in the sense of "bearing"; the preposition phrase «من النار» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «نصيبًا».

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: «كلٌّ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); beginning with an indefinite is permitted because it indicates generality; the preposition phrase «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «كل»; the clause is the khabar of «إن»; and the clause «إن الله ...» is resumptive within the scope of the saying.

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The clause «وقال الذين» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {قَالَ الَّذِينَ}; the clause «يخففْ» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; «يومًا» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يخفف»; «مِنْ» is partitive: they asked that some of the punishment be lightened for them on some day.

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: His saying «أولم»: the wāw conjoins to something implied (muqaddar), and this implied thing is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), i.e.: did the messengers fall short, and were your messengers not coming to you? The verb «تك» is an abrogating (nāsikh) imperfect, jussive (majzūm) with the sukūn implied on the nūn that was omitted for lightness; its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); «رسلكم» is the fāʿil (agent) of «تأتيكم», and the clause «تأتيكم رسلكم» is the khabar (predicate) of «تك». It is weak to parse «رسلكم» as the noun of «تك» and the clause «تأتيكم» as the khabar, because the khabar of a mubtadaʾ (subject), if it is a verb, does not come first, in an example such as: زيد يدرس (Zayd studies), and likewise what resembles it. The object of the saying of «قالوا» is implied, i.e.: yes, the messengers came to us. The fāʾ in «فادعوا» occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if you want to call, then call; and the conditional clause is the object of the saying. The preposition phrase «في ضلال» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar, and «ما» is inoperative because its negation is broken by «إلا».

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The preposition phrase «في الحياة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ننصر»; «يوم» is an adverb conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the position of «في الحياة» and is attached to what it is attached to; and the clause «يقوم» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: «يوم»: a badal (substitute) from «يوم» before it; «معذرتهم» is the fāʿil (agent) of «ينفع»; and the clause «ولهم اللعنة» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لا ينفع».

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: «هدى» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the preposition phrase «لأولي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ذكرى».

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The clause «فاصبر» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «بحمد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «سبح».

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The preposition phrase «بغير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in «يجادلون»; the clause «أتاهم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «سلطان»; «إن» is negative; «كِبْر» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the negated clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; the clause «ما هم ببالغيه» is a naʿt of «كبر», and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar of «ما»; the clause «فاستعذ» is resumptive; «هو» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ in «إنه»; and «البصير» is a second khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: The lām is of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); the preposition phrase «من خلق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أكبر»; the clause of rectification (istidrāk) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لخلق السماوات والأرض أكبر».

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: The clause «وما يستوي الأعمى» is resumptive. His saying «والذين»: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «البصير». His saying «ولا المسيء»: «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation, and [«المسيء» is] a noun conjoined to «الذين»; «قليلا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and «ما» is redundant; and the clause «تتذكرون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: The clause «لا ريب» is a second khabar (predicate) of «إن», and the clause of rectification (istidrāk) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «إن الساعة لآتية».

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: The clause «وقال ربكم» is resumptive; the clause «أستجبْ» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; and «داخرين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw.

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: The clause «الله الذي» is resumptive; the interpreted maṣdar «لتسكنوا» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object in «جعل»; His saying «والنهار» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الليل», and «مبصرًا» is a noun conjoined to the preceding implied (muqaddar) second object; the preposition phrase «على الناس» is attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun) «فضل»; and the clause of rectification (istidrāk) is conjoined to the clause «إن الله لذو».

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: «ربكم» is a second khabar (predicate); «خالق» is a third khabar; the clause of transcendence [«لا إله إلا هو»] is a fourth khabar; «هو» is a badal (substitute) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar; the clause «فأنى تؤفكون» is resumptive; and «أنى» is an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: The kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: they are turned away with a turning-away like that turning-away; the clause «يجحدون» is the khabar of kāna; the preposition phrase «بآيات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يجحدون».

harrat-mujtaba:64-64.t: «الذي» is a khabar (predicate); the preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعل»; «السماء» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الأرض», and «بناء» is conjoined to «قرارًا»; the clause «ذلكم الله» is resumptive, and the clause «فتبارك الله» is conjoined to the clause «ذلكم الله»; «رب» is a badal (substitute).

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: The clause of transcendence [«لا إله إلا هو»] is a second khabar (predicate); the clause «فادعوه» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «هو الحي»; «مخلصين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw; the preposition phrase «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مخلصين»; «الدين» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «رب» is a badal (substitute).

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أن أعبد» is accusative by removal of the preposition (عن); the preposition phrase «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the relative noun; the conditional clause is parenthetical between the two conjoined items «نُهيت» and «أُمرت», and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it; the preposition phrase «من ربي» is attached to a ḥāl of «البينات»; the clause «وأُمرت» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «نهيت»; and the interpreted maṣdar «أن أسلم» is accusative by removal of the preposition (الباء).

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: The clause «ثم يخرجكم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «خلقكم»; «طفلا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the interpreted maṣdar «لتبلغوا» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being: then He keeps you alive so that you reach; the clause of the implied verb is conjoined to the clause «يخرجكم»; the clause «ومنكم مَنْ يتوفى» is parenthetical between the two interpreted maṣdars; and the clause «ولعلكم تعقلون» is conjoined to the single [word], the genitive maṣdar, i.e.: and for reaching the appointed term «ولعلكم تعقلون».

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «هو الذي»; «كن» is a complete (tāmm) imperative verb; the fāʾ is resumptive; and the clause «يكون» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: so it is.

harrat-mujtaba:69-69.t: «أنى» is an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause «يصرفون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: «الذين» is a badal (substitute) from the preceding relative noun, and the clause «فسوف يعلمون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: «إذ» is an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, attached to (mutaʿalliq) {يَعْلَمُونَ}, i.e.: they will come to know at the time when the shackles are on their necks; the clause «الأغلال في أعناقهم» is a nominal clause, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «السلاسل» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «يسحبون» is the khabar (predicate), the implied form being: they are dragged by them.

harrat-mujtaba:72-72.t: The preposition phrase «في الحميم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {يُسْحَبُونَ}; the clause «يُسْجرون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to {يُسْحَبُونَ}; and the preposition phrase «في النار» is attached to «يُسجرون».

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: «أين» is an interrogative noun, an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «ما».

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: The preposition phrase «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of {مَا} in the previous verse; the clause «قالوا» is resumptive; the clause «لم نكن» is resumptive; the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: Allah leads the disbelievers astray with a leading-astray like that leading-astray; and the clause «يضلُّ» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:75-75.t: The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the bāʾ is a preposition; «ما» is a relative noun in the position of the genitive, and the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the preposition phrase «بغير» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «تفرحون»; and the clause «ذلكم بما كنتم» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied (muqaddar) saying.

harrat-mujtaba:76-76.t: «خالدين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «ادخلوا»; the preposition phrase «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خالدين»; the clause «فبئس مثوى» is resumptive, and the specified noun (al-makhṣūṣ) is omitted, i.e.: Hell.

harrat-mujtaba:77-77.t: The clause «فاصبر» is resumptive. His saying «فإما»: the fāʾ is conjunctive, «إن» is conditional and «ما» is redundant (zāʾida); [«نرينك» is] an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the nūn, and the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «فإمَّا نرينك» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «إن وعد الله حق»; and the clause «فإلينا يرجعون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of both conditions together. The apodosis is joined with the fāʾ, although originally it does not need it, because the preposition phrase is placed before the apodosis.

harrat-mujtaba:78-78.t: The clause «ولقد أرسلنا» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «من قبلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رسلا»; the clause «منهم مَنْ قصصنا» is a second naʿt of «رسلا»; the clause «وما كان لرسول أن يأتي» is resumptive, and the interpreted maṣdar is the noun of kāna; the preposition phrase «بإذن» is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «وما كان لرسول ...»; «هنالك»: a demonstrative, an adverb of place, attached to «خسر».

harrat-mujtaba:79-79.t: «الذي» is the khabar (predicate) of the name of Majesty; «جعل» is in the sense of "created", transitive to one object; the interpreted maṣdar in the genitive «لتركبوا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعل»; the clause «ومنها تأكلون» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items. Conjunction is not valid, because the verb is nominative and what it would be conjoined to is accusative; nor is resumption valid, because of the strength of the connection.

harrat-mujtaba:80-80.t: The clause «ولكم فيها منافع» is a nominal clause conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the single [word] {لِتَرْكَبُوا}, i.e.: He created the livestock for you for your riding «ولكم فيها منافع», as in: جئت للدراسة، ولي حاجة أخرى ("I came for study, and I have another need"). The preposition phrase «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «منافع»; the second interpreted maṣdar «ولتبلغوا» is conjoined to the earlier interpreted maṣdar {لِتَرْكَبُوا}; the preposition phrase «في صدوركم» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «حاجة»; and the clause «وعليها ... تُحملون» is conjoined to the clause «منها تأكلون»; the distant item was chosen as what it is conjoined to, so that the clauses match one another.

harrat-mujtaba:81-81.t: The clause «ويريكم آياته» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ṣila (relative clause) of {الَّذِي جَعَلَ} in verse (79), and «آياته» is a second object; the fāʾ in «فأيَّ» is conjunctive, and the clause «تنكرون» is conjoined to the clause «ويريكم»; «أيَّ» is an interrogative noun, an object of «تنكرون» placed first. Resumption is far-fetched because of the strong connection between seeing the signs and the question about denying them.

harrat-mujtaba:82-82.t: The clause «أفلم يسيروا» is resumptive, and the clause «فينظروا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive one; «كيف» is an interrogative noun, the khabar of kāna; the clause «كان» is the object of the looking, which carries the meaning of knowing, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative; the preposition phrase «من قبلهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause); the clause «كانوا» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «منهم» is attached to «أكثر», and «قوة» is tamyīz (specification); the preposition phrase «في الأرض» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «آثار»; the clause «فما أغنى» is conjoined to the clause «كانوا»; «ما» is a nominal relative, the fāʿil (agent) of «أغنى».

harrat-mujtaba:83-83.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «كانوا»; the adverb «عندهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause); the preposition phrase «من العلم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما»; «ما» is the fāʿil (agent) of «حاق»; the preposition phrase «بهم» is attached to «يستهزئون».

harrat-mujtaba:84-84.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding conditional clause; «وحده» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the name of Majesty; the preposition phrase «به» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مشركين».

harrat-mujtaba:85-85.t: The clause «فلم يك» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «كفرنا»; «يك» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) with the sukūn implied (muqaddar) on the nūn that was omitted for lightness; the noun of «يك» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause «ينفعهم» is its khabar (predicate). It is weak for the noun of «يك» to be «إيمانهم», because the khabar clause does not come first in an example such as: «زيد يدرس» (Zayd studies). The clause «لما رأوا» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it; «سنة» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied governor, i.e.: سَنَّ ("He laid down as a practice"). «هنالك» is a demonstrative, an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خسر», and the clause «خسر.. الكافرون» is conjoined to the clause «فلم يك».

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying حم: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read حاميمَ with fatḥa on the mīm because of the meeting of two quiescents; he intended joining (waṣl) and did not intend pausing. Pausing is the basic rule for the disjointed letters and for the enumeration of numbers, when you say "one, two, three, four"; if you conjoin some of them to others or predicate something of them, you inflect them, and likewise the letters. It has also been said that حاميم is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "recite Ḥā Mīm" or "read Ḥā Mīm"; but it is not fully declined (a diptote) because it is the name of the surah, so it is the name of something feminine, and because it is on the pattern of a foreign noun, like هابيل.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {إِذْ تدعون إِلَى الْإِيمَان فتكفرون}: what governs إذ is a verb, its implied form being "remember when you were called". It is not permissible for لمقت to govern it, because the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) has come before it and is not included in the ṣila (relative complement); and إذ would be included in the ṣila of لمقت if you made it govern it, so you would have separated the ṣila from what it belongs to (the maṣdar) by the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. Nor is it good for تُدعون to govern إذ, because إذ is in construct with it, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf. Nor is it permissible for مقتكم to govern إذ, because the meaning does not support it: they were not hating themselves at the time when they were called to faith and disbelieved.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {يَوْم هم بارزون}: هم بارزون is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the genitive position, because يوم is put in construct with it. Adverbs of time, when they are in the sense of إذ, are put in construct with clauses — with verb and agent and with mubtadaʾ and khabar — just as is done with إذ. When they are in the sense of إذا, they are put in construct only with verb and agent, as is done with إذا. If a nominative noun occurs after إذا, it is nominative by an implied verb, because إذا carries the meaning of condition and is for what is in the future, and a condition is only for the future, in wording or in meaning; and a condition is only with a verb. So إذا is more suited to the verb, and that is why a verb follows it, implied or overt. إذ is not like that, because there is no meaning of condition in it, since it is for what is past, and a condition is not for what is past. So understand that.

mekki-muskil:18-18.t:
His saying {وَلَا شَفِيع يطاع}: يطاع is a naʿt (adjective) of شفيع. It is in the genitive position according to the wording of شفيع, or in the nominative position according to the position of شفيع, since it is nominative in meaning; من is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. The meaning is: "The wrongdoers have no devoted friend nor intercessor who is obeyed."

[Translator's note: the من referred to is not in the quoted words; the verse reads ما للظالمين من حميم ولا شفيع يطاع.]

mekki-muskil:21-21.t:
His saying فينظروا is in the (accusative) position as the answer to the question; and if you wish, in the jussive position, conjoined to يسيروا. [Translator's note: the source has «في موضع على جواب الاستفهام», with the case word (evidently «نصب») missing.]

His saying كيف كان عاقبة: كيف is the khabar (predicate) of كان and عاقبة its ism (noun); in كيف there is a pronoun referring back to العاقبة, just as when you say أين زيد and كيف عمرو, in أين and كيف there are two pronouns referring back to the mubtadaʾ (subject); they are two fronted khabars which take the head of the sentence. It is also possible that كان is in the sense of حدث ("came about"), so it needs no khabar, and كيف is then a superfluous ẓarf with no pronoun in it. Likewise الذين كانوا من قبلهم has the two views, and likewise كانوا هم أشد منهم has the two views; if you make كان in the sense of حدث, أشد is then an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:28-28.t: His saying {وَإِن يَك كَاذِبًا}: the nūn was dropped from يك, according to Sībawayh, only because of frequency of use. Al-Mubarrad said: because it resembled the nūn of inflection — he means in your saying تدخلين, تدخلون and تدخلان.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying {مثل دأب} is a badal (substitute) for the first مثل.

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His saying {يَوْم تولون} is a badal (substitute) for the first يوم.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t:
His saying {الَّذين يجادلون}: الذين is in the accusative position as a badal (substitute) for من, (or) in the nominative position by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are those who…".

[Translator's note: the source reads «على البدل من من في موضع رفع» with no "or"; the conjunction is supplied from the sense.]

mekki-muskil:46-46.t:
His saying {النَّار يعرضون عَلَيْهَا}: النار is a badal (substitute) for سوء العذاب, or (nominative) by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); and (on another view, النار is a mubtadaʾ and) يعرضون the khabar (predicate). In (ordinary) speech the accusative is permissible by an implied verb, its implied form being "they come to the Fire, being exposed to it". The genitive is also permissible, as a badal from العذاب.

His saying {وَيَوْم تقوم السَّاعَة}: يوم is accusative, governed by أدخلوا, when you make the alif conjunctive (hamzat al-waṣl). [Translator's note: in either reading يوم is governed by the imperative.] Whoever made the alif of أدخلوا disjunctive (hamzat al-qaṭʿ) and gave the khāʾ kasra (أَدْخِلوا) put آل فرعون in the accusative by أدخلوا; and whoever read it with the alif conjunctive and the khāʾ with ḍamma (ادْخُلوا) put آل فرعون in the accusative as a vocative with a muḍāf.

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {إِنَّا كُنَّا لكم تبعا}: تبعا is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the khabar (predicate) of كان; that is why it was not put in the plural.

mekki-muskil:48-48.t: His saying {إِنَّا كل فِيهَا}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the khabar of إنّ. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ allowed كلًّا in the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of the pronoun made accusative by إنّ. That is not permissible according to the Basrans, because a pronoun is not given an adjective, and because كلّ is indefinite in wording. (Yet) كلّ, although its wording is indefinite, is definite according to Sībawayh, on the implied construct and omission. Nor is the badal (substitute) permissible, because nothing else is substituted for (a pronoun of the speaker) speaking about himself.

mekki-muskil:54-54.t: His saying {هدى} is in the accusative position as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and ذكرى is conjoined to it.

mekki-muskil:55-55.t: His saying {وَالْإِبْكَار}: whoever gave the hamza fatḥa (الأبكار), it is the plural of بُكَر.

mekki-muskil:56-56.t: His saying {مَا هم ببالغيه}: the hāʾ refers to what they want, i.e. they will not attain their desire in it. It has also been said that the hāʾ refers to الكبر (the pride).

mekki-muskil:71-71.t: His saying {يسْحَبُونَ} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in أعناقهم. It has also been said that it is nominative as a new (resumptive) sentence. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read والسلاسلَ in the accusative and يَسحَبون with fatḥa on the yāʾ, putting السلاسل in the accusative by يسحبون. It has also been read والسلاسلِ in the genitive, conjoined to الأعناق; this is an error, because it would make the shackles be in the necks and in the chains, and a shackle in a chain makes no sense. It has also been said that it is conjoined to الحميم, and that too is not permissible, because a genitive conjoined element cannot come before what it is conjoined to: مررت وزيد بعمرو is not permissible. It is permissible with the nominative: you say قام وزيد عمرو. It is far-fetched with the accusative: رأيت وزيدا عمرا is not good. No one has allowed it with the genitive.

mekki-muskil:75-75.t: His saying {ذَلِكُم بِمَا كُنْتُم}: ذلكم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) omitted, its implied form being "that punishment of yours is because of your exulting in this world in sins"; and that is the meaning of His saying بغير الحق.

mekki-muskil:81-81.t: His saying {فَأَي آيَات الله تنكرون}: أيّ is accusative, governed by تنكرون. Had there been a hāʾ with the verb, the nominative would be preferred for أيّ — unlike the interrogative alif entering upon a noun followed by a verb that falls on a pronoun of the noun; there the accusative is preferred, as in your saying أزيدا ضربته.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿حم﴾: The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم﴾: ﴿تنزيل الكتاب﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿من الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); and ﴿العزيز العليم﴾ are two attributes (ṣifatān).

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿غافر الذنب وقابل التوب شديد العقاب ذي الطول﴾: attributes of the Divine Name in the previous verse.
﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation (lā al-nāfiya li-l-jins).
﴿إله﴾: its ism (noun), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿هو﴾: a badal (substitute) from the position of لا together with its ism, because their position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); or a badal from the pronoun concealed in the omitted khabar (predicate).
﴿إليه المصير﴾: ﴿إليه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar; and ﴿المصير﴾ is a postponed mubtadaʾ.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿ما يجادل في آيات الله إلا الذين كفروا﴾: ﴿ما﴾ is negating; ﴿يجادل﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿في آيات الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يجادل﴾; ﴿إلا﴾ is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿الذين﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿كفروا﴾ is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿فلا يغررك تقلبهم في البلاد﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; ﴿لا﴾ is prohibitive (nāhiya); ﴿يغررك﴾ is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿تقلبهم﴾ is the fāʿil; and ﴿في البلاد﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تقلبهم﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح والأحزاب من بعدهم﴾: ﴿كذبت﴾ is a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; ﴿قبلهم﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿قوم نوح﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿الأحزاب﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿قوم نوح﴾; and ﴿من بعدهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl.
﴿وهمت كل أمة برسولهم ليأخذوه﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿همت﴾ is conjoined to ﴿كذبت﴾; ﴿كل أمة﴾ is the fāʿil; ﴿برسولهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿همت﴾; the lām is for cause (taʿlīl); ﴿يأخذوه﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿همت﴾.
﴿وجادلوا بالباطل ليدحضوا به الحق فأخذتهم فكيف كان عقاب﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿جادلوا﴾ is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and it is conjoined to ﴿همت﴾; ﴿بالباطل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl, or attached to ﴿جادلوا﴾; ﴿ليدحضوا﴾: the lām is for cause, and ﴿يدحضوا﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿جادلوا﴾; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يدحضوا﴾; ﴿الحق﴾ is mafʿūl bihi; ﴿فأخذتهم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿جادلوا﴾; ﴿فكيف﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ﴿كيف﴾ is an interrogative noun, in the position of accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان; and ﴿عقاب﴾ is the ism (noun) of كان, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the letter before the omitted yāʾ of the first person.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وكذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين كفروا أنهم أصحاب النار﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative as an attribute (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) placed before its governing word; or in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and the matter is like that"; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; ﴿كلمة ربك﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿على الذين كفروا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حقت﴾; and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أنهم أصحاب النار﴾ is a nominative badal (substitute) from ﴿كلمة ربك﴾, or in [the position of] accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), that preposition being the lām of cause [Translator's note: the source reads «أو في منصوب», apparently a slip for «أو في محل نصب» or «أو منصوب»].

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿الذين يحملون العرش ومن حوله يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويؤمنون به﴾: ﴿الذين﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يحملون﴾ is an imperfect verb, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and العرش is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿يحملون العرش﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; ﴿من﴾ is a relative noun in the position of nominative, conjoined to the mubtadaʾ; ﴿حوله﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila of ﴿مَن﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. ﴿يسبحون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; ﴿بحمد﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "accompanied by praise"; ﴿ربهم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿يسبحون بحمد ربهم﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿الذين﴾; ﴿يؤمنون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يؤمنون﴾; and ﴿يؤمنون﴾ is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿يسبحون﴾.
﴿ويستغفرون للذين آمنوا ربنا وسعت كل شيء رحمة وعلما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿يستغفرون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; ﴿للذين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يستغفرون﴾; the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position, and it is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; ﴿ربنا﴾ is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, from which the vocative particle has been omitted, and the vocative clause is the object of an omitted saying, in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "saying"; ﴿وسعت﴾ is a past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil; ﴿كل شيء﴾ is mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿رحمة وعلمًا﴾ are two tamyīz (specification) [accusatives], and the tamyīz here is converted from the fāʿil, i.e. "Your mercy encompasses everything, and Your knowledge encompasses everything".
﴿فاغفر للذين تابوا واتبعوا سبيلك﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; ﴿اغفر﴾ is a verb of supplication, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت"; ﴿للذين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿اغفر﴾; the clause ﴿تابوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; ﴿اتبعوا سبيلك﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and سبيلك is mafʿūl bihi; and the clause is conjoined to ﴿للذين تابوا﴾.
﴿وقهم عذاب الجحيم﴾: ﴿قِ﴾ is a verb of supplication, mabnī (indeclinable) on the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "أنت"; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿عذاب الجحيم﴾ is the second mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿ربنا وأدخلهم جنات عدن التي وعدتهم ومن صلح من آبائهم وأزواجهم وذرياتهم﴾: ﴿ربنا﴾ is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, from which the vocative particle has been omitted; ﴿أدخلهم﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded, and ﴿أدخلهم﴾ is a verb of supplication, the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت", and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿جنات عدن﴾ is the second mafʿūl bihi, by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); ﴿التي﴾ is an attribute (ṣifa); and the clause ﴿وعدتهم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾, with no grammatical position. ﴿مَن﴾ is a relative noun in the position of accusative, conjoined to the object of ﴿أدخلهم﴾ or to the object of ﴿وعدتهم﴾; the clause ﴿صلح﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; ﴿من آبائهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿أزواجهم وذرياتهم﴾ are conjoined to ﴿آبائهم﴾.
﴿إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the kāf is its ism (noun); ﴿أنت﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and العزيز الحكيم are two predicates (khabarān) of ﴿أنت﴾, and the clause is the khabar of ﴿إنك﴾; or ﴿أنت﴾ is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, and ﴿العزيز الحكيم﴾ are two predicates of ﴿إن﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وقهم السيئات ومن تق السيئات يومئذ فقد رحمته﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿قهم﴾ is an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت"; ﴿هم﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿السيئات﴾ is the second mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿مَن﴾ is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿تق﴾ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; ﴿السيئات﴾ is mafʿūl bihi; ﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تقِ﴾, and إذٍ is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied sukūn, because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when he is taken to account for them". ﴿فقد﴾: the fāʾ links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿أخزيته﴾ is a past verb, the tāʾ is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi, and the clause has no grammatical position [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse here reads ﴿فقد رحمته﴾, and «أخزيته» appears to be carried over from a similar verse (Āl ʿImrān 3:192); the analysis applies equally to رحمته].
﴿وذلك هو الفوز العظيم﴾: ﴿ذلك﴾ is the mubtadaʾ; ﴿هو﴾ is a second mubtadaʾ; and ﴿الفوز العظيم﴾ are two predicates (khabarān) of ﴿هو﴾; or ﴿هو﴾ is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, and ﴿الفوز العظيم﴾ are two predicates of ﴿ذلك﴾.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿إن الذين كفروا ينادون لمقت الله أكبر من مقتكم أنفسكم﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿الذين﴾ is its ism (noun); ﴿كفروا﴾ is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿الذين﴾, with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿ينادون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of إن; ﴿ينادون﴾ is an imperfect verb, passive, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); ﴿مقت الله﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject), the annexation being of the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its agent, while the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, i.e. "you (إياكم)"; ﴿أكبر﴾ is the khabar; ﴿من مقتكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أكبر﴾; and ﴿أنفسكم﴾ is the object of ﴿مقتكم﴾.
﴿إذ تدعون إلى الإيمان فتكفرون﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being: "He detested you when you were called", or: "remember when you were called"; the clause ﴿تدعون﴾ is in the position of genitive by annexation; ﴿تدعون﴾ is an imperfect verb, passive, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; ﴿إلى الإيمان﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تدعون﴾; ﴿فتكفرون﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ﴿تكفرون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿قالوا ربنا أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين فاعترفنا بذنوبنا فهل إلى خروج من سبيل﴾: ﴿قالوا﴾ is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿ربنا﴾ is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, from which the vocative particle has been omitted; ﴿أمتنا﴾ is a past verb, the tāʾ is the fāʿil, and ﴿نا﴾ is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿اثنتين﴾ stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is its number; ﴿أحييتنا اثنتين﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿أمتنا اثنتين﴾; ﴿اعترفنا﴾ is a past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil; ﴿بذنوبنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اعترفنا﴾; ﴿فهل﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ﴿هل﴾ is an interrogative particle; ﴿إلى خروج﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿من﴾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) particle; and ﴿سبيل﴾ is genitive in form and nominative in position, as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿ذلكم بأنه إذا دعي الله وحده كفرتم﴾: ﴿ذلكم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿بأنه﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, ﴿أن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its ism (noun); ﴿إذا﴾ is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; ﴿دعي﴾ is a past verb, passive; ﴿الله﴾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause ﴿دعي﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; ﴿وحده﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿كفرتم﴾ is a past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿كفرتم﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the answer of ﴿إذا﴾; the conditional clause and its answer are the khabar (predicate) of ﴿أنه﴾; and the clause ﴿بأنه...﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
﴿وإن يشرك به تؤمنوا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿إن﴾ is conditional; ﴿يشرك﴾ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), and it is an imperfect verb, passive; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted [word] that takes the place of the nāʾib fāʿil; and ﴿تؤمنوا﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
﴿فالحكم لله العلي الكبير﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; ﴿الحكم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ; ﴿لله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to its omitted khabar; and ﴿العلي الكبير﴾ are two attributes (ṣifatān).

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿هو الذي يريكم آياته وينزل لكم من السماء رزقا﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; ﴿هو﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿الذي﴾ is the khabar (predicate); ﴿يريكم﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿يريكم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; ﴿آياته﴾ is mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) with kasra; ﴿ينزل﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative, the fāʿil is latent, and it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿يريكم﴾; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينزل﴾; and ﴿من السماء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ينزل﴾.
﴿وما يتذكر إلا من ينيب﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿ما﴾ is negating; ﴿يتذكر﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative; ﴿إلا﴾ is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿مَن﴾ is the fāʿil; ﴿ينيب﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is latent; and the clause ﴿ينيب﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿فادعوا الله مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; ﴿ادعوا﴾ is an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the Divine Name is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿مخلصين﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مخلصين﴾; ﴿الدين﴾ is mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿لو﴾ is conditional; ﴿كره الكافرون﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil, and the mafʿūl bihi is omitted, i.e. "your sincerity", or: "your calling [upon Him]".

muyesser-irab:15-15.t: ﴿رفيع الدرجات ذو العرش يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده لينذر يوم التلاق﴾: ﴿رفيع الدرجات﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿ذو العرش﴾ is a second khabar; ﴿يلقي الروح﴾: an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الروح﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is a third khabar; ﴿من أمره﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يلقي﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿الروح﴾, i.e. "in the state of its arising from His command"; ﴿على من﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يلقي﴾; the clause ﴿يشاء﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; ﴿من عباده﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿لينذر﴾: the lām is for cause (taʿlīl), and ﴿ينذر﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يلقي﴾; the fāʿil is "هو": Allah, or the Spirit (الروح), or whomever He wills; ﴿يوم﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi of ﴿ينذر﴾; and ﴿التلاق﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿يوم هم بارزون لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء﴾: ﴿يوم﴾ is a badal (substitute) from ﴿يوم التلاق﴾, a badal of the whole for the whole; ﴿هم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿بارزون﴾ is the khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; ﴿لا﴾ is negating; ﴿يخفى﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿على الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يخفى﴾; ﴿منهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an attribute of ﴿شيء﴾; ﴿شيء﴾ is the fāʿil (agent) of ﴿يخفى﴾; and the clause ﴿لا يخفى ...﴾ is a ḥāl from the pronoun of ﴿بارزون﴾, or a second khabar; and it was said: it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿لمن الملك اليوم لله الواحد القهار﴾: the clause is the object of an omitted saying, i.e. He the Exalted says it and answers Himself; the saying is conjoined to what precedes it, or it is resumptive, in answer to an implied question, as if it were asked: "So what will happen then?", and it was said: "It will be said: To whom belongs the dominion…?"; ﴿لمن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; ﴿الملك﴾ is a postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿اليوم﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf), attached to ﴿الملك﴾; ﴿لله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "the dominion is Allah's"; and ﴿الواحد القهار﴾ are two naʿts (adjectives) of الله.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿اليوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت﴾: ﴿اليوم﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تجزى﴾, and the speech is a continuation of what is said; ﴿تجزى﴾ is an imperfect verb, passive; ﴿كل نفس﴾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿بما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تجزى﴾, and ﴿ما﴾ is relative or adverbial (ẓarfiyya); ﴿كسبت﴾ is a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and the clause ﴿كسبت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
