muyesser-irab:63-63.t: ﴿كذلك يؤفك الذين كانوا بآيات الله يجحدون﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative as an attribute of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "like your being turned away, those who … are turned away"; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; يؤفك: a passive imperfect verb (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu); الذين: the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause ﴿كانوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. kāna is an incomplete past verb (one of kāna and its sisters), and the wāw of the plural is its ism (noun); بآيات: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يجحدون﴾; يجحدون: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); and the clause ﴿يجحدون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of kāna.

muyesser-irab:64-64.t:
﴿الله الذي جعل لكم الأرض قرارا والسماء بناء وصوركم فأحسن صوركم﴾: resumptive speech, with no grammatical position; الله: the mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي: its khabar (predicate); جعل: a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause ﴿جعل﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. لكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جعل﴾; الأرض: the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); قرارًا: the second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿والسماء بناء﴾: both conjoined to ﴿الأرض قرارا﴾, accusative; صوركم: a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; فأحسن: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and أحسن is a past verb, and the fāʿil is latent; and صوركم: the mafʿūl bihi.
﴿ورزقكم من الطيبات ذلكم الله ربكم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; رزقكم: a verb with a latent fāʿil, and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; من الطيبات: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿رزقكم﴾; ذلكم: the mubtadaʾ; الله: the khabar; ربكم: a second khabar, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿فتبارك الله رب العالمين﴾: the fāʾ: a conjunction; تبارك: a past verb; الله: the fāʿil; رب: a naʿt (adjective) of Allah; and العالمين: muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:65-65.t:
﴿هو الحي﴾: هو: the mubtadaʾ (subject), and الحي: the khabar (predicate); ﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation (lā al-nāfiya li-l-jins).
﴿إله﴾: its ism (noun), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿هو﴾: a badal (substitute) from the position of lā together with its ism, because their position is nominative as mubtadaʾ; or a badal from the pronoun concealed in the omitted khabar; and the clause ﴿لا إله إلا هو﴾ is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of ﴿هو﴾.
﴿فادعوه مخلصين له الدين﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; ادعوه: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); مخلصين: a ḥāl (circumstantial); له: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مخلصين﴾; and الدين: the mafʿūl bihi of ﴿مخلصين﴾.
﴿الحمد لله رب العالمين﴾: الحمد: the mubtadaʾ; لله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar; رب: an attribute (ṣifa) of Allah; العالمين: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ in place of the kasra, because it is treated like the sound masculine plural; and the clause is the object of an omitted saying which is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of fa-dʿūhu, i.e. saying: ﴿الحمد لله ...﴾; or it is resumptive, being His own speech, Glorified is He, and it has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:66-66.t:
﴿قل إني نهيت أن أعبد الذين تدعون من دون الله لما جاءني البينات من ربي﴾: resumptive speech, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿إني نهيت...﴾ is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech); إن is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), and the yāʾ is its ism (noun); the clause ﴿نهيت﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna; نهيت: a passive past verb (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); أن: a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; أعبد: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); الذين: a relative noun in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar formed from ﴿أن﴾ and what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. "from worshipping those whom you call upon"; تدعون: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿تدعون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; من دون الله: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and the Divine Name is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); لما: an adverb (ẓarf) meaning "when", in the position of accusative, attached to ﴿نهيت﴾; ﴿جاءني البينات﴾: a past verb, the yāʾ is a fronted mafʿūl bihi, and البينات is a postponed fāʿil; and the clause ﴿جاءني﴾ is in the position of genitive through the adverb's annexation to it.
﴿وأمرت أن أسلم لرب العالمين﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; أمرت: a past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil; أن: a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; أسلم: an imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is latent; an together with what falls within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "with submission"; لرب: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أسلم﴾; and العالمين: muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:67-67.t:
﴿هو الذي خلقكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة﴾: هو: the mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي: the khabar (predicate); خلقكم: a past verb, the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿خلقكم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. من تراب: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلقكم﴾; and the speech is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة﴾ is conjoined to ﴿من تراب﴾.
﴿ثم يخرجكم طفلا﴾: also conjoined; يخرجكم: an imperfect verb with a latent fāʿil, and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; and طفلًا: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf in ﴿يخرجكم﴾.
﴿ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم ثم لتكونوا شيوخا﴾: also conjoined; the lām is causal (li-l-taʿlīl); تبلغوا: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "then He keeps you alive"; ﴿لتكونوا﴾: the lām is causal, and تكونوا is an incomplete imperfect verb (one of kāna and its sisters), accusative by an implied an after the lām; the wāw is the ism (noun) of ﴿تكون﴾, and شيوخا is its khabar; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "then He keeps you alive".
﴿ومنكم من يتوفى من قبل﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; منكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar of ﴿مَن﴾; ﴿من﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; يتوفى: a passive imperfect verb (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; and من قبل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يتوفى﴾.
﴿ولتبلغوا أجلا مسمى ولعلكم تعقلون﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ولتبلغوا: the lām is causal, and تبلغوا is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied an after the lām, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "then He keeps you alive"; أجلًا: the mafʿūl bihi; مسمى: a naʿt (adjective); ولعلكم: the wāw is conjunctive, laʿalla is an abrogating particle of hope (one of inna and its sisters), and ﴿كم﴾ is its ism; the clause taʿqilūn is the khabar of laʿalla; and تعقلون: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:68-68.t: ﴿هو الذي يحيي ويميت فإذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون﴾: هو: the mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي: its khabar (predicate); يحيي: an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause ﴿يحيي﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. يميت: conjoined to yuḥyī; فإذا: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and إذا is a future adverb (ẓarf) in the position of accusative, containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يقول﴾; قضى: a past verb, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause ﴿قضى﴾ is in the position of genitive through the adverb's annexation to it; أمرًا: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فإنما﴾: the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa), and إنما is a restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle; يقول: an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being: huwa; له: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يقول﴾; كن: a complete (tāmm) imperative verb with a latent fāʿil, its implied form being: anta. ﴿فيكون﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; يكون: a complete imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is latent; the clause ﴿يكون﴾ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "so it is"; or it is conjoined to ﴿يقول﴾ or to ﴿كن﴾; and the clause ﴿فيكون﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:69-69.t: ﴿ألم تر إلى الذين يجادلون في آيات الله أنى يصرفون﴾: the hamza is interrogative; لم: a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; تر: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: anta; إلى الذين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تر﴾; يجادلون: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿يجادلون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. في آيات: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يجادل﴾, and the Divine Name is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); أنى: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and يصرفون: a passive imperfect verb (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

muyesser-irab:70-70.t: ﴿الذين كذبوا بالكتاب وبما أرسلنا به رسلنا فسوف يعلمون﴾: الذين: a relative noun in the position of genitive as a badal (substitute) from ﴿الذين﴾ in the previous verse; or in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); or in the position of accusative on account of censure (ʿalā al-dhamm); or in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is ﴿فسوف يعلمون﴾. كذبوا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿كذبوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; بالكتاب: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبوا﴾; وبما: the wāw is conjunctive, the bāʾ is a preposition, and ما is a relative noun in the position of genitive; أرسلنا: a past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿أرسلنا﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; به: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أرسلنا﴾; and رسلنا: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فسوف يعلمون﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; سوف: a particle of futurity; يعلمون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); and the clause ﴿فسوف يعلمون﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; or it is in the position of nominative as a khabar, on considering ﴿الذين﴾ a mubtadaʾ, and the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa) because of the hint of condition in the relative noun.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
With a sukūn on the final mīm, because they are letters of the alphabet (ḥurūf al-hijāʾ), and their rule is to be quiescent, since one pauses on them.
As for the reading of ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar «حاميمَ تنزيل», it has fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; and it is also possible that it is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by an implied verb, and it is not declined [i.e. is a diptote] because it is the name of something feminine, or because it is foreign, like «هابيل» (Abel) and «قابيل» (Cain).

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتابِ: [nominative] by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), and «تنزيل» stands in the place of «منزّل» ("sent down") figuratively (ʿalā al-majāz). It is also possible that «تنزيل» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar (predicate) being مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: غافِرِ الذَّنْبِ وَقابِلِ التَّوْبِ شَدِيدِ الْعِقابِ: al-Farrāʾ said: I treated them like a naʿt (adjective) of a definite noun, though they are indefinite. Abū Isḥāq said: they are genitive as a badal (substitute). Abū Jaʿfar said: the precise statement on this and its summary is that غافر الذنب and قابل التوب may be definite, on the basis that they refer to the past, in which case they are naʿts; and they may refer to the future and the present, in which case they are indefinite, and on this basis they cannot be naʿts, but their genitive is by way of badal; and the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) is also permissible. As for شَدِيدِ الْعِقابِ, it is indefinite, so its genitive is by way of badal. «التواب» [Translator's note: so in the text; the word in the verse is «التَّوْب»] is the plural of «توبة» (repentance) or a maṣdar (verbal noun). Abū al-ʿAbbās said: what comes first to mind is that it is a maṣdar, that is, He accepts this act, just as you say «قال يقول قولا». If it is a plural, its meaning is: He accepts repentances. ذِي الطَّوْلِ: by way of badal because it is indefinite, and by way of naʿt because it is definite.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: ما يُجادِلُ فِي آياتِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: this is figurative (majāz), that is, in repelling the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. فَلا يَغْرُرْكَ تَقَلُّبُهُمْ فِي الْبِلادِ: Abū al-ʿAbbās said: that is, their free movement about, as it is said: «فلان يتقلب في ماله» ("so-and-so moves about freely in his wealth").

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ: [the verb is feminine] on the basis of the femininity of the group; that is, they denied the messengers. Abū al-ʿAbbās said: لِيُدْحِضُوا means "in order to make [it] slip away". From it is «مكان دحض», that is, a slippery place.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: He said: وَكَذلِكَ حَقَّتْ — it became binding and necessary, because it is taken from «الحقّ», since that is what is binding. أَنَّهُمْ: al-Akhfash said: that is, «لأنهم» and «بأنهم» ("because they" / "that they"). Abū Isḥāq said: «إنّهم» with kasra on the hamza is also permissible. أَصْحابُ النَّارِ: those punished in it.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: This is connected with the mention of the disbelievers because the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: those who carry the Throne and those around it declare Allah, Mighty and Majestic, free of what the disbelievers say. وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا, although He has forgiven them, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves that, so they are obedient to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by it. رَبَّنا وَسِعْتَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ رَحْمَةً وَعِلْماً: both are accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)). فَاغْفِرْ لِلَّذِينَ تابُوا وَاتَّبَعُوا سَبِيلَكَ: it is not permissible to assimilate the rāʾ into the lām, because the rāʾ has repetition (takrīr).

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: مَنْ is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the hāʾ and mīm in وَعَدْتَهُمْ, or to the hāʾ and mīm in أَدْخِلْهُمْ.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: He called the punishment "evil deeds" (sayyiʾāt) figuratively, because it is a punishment for evil deeds.

nahhas-irab:10-11.t: Al-Akhfash said: لَمَقْتُ — this is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), and it occurs after يُنادَوْنَ because its meaning is "it will be said to them", and calling out is a kind of saying. Others said: the meaning is: it will be said to them: Allah's loathing of you in the world, when you were called to faith and you disbelieved, is greater than your loathing of one another on the Day of Resurrection — because they were hostile to one another and loathed one another on the Day of Resurrection. Then at that they submitted and humbled themselves and sought to leave the Fire, and said: رَبَّنا أَمَتَّنَا اثْنَتَيْنِ وَأَحْيَيْتَنَا اثْنَتَيْنِ فَاعْتَرَفْنا بِذُنُوبِنا فَهَلْ إِلى خُرُوجٍ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ; and «من» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis (tawkīd).

nahhas-irab:12-13.t: ذلِكُمْ is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ), that is: the matter is that; that is, that punishment. بِأَنَّهُ إِذا دُعِيَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ كَفَرْتُمْ: that is, because when Allah was declared One, you disbelieved and denied; and if a polytheist associated partners with Him, you believed him and had faith in it. The hāʾ is an allusive pronoun referring to the situation (ḥadīth) [i.e. the pronoun of the matter]. فَالْحُكْمُ لِلَّهِ: that is, to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, alone, not to the idols you worship, الْعَلِيِّ الْكَبِيرِ.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: فادعوه: that is, for that reason call upon Him. مُخْلِصِينَ is [accusative] as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: رَفِيعُ الدَّرَجاتِ ذُو الْعَرْشِ: [nominative] by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). Al-Akhfash said: its accusative as praise (madḥ) is permissible. Al-Ḥasan read «لتنذر يوم التلاق» ("that you may warn of the Day of Meeting"), and this is an address to the Prophet ﷺ. Abū ʿUbayd interpreted the reading of whoever read «لينذر» with yāʾ as meaning: that Allah may warn. Abū Isḥāq said: the better [view] is that it refers to the Prophet ﷺ, because he is nearer. The yāʾ was omitted from «التلاق» because it is the end of a verse.

nahhas-irab:16-17.t: يَوْمَ هُمْ بارِزُونَ: هُمْ is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and بارِزُونَ is its khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), and that is why the tanwīn was dropped from «يوم». According to Sībawayh this happens only when the adverb has the meaning of «إذ» ("when", past): you say «لقيتك يوم زيد أمير» ("I met you on the day Zayd was a governor"); but if it has the meaning of «إذا» ("when", future), it is not permissible, as in «أنا ألقاك يوم زيد أمير». [Translator's note: the text reads «إذا كان كان الظرف», with «كان» repeated.] لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ الْواحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ: the soundest thing said about it is what Abū Wāʾil reported from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: people will be gathered on a white land like silver, upon which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not been disobeyed, and a caller will be commanded to call out: "Whose is the dominion today?" This is a clear view. As for [the view] that this is while creation does not exist, that is far-fetched, because there would be no benefit in it. The first view is authentic from Ibn Masʿūd, and it is not among the things that are arrived at by analogy (qiyās) or interpretation. The meaning according to his view is: a caller will call out on the Day of Resurrection, to make people acknowledge, "Whose is the dominion today?" and the servants, believers and disbelievers alike, will say: "Allah's, the One, the Subduer." The believers will say this out of joy and delight, and the disbelievers will say it in spite of themselves, in submission and humility.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: إِذِ الْقُلُوبُ لَدَى الْحَناجِرِ كاظِمِينَ: كاظمين is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), construed according to the meaning. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is: when the hearts of the people are at the throats, in the state of their suppressing [their grief]. Al-Farrāʾ permitted the implied form to be: "and warn them, suppressing [grief]", on the basis that it is the khabar of «القلوب»; and he said: because the meaning is «إذ هم كاظمين» ("when they are suppressing"). Al-Kisāʾī said: the nominative «كاظمون» is permissible, as a mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: so in the text: «على الابتداء»]. ما لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ: that is, a close relative; وَلا شَفِيعٍ يُطاعُ: [يُطاعُ] is a naʿt (adjective) of «شفيع», that is, nor an intercessor who asks and is answered.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: يَعْلَمُ خائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ: Abū Isḥāq said: that is, one who looks with the intention of betrayal. Al-Farrāʾ said: يعلم خائنة الأعين is the second glance, وَما تُخْفِي الصُّدُورُ is the first glance.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ: «هو» is a redundant separating pronoun (fāṣila); it is also possible that it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with what follows it as its khabar (predicate), and the clause as the khabar of «إنّ».

nahhas-irab:21-22.t: أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا: [فَيَنْظُرُوا] is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يسيروا, in the position of the jussive (jazm); it may also be in the position of the accusative, as an answer [to the question]; the jussive and the accusative are the same [in form] in the dual and the plural. كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ: [عاقِبَةُ] is the noun of «كان», and the khabar is in «كيف». واقٍ is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the wording; it may also be in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the position; its nominative and genitive are the same, because the yāʾ is dropped and the kasra remains to indicate it.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: On His saying, Mighty and Majestic: وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى تِسْعَ آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ [al-Isrāʾ: 101] [Translator's note: so in the text; the verse here (40:23) is «وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا مُوسى بِآياتِنا وَسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ»]. «وسلطان مبين»: «السلطان» is the proof, and it is treated as masculine and as feminine.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَهامانَ وَقارُونَ: foreign names, diptotes (not declined), and they are definite; if you make them indefinite they become declined. فَقالُوا ساحِرٌ كَذَّابٌ: nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, "he is a sorcerer".

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: قالُوا اقْتُلُوا أَبْناءَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ: [أَبْناءَ] is the plural of «ابن» according to the original form, the original being «بني». Qatāda said: this is the second killing; so according to his view it was a punishment for them. The first killing was because Pharaoh was told: "A child will be born among the Children of Israel at whose hands your kingdom will come to an end," so he ordered their sons to be killed and their women to be spared; then the second killing was a punishment for them, so that people would refrain from faith. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ما كَيْدُ الْكافِرِينَ إِلَّا فِي ضَلالٍ, that is, people do not refrain from faith even if the like of this is done to them, so how it goes for nothing!

nahhas-irab:26-27.t: أَقْتُلْ is jussive because it is the answer to the command; وَلْيَدْعُ is jussive because it is a command; and ذَرُونِي is not jussive, even though it is a command, but its form is the form of the jussive, and it is indeclinable (mabnī). It is said: this indicates that Pharaoh was told: "We fear that we may call upon [Moses' Lord] against you and be answered," so he said: وَلْيَدْعُ رَبَّهُ. إِنِّي أَخافُ أَنْ يُبَدِّلَ دِينَكُمْ أَوْ أَنْ يُظْهِرَ فِي الْأَرْضِ الْفَسادَ: this is the reading of the Medinans, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū ʿAmr; and the reading of the Kufans is أَوْ أَنْ يُظْهِرَ فِي الْأَرْضِ الْفَسادَ, and likewise in the codices of the Kufans «أو» with an alif. [Translator's note: the two readings are printed identically here; the reading of the Medinans and those with them is «وأن يَظهر … الفسادُ» (with wāw), and that of the Kufans «أو أن يُظهر … الفسادَ».] Abū ʿUbayd inclines to it; he said: because «أو» may have the meaning of wāw, because in that is the nullification of meanings [Translator's note: so in the text; the sentence appears to be corrupt — the sense of the reply that follows is that «أو» does not have the meaning of wāw, since that would nullify the distinction of meanings]. And if it were permissible for it to have the meaning of wāw, this would not be needed here, because the meaning of the wāw is: I fear both matters together, and the meaning of «أو» is: one of the two matters, that is, I fear that he will change your religion, and if that is beyond him, he will spread corruption in the land.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: أَنْ يَقُولَ رَبِّيَ اللَّهُ is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), that is, "for saying". وَإِنْ يَكُ كاذِباً فَعَلَيْهِ كَذِبُهُ: had it been «يكن» it would have been permissible; but the nūn was dropped because of frequency of use, according to Sībawayh's view, and because it is the nūn of the inflection (iʿrāb), according to the view of Abū al-ʿAbbās.

nahhas-irab:29-30.t: ظاهِرِينَ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). We have already mentioned what comes after it. مِثْلَ يَوْمِ الْأَحْزابِ: He means by it those who were destroyed, and Allah knows best.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: مِثْلَ دَأْبِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ: by way of badal (substitute). وَعادٍ وَثَمُودَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ: ثمود is not declined (a diptote) because it is the name of the tribe; declining it is permissible on the basis that it is the name of the clan (ḥayy). وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ is in the position of the genitive by conjunction (nasaq).

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: The reading of al-Ḍaḥḥāk is يَوْمَ التَّنادِ with a doubled [dāl] («التنادّ»), and it has been reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, except that it is from the transmission of al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ. Abū Jaʿfar said: it is said «ندّ البعير يندّ» when the camel bolts from something it sees, then that is used metaphorically for other than the camel. In this reading there is a combination of two quiescent letters, but it is permissible.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ مُدْبِرِينَ: by way of badal (substitute) from يَوْمَ التَّنادِ. مُدْبِرِينَ is a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَما لَهُ مِنْ هادٍ: [هادٍ] is in the position of the genitive by «من», and «من» with what follows it is in the position of the nominative; the nominative and the genitive of «هاد» are the same [in form].

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: وَلَقَدْ جاءَكُمْ يُوسُفُ مِنْ قَبْلُ بِالْبَيِّناتِ: before Moses — may Allah bless them both. Wahb ibn Munabbih mentioned that the Pharaoh of Moses was the Pharaoh of Joseph ﷺ, having lived a long life; and others say: he was another one. There is no evidence in this verse that it was the same one, because when he brought the clear proofs, they were for those with him and for those after him; he brought them to all of them, and it was incumbent upon them to believe him on account of them. كَذلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ مُرْتابٌ.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
الَّذِينَ يُجادِلُونَ is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from «من»; it may also be in the position of the nominative, with the meaning "they are those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah", or as a mubtadaʾ (subject). مَقْتاً is by way of clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)), that is, their disputing is grievous as loathing. كَذلِكَ يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ قَلْبِ مُتَكَبِّرٍ جَبَّارٍ: the reading of Abū ʿAmr is عَلى كُلِّ قَلْبِ مُتَكَبِّرٍ جَبَّارٍ with tanwīn [i.e. «قلبٍ»]. Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq said:
the annexation (iḍāfa) is preferable, because the arrogant one is the person; but one may say «قلب متكبر» ("an arrogant heart"), meaning by it the person.

nahhas-irab:36-37.t: أَسْبابَ السَّماواتِ is a badal (substitute) from «الأسباب». فَأَطَّلِعَ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أَبْلُغُ [Translator's note: on this analysis the verb is nominative, «فأطّلعُ»]; and al-Aʿraj read «فأطّلعَ» in the accusative. Abū ʿUbayd said: as the answer. Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning of the accusative differs from the meaning of the nominative, because the meaning of the accusative is: whenever I reach the means, I will look; and the meaning of the nominative is: perhaps I will reach the means, then perhaps I will look after that — except that «ثم» indicates a greater interval than the fāʾ. وَكَذلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِفِرْعَوْنَ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ وَصُدَّ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ: the reading of the Kufans is «وصُدّ» (passive); and on this reading «وصِدّ» is permissible, with the kasra of the dāl transferred onto the ṣād; and the reading of Ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakra is «وصدٌّ عن السبيل». [Translator's note: the vowels distinguishing these readings are not marked in the text; they have been supplied according to the sense of the discussion.]

nahhas-irab:38-42.t: The reading of Muʿādh is أَهْدِكُمْ سَبِيلَ الرَّشادِ [Translator's note: the variant is not distinguishable in the text as printed; the reading attributed to Muʿādh is «الرَّشّاد» with a doubled shīn]. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned it.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
لَيْسَ لَهُ دَعْوَةٌ: Abū Isḥāq said: that is, it has no answering of a call that would be of benefit. Others said:
it has no claim (daʿwa) that would establish divinity for it, in this world or in the Hereafter.

nahhas-irab:44-45.t: فَسَتَذْكُرُونَ ما أَقُولُ لَكُمْ: that is, in the Hereafter. وَأُفَوِّضُ أَمْرِي إِلَى اللَّهِ: it is said: this indicates that they wanted to kill him. Al-Kisāʾī said: one says «حاق يحيق حيقا وحيوقا» when [something] descends and clings.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: النَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْها: there are six aspects (awjuh) in it: «النار» may be a badal (substitute) from «سوء»; it may be in the sense of "it is the Fire"; it may be [nominative] as a mubtadaʾ (subject); and al-Farrāʾ said: it may be nominative by the returning pronoun (al-ʿāʾid). These are four aspects. Al-Farrāʾ permitted the accusative, because after it there is a returning pronoun and before it there is something it connects with; and al-Akhfash permitted the genitive, as a badal from «العذاب». Some of the philologists argued for establishing the punishment of the grave from His saying, Mighty and Majestic: النَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْها غُدُوًّا وَعَشِيًّا; he said: this is in this world [i.e. before the Resurrection]. In the ḥadīth from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: «The souls of the family of Pharaoh, and of those disbelievers who were like them, are exposed to the Fire morning and evening, and it is said: "This is your abode."» And in the ḥadīth of Ṣakhr ibn Juwayriya from Nāfiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «When the disbeliever dies, he is exposed to the Fire morning and evening» — then he recited النَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْها غُدُوًّا وَعَشِيًّا — «and when the believer dies, his soul is exposed to Paradise morning and evening». Al-Farrāʾ said: in the morning and evening, that is, in the measures of those [times] in this world. Abū Jaʿfar said: «غدوّ» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) made into an adverb by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa). وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ: you make «يوما» accusative by His saying أَدْخِلُوا. The reading of al-Ḥasan, Abū al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim is «ادخلوا آل فرعون أشد العذاب» ("Enter, O family of Pharaoh, the severest punishment"): in this reading you make «آل فرعون» accusative as an annexed vocative (munādā muḍāf). Whoever reads «أدخلوا آل فرعون» ("Make the family of Pharaoh enter") makes them accusative because the verb falls upon them [as its object]. وآلَ فِرْعَوْنَ are those who were upon his religion and his way; and if those who were upon his religion and his way are in the severest punishment, he himself is nearer to that. Qatāda reported from Abū Ḥassān al-Aʿraj from Nājiya ibn Kaʿb from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd from the Prophet ﷺ: «A servant is born a believer, lives a believer and dies a believer — among them is Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace: he was born a believer, lived a believer and died a believer. And a servant is born a disbeliever, lives a disbeliever and dies a disbeliever — among them is Pharaoh: he was born a disbeliever, lived a disbeliever and died a disbeliever».

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: فَيَقُولُ الضُّعَفاءُ لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا إِنَّا كُنَّا لَكُمْ تَبَعاً: [تَبَعاً] is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and that is why it is not pluralised; if it were pluralised, «أتباع» would be said.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: قالَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا إِنَّا كُلٌّ فِيها: al-Akhfash said: «كل» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī permitted «إنّا كلا فيها» in the accusative as a naʿt (adjective). Abū Jaʿfar said: this is among the gravest of errors — that a pronoun should be given a naʿt; and moreover «كلّا» neither takes a naʿt nor serves as one. This is Sībawayh's view verbatim. And more than this: it is not permissible to make a badal (substitute) from the pronoun here, because it is a speaker [Translator's note: the text reads «مخاطب» ("addressee")], and no badal is made from the addressee or the speaker [Translator's note: the text reads «ولا المخاطب», apparently for «المتكلّم»], because they are not ambiguous so as to need a badal. This is the view of Muḥammad ibn Yazīd verbatim. إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ حَكَمَ بَيْنَ الْعِبادِ: that is, He has judged between them that He will not take anyone to task for the sin of another.

nahhas-irab:49-50.t: الَّذِينَ is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ). Some of the Arabs say «اللذون», on the basis that it is a sound plural that is declinable; and whoever says «الذين» in the position of the nominative treats it as indeclinable (mabnī), just as it was indeclinable in the singular. Saʿīd al-Akhfash said: the nūn was joined to «الذي», so it resembled «خمسة عشر» (fifteen) and was made indeclinable on fatḥa. «خزنة» is the plural of «خازن» (keeper); one also says «خزّان» and «خزّن». ادْعُوا رَبَّكُمْ يُخَفِّفْ: [يُخَفِّفْ] is a jussive answer; and when it is with the fāʾ it is accusative, except that what is most frequent in the speech of the Arabs after the command and what resembles it is that it be without the fāʾ; on this basis the Qurʾān came in the most eloquent of usages, as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 394- قفا نبك من ذكرى حبيب ومنزل ("Halt, you two, let us weep at the memory of a beloved and an abode"). And in the ḥadīth from Abū al-Dardāʾ, he said: «Hunger will be cast upon the people of the Fire until it equals the punishment they are in, and they will cry for help from it, and they will be helped with ḍarīʿ, which neither nourishes nor avails against hunger; they will eat, and it will avail them nothing. Then they will cry for help, and they will be helped with food that chokes, and they will choke on it. Then they will remember that in the world they used to wash down choking with water, so they will cry for drink, and the boiling water will be raised to them with hooks; when it comes near their faces it will scorch them, and when it enters their bellies it will cut up their intestines and what is in their bellies. Then they will cry for help to the angels, saying: «ادعوا ربكم يخفّف عنا يوما من العذاب», and they will answer them: أَوَلَمْ تَكُ تَأْتِيكُمْ رُسُلُكُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ قالُوا بَلى قالُوا فَادْعُوا وَما دُعاءُ الْكافِرِينَ إِلَّا فِي ضَلالٍ».

nahhas-irab:51-53.t:
إِنَّا لَنَنْصُرُ رُسُلَنا: dropping the ḍamma because of its heaviness is permissible, so that one says «رسْلنا». وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا is in the position of the accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الرسل». In the ḥadīth from Abū al-Dardāʾ — and some of the ḥadīth transmitters say: from the Prophet ﷺ — he said: «Whoever defends the honour of his Muslim brother, it is a right upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to ward off from him the fire of Hell» — then he recited إِنَّا لَنَنْصُرُ رُسُلَنا وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا. And Sahl ibn Muʿādh ibn Anas reported from his father that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Whoever protects a believer from a hypocrite who backbites him, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will send an angel to protect his flesh from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection; and whoever mentions a Muslim with something in order to disgrace him by it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will make him stand on the bridge over Hell until he comes out of what he said». وَيَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْأَشْهادُ: Sufyān al-Thawrī said: I asked al-Aʿmash about «الأشهاد», and he said: the angels, may Allah bless them and grant them peace. Zayd ibn Aslam said: «الأشهاد» are the angels, the prophets, the believers and the bodies. Abū Isḥāq said:
«الأشهاد» is the plural of «شاهد», like «صاحب» and «أصحاب». Abū Jaʿfar said: it is not the pattern of fāʿil to be pluralised on afʿāl, and no analogy is made on it; but what has come of it by hearing (masmūʿ) is reproduced as it was heard, and it is on the basis of dropping the augment. Al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ permitted «ويوم تقوم الأشهاد» with tāʾ, on the basis of the femininity of the group.
Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read «لا تنفع الظالمين معذرتهم» (with tāʾ). One of the philologists said: it would have been more fitting for him to read «ويوم تقوم الأشهاد», because the verb is immediately followed by the nouns, and to read لا يَنْفَعُ الظَّالِمِينَ with yāʾ, because [something] has intervened between the verb and the noun. Abū Jaʿfar said: this does not necessarily follow, because the singular of «الأشهاد» is «شاهد», which is masculine, so making the whole masculine is good in their case; and «معذرة» is feminine in form, so making it feminine is good.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: هُدىً is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), except that the inflection does not show in it, because it is a maqṣūr noun (ending in alif). [Translator's note: the text reads «يتبيّن» ("shows"), apparently for «لا يتبيّن».] وَذِكْرى is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it, and both are accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ بِالْعَشِيِّ وَالْإِبْكارِ: [الإبكار] is a maṣdar (verbal noun) made into an adverb by extension; and «الأبكار» is the plural of «بكر» (early morning).

nahhas-irab:56-56.t:
Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is: those who dispute concerning the repelling of the signs of Allah and His decree — like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82] [i.e. with an omitted muḍāf]. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: بِغَيْرِ سُلْطانٍ means without a proof. «السلطان» is treated as masculine and as feminine; and had it been «بغير سلطان أتتهم» (with the feminine verb), it would have been permissible. أَتاهُمْ is a naʿt (adjective) of «سلطان», and it is in the position of the genitive. إِنْ فِي صُدُورِهِمْ إِلَّا كِبْرٌ ما هُمْ بِبالِغِيهِ: Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is:
there is nothing in their breasts but a pride whereby they will not attain their desire; so he construed it as involving an omission. Others said:
the meaning is: [they will not] attain the greatness, without any omission, because these were people who saw that if they followed the Prophet ﷺ their eminence would diminish and their circumstances would decline, and that they would rise if they were not followers; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that they would not attain the eminence they hoped for by denial. فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ: that is, from their evil.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t:
لَخَلْقُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). This is the lām of emphasis (tawkīd), and its proper place is at the beginning of the sentence, because it emphasises the whole clause, except that it is shifted from its place (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). Thus said Sībawayh: you say:
«إن عمرا لخارج» ("ʿAmr is indeed going out"); it is only moved back from its place so that it is not combined with «إنّ», because both convey a single meaning; likewise «إنّ» and «أنّ» are not combined according to the Basrans. Hishām permitted «إنّ أنّ زيدا منطلق حقّ» ("That Zayd is departing is indeed true"); but if you omit «حقّ», it is not permissible according to any grammarian I know of. Among cases where the lām enters the khabar is His saying, Mighty and Majestic, after this: إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ لَآتِيَةٌ لا رَيْبَ فِيها.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: ادْعُونِي is an imperative, not declinable and not jussive according to the Basrans unless the lām is with it; and according to al-Farrāʾ it is jussive by an omitted lām. «أستجب» is jussive according to all, because it has the meaning of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). This hamza is a disjunctive hamza (hamzat qaṭʿ), because it is in the position of the nūn in «نفعل»; and the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) dropped because it was no longer needed.

nahhas-irab:61-63.t: جَعَلَ here has the meaning of «خلق» (created). The Arabs distinguish between «جعل» when it means «خلق» and «جعل» when it does not mean «خلق»: [in the first case] they make it transitive to only one object, and when it does not mean «خلق» they make it transitive to two objects, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: إِنَّا جَعَلْناهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيًّا [al-Zukhruf: 3]. وَالنَّهارَ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; مُبْصِراً is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:64-64.t: وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ: it is reported from Ibn Razīn as «فأحسن صِوَركم» with kasra on the ṣād. Sībawayh explained this and mentioned that the kasra is a neighbour of the ḍamma, because the Arabs say «رُكْبة» and «رُكُبات», and drop the ḍamma, saying «رُكْبات»; and likewise «هِنْد» and «هِنِدات», and they drop the kasra, saying «هِنْدات». So the ḍamma and the kasra are neighbours, and they pluralised fiʿla on fiʿal [as they did fuʿla on fuʿal] — «رِشوة» and «رِشى» — and thus, in his view, «صورة» and «صِوَر». This is among the finest and clearest statements in grammar. Its parallel is that they say «فَخِذ» and «فَخْذ», «عَضُد» and «عَضْد», dropping the kasra and the ḍamma, but they do not say «جَمْل» for «جَمَل», dropping the fatḥa, because of its lightness. And they say «سُورة» and «سُوَر» [Translator's note: the text reads «وسورة», apparently for «وسُوَر»], but for faʿla with a fatḥa on the first radical they say only fiʿāl, as in «جَفْنة» and «جِفان»; while for fiʿla, like fuʿla, they say fiʿal. Do you not see the kinship of fiʿla and fuʿla and the divergence of faʿla from both? [Translator's note: the text is unvowelled throughout this paragraph; the vowels of the patterns have been supplied according to the sense of Sībawayh's argument.]

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: مُخْلِصِينَ is a ḥāl (circumstantial). لَهُ الدِّينَ: [الدِّينَ is accusative] because the verb falls upon it [as its object]. The implied meaning is: say «الحمد لله ربّ العالمين» ("Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds").

nahhas-irab:67-70.t:
ثُمَّ لِتَكُونُوا شُيُوخاً: this is the plural of multitude (jamʿ al-kathra); one also says «شِيوخا» [with kasra], and for a small number «أشياخ». The original was «أشيخ», like «فلس» and «أفلس», except that a vowel on the yāʾ is heavy. The pattern faʿl used to be pluralised on afʿāl [even] when there was no yāʾ in it, by likening it to faʿal; they said «زند» and «أزناد». So when the vowel on the yāʾ was felt to be heavy, they likened faʿl to faʿal and said «شيخ» / «أشياخ». If a poet were compelled, he could say «أشيخ», like «عين» / «أعين», except that it is good in «عين» because it is feminine. «الشيخ» is one who has passed forty years.
وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُتَوَفَّى مِنْ قَبْلُ: Mujāhid said: that is, before he becomes old. Abū Jaʿfar said:
it is because of this omission that «قبل» has ḍamma, and we have already mentioned the reason for their choosing the ḍamma for it. Mujāhid said:
وَلِتَبْلُغُوا أَجَلًا مُسَمًّى: death, for all.

nahhas-irab:71-74.t:
إِذِ الْأَغْلالُ فِي أَعْناقِهِمْ وَالسَّلاسِلُ: [السَّلاسِلُ] is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الأغلال». Abū Ḥātim said: يُسْحَبُونَ is resumptive (mustaʾnaf) on this reading; others said: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form being: "when the shackles are on their necks, and the chains, being dragged". Abū al-Jawzāʾ reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read «والسلاسلَ» in the accusative, «يَسحبون» (active), and the implied meaning in his reading is: and they drag the chains. Abū Isḥāq said: whoever reads «والسلاسلِ» in the genitive, the meaning according to him is: and in the chains they are dragged, and in the boiling water and the chains. That is how it is in the book of Abū Isḥāq ("On the Qurʾān"), and what appears to me is that it is a mistake, because it is clear that he construes it as "they are dragged in the boiling water and the chains", so that «السلاسل» would be conjoined to «الحميم»; and this is an error: we know of no one who permits «مررت وزيد بعمرو» ("I passed — and Zayd — by ʿAmr"), and likewise with every genitive. They permitted that only with the nominative: they permitted «قام وزيد عمرو» ("ʿAmr — and Zayd — stood up"); it is far-fetched with the accusative, as in:
«رأيت وزيدا عمرا» ("I saw — and Zayd — ʿAmr"); and with the genitive it is not permissible, because the verb does not indicate it.

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: That is: that punishment of yours is because you used to rejoice in acts of disobedience. In one ḥadīth: "Had Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not punished [us] except for our rejoicing in acts of disobedience and their going smoothly for us [it would have been enough]." This is one interpretation. And it is said: their rejoicing in what they had was that they said to the messengers, peace be upon them: "We know that we will not be resurrected nor punished." Mujāhid said likewise regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic: فَلَمَّا جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ فَرِحُوا بِما عِنْدَهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ. He said: بِما كُنْتُمْ تَفْرَحُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ, that is, because you used to be insolent; وَبِما كُنْتُمْ تَمْرَحُونَ, that is, you used to be arrogantly exultant.

nahhas-irab:76-76.t: فَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ: [مثوى] is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ), that is, evil is the abode of the arrogant.

nahhas-irab:77-78.t: فَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ is in the position of the jussive (jazm) by the condition; «ما» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis (tawkīd), and so is the nūn; the jussive disappeared and the verb was made indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, because it is like two things one of which is joined to the other. أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. فَإِلَيْنا يُرْجَعُونَ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). مِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَصَصْنا عَلَيْكَ: «من» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and likewise وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ لَمْ نَقْصُصْ عَلَيْكَ.

nahhas-irab:79-80.t: اللَّهُ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَنْعامَ: Abū Isḥāq said: «الأنعام» here are camels. لِتَرْكَبُوا مِنْها وَمِنْها تَأْكُلُونَ: those who forbade eating horses and permitted eating camels argued that Allah the Exalted said about livestock وَمِنْها تَأْكُلُونَ, whereas He said about horses, mules and donkeys وَالْخَيْلَ وَالْبِغالَ وَالْحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوها [al-Naḥl: 8] and did not mention the permissibility of eating them.

nahhas-irab:81-81.t:
َيَّ آياتِ اللَّهِ تُنْكِرُونَ [Translator's note: the beginning of the quotation is cut off in the text; the verse reads «فَأَيَّ آياتِ اللَّهِ تُنْكِرُونَ».]
You make «أيّ» accusative by «تنكرون», because an interrogative is governed by what comes after it. Had there been a hāʾ [pronoun] with the verb, the nominative would have been preferred for «أيّ»; and had the interrogative been with the alif or with «هل», and after it a noun followed by a verb with a hāʾ, the accusative would have been preferred.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: كانُوا أَكْثَرَ مِنْهُمْ: [أَكْثَرَ] is the khabar (predicate) of «كان», and it is not declined (a diptote) because it is on the pattern afʿal. The Kufans claimed that everything that is not declined may be declined [in poetry], except «أفعل من كذا», which may not be declined in any way, in poetry or otherwise, when «من» is with it. Abū al-ʿAbbās said: if «من» were what prevented its declension, it would follow that you could not say «مررت بخيرٍ منك وشرٍّ من عمرو» ("I passed by someone better than you and worse than ʿAmr"). And how can what is not declined be declined while the causes preventing declension are in it? And if it is declined, what is the meaning of our saying "it is not declined because of such-and-such a cause"?

nahhas-irab:83-83.t: There are three views on its meaning. The view of Mujāhid: [it refers to] the disbelievers who rejoiced in the knowledge they had and said: "We know better than them; we will not be punished and we will not be resurrected." And it is said: the disbelievers rejoiced in the knowledge of this world that they had, as in يَعْلَمُونَ ظاهِراً مِنَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا [al-Rūm: 7]. And it is said: those who rejoiced were the messengers: when their peoples denied them, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed them that He would destroy the disbelievers and save them and the believers, so they rejoiced in the knowledge they had of the salvation of the believers; and there encompassed the disbelievers what they used to mock, that is, the punishment for their mocking what the messengers brought.

nahhas-irab:84-85.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنا قالُوا آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ ... سُنَّتَ اللَّهِ: [سُنَّتَ] is a maṣdar (verbal noun), that is, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, laid down as a practice regarding the disbelievers that faith does not benefit them when they see the punishment. وَخَسِرَ هُنالِكَ الْكافِرُونَ: Abū Isḥāq said: they had been losers before that, but the loss became clear to them when they saw the punishment.

nahhas-meani:1-2.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حـمۤ. تَنزِيلُ ٱلْكِتَابِ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْعَلِيمِ﴾ [verses 1 and 2].
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: ﴿حـمۤ﴾ is one of the names of the Qurʾān.
And it is said: the meaning of ﴿حـمۤ﴾ is: ḥumma al-amr (the matter has been decreed).
And in the narration of ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ﴿الۤر﴾, ﴿حـمۤ﴾ and ﴿نونْ﴾ are the letters of [the name] al-Raḥmān, Mighty and Majestic is He, separated.
And ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read ﴿حَامِيمَ تَنْزِيلَ﴾; and the meaning according to his reading is: "Recite Ḥāmīm"; he did not make it fully declinable (lam yaṣrifhu) because he made it a name of the sūra.
And it may be that it was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
And the meaning [on the usual reading] is: this is the sending down of the Book from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿غَافِرِ ٱلذَّنبِ وَقَابِلِ ٱلتَّوْبِ﴾.
And al-tawb may be the plural of tawba, as the poet said:
* "فَيَخْبُو سَاعَةً وَيَهُبُّ سَاعَا" *
(It dies down for an hour and blazes up for hours [sāʿ, plural of sāʿa].)
And al-tawb may be in the sense of al-tawba (repentance).
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿شَدِيدِ ٱلْعِقَابِ ذِي ٱلطَّوْلِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated: ﴿ذِي ٱلطَّوْلِ﴾: he said: possessor of wealth.
And Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: possessor of favour.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-ṭawl in the language is bounty and power; one says "So-and-so has ṭawl over So-and-so", and "O Allah, bestow (ṭul) Your mercy upon us."
And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿ذِي ٱلطَّوْلِ﴾: he said: possessor of abundance and wealth.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا يُجَادِلُ فِيۤ آيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَلاَ يَغْرُرْكَ تَقَلُّبُهُمْ فِي ٱلْبِلاَدِ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, let not their coming and going and their moving about in their journeys deceive you.
Abū Jaʿfar said: like it is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لا يَغُرَنَّكَ تَقَلُّبُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي البِلاَدِ. مَتَاعٌ قَلِيلٌ﴾.
And the meaning is: let not their safety and Allah's forbearance with them deceive you, for their outcome is blameworthy and their destination is the Fire.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
Then He made clear that this was the way of those before them, and said: ﴿كَـذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ وَٱلأَحْزَابُ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ﴾.
They are: Thamūd, ʿĀd, the people of Lūṭ, and whoever was like them.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهَمَّتْ كُـلُّ أُمَّةٍ بِرَسُولِهِمْ لِيَأْخُذُوهُ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: to seize him and kill him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and this is made clear by His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿فَأَخَذْتُهُمْ﴾, i.e. I destroyed them; and a captive is called akhīdh.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ أَصْحَابُ ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
That is, by His saying: ﴿لأَمْلأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الجِنَّةِ والنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: the punishment became due upon them because of their disbelief.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
Then He informed that the angels seek forgiveness only for the believers, and said: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ ٱلْعَرْشَ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهُ، يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ وَيُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ، وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ، رَبَّنَا وَسِعْتَ كُـلَّ شَيْءٍ رَّحْمَةً وَعِلْماً، فَٱغْفِرْ لِلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ سَبِيلَكَ، وَقِهِمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْجَحِيمِ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: ﴿فَٱغْفِرْ لِلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ سَبِيلَكَ﴾: he said: they repented of associating partners [with Allah] and followed obedience to You.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَبَّنَا وَأَدْخِلْهُمْ جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ ٱلَّتِي وَعَدْتَّهُمْ﴾.
It is narrated that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to Kaʿb al-Aḥbār: What are the gardens of ʿAdn? He said: palaces of gold in the Garden, which the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the just leaders will enter.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-ʿadn in the language is residing; ʿadana bi-l-makān means he resided in the place.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقِهِمُ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ وَمَن تَقِ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَقَدْ رَحِمْتَهُ﴾.
﴿وَقِهِمُ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ﴾: Qatāda said: that is, the punishment; ﴿وَمَن تَقِ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَقَدْ رَحِمْتَهُ﴾: he said: the punishment.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يُنَادَوْنَ لَمَقْتُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ مِن مَّقْتِكُمْ أَنفُسَكُـمْ إِذْ تُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلإِيمَانِ فَتَكْفُرُونَ﴾.
There is fronting and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in the speech, and the exegetes have explained it.
Al-Ḥasan said: they are given their record, and when they look at their evil deeds, they loathe themselves; so they are called out to: "Allah's loathing of you in the world, when you were called to faith and disbelieved, is greater than your loathing of yourselves today."
And Mujāhid said: when they behold their evil deeds, they loathe themselves, and they are called out to: "Allah's loathing of you, when you were called to faith, is greater than your loathing of yourselves when you beheld the Fire."

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ أَمَتَّنَا ٱثْنَتَيْنِ وَأَحْيَيْتَنَا ٱثْنَتَيْنِ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq narrated from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: it is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ أَمْوَاتاً فَأَحْيَاكُمْ، ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning of ﴿أَمَتَّنَا ٱثْنَتَيْنِ﴾ on this [view] is: You created us dead, i.e. as drops of fluid, then You gave us life, then You caused us to die, then You gave us life for the resurrection.
And it is said: one of the two lives and one of the two deaths are the bringing to life in the grave and then the death [that follows], and they did not mean their life in the Hereafter.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكُم بِأَنَّهُ إِذَا دُعِيَ ٱللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ كَـفَرْتُمْ﴾.
That is, you denied; ﴿وَإِن يُشْرَكْ بِهِ تُؤْمِنُواْ﴾, i.e. you believe [it] true.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُلْقِي ٱلرُّوحَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ﴾.
ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿الرُّوحُ﴾ is prophethood.
And Ibn [Abī] Najīḥ [Translator's note: the text has «ابن نجيح»] narrated from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿الرُّوحُ﴾ is revelation.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: ﴿يلقي الرُّوحَ﴾: he said: revelation and mercy.
Abū Jaʿfar said: He casts the revelation upon whomever He singles out among His servants; and revelation is called "spirit" (rūḥ) because people live by it, i.e. are guided [by it]; the guided one is alive and the one astray is dead, by way of figurative representation; and from this it is said to one who does not understand: "You are nothing but dead"; and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿فَإنَّكَ لاَ تُسْمِعُ المَوْتَى﴾.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيُنذِرَ يَوْمَ ٱلتَّلاَقِ يَوْمَ هُم بَارِزُونَ﴾.
That is: so that the one to whom revelation is given may warn.
And the meaning may be: so that Allah may warn of the Day of Meeting.
Qatāda said: that is, the day on which the people of heaven and the people of earth meet, and the first and the last meet.
﴿يَوْمَ هُم بَارِزُونَ﴾: Qatāda said: that is, no mountain or anything else will screen them.
That is [Translator's note: this belongs to the next verse, ﴿لِّمَنِ ٱلْمُلْكُ ٱلْيَوْمَ﴾], this will be said.
Abū Wāʾil narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: (People will be gathered on a white land like silver, on which Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has never been disobeyed. The first thing to be said is: ﴿لِّمَنِ ٱلْمُلْكُ ٱلْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ ٱلْوَاحِدِ ٱلْقَهَّارِ﴾. Then the first of the disputes to be examined concern blood: the killer and the slain are brought, and [the slain] says: Ask this one why he killed me. If he says: I killed him so that might would belong to So-and-so, it is said to the slain: Kill him as he killed you. And likewise if he killed a group, he is made to taste killing as he made them taste it in the world. He said: ﴿لاَ ظُلْمَ اليَوْمَ إنَّ اللهَ سَرِيعُ الحِسَاب﴾.)

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنذِرْهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلأَزِفَةِ إِذِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ لَدَى ٱلْحَنَاجِرِ كَاظِمِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: that is, the Resurrection.
Al-Kisāʾī said: one says azifa al-shayʾu yaʾzafu, i.e. [it drew near and approached].
Abū Jaʿfar said: the Resurrection was called al-āzifa because of its nearness, even if it seems far to people; and from this one says: "So-and-so's departure has drawn near (azifa)."
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ لَدَى ٱلْحَنَاجِرِ كَاظِمِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: they rose up from their breasts and stuck in their throats, neither coming out nor going back.
And someone else said: their hearts were dislodged by terror, and neither came out so that they might find relief, nor went back.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿كَاظِمِينَ﴾, i.e. filled with rage, with nothing to remove their rage; one says kaẓama al-baʿīru bi-jirratihi when the camel keeps its cud turning in its throat, and kaẓama ghayẓahu when he restrained his rage.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ وَلاَ شَفِيعٍ يُطَاعُ﴾.
That is, they have no intercessor who is obeyed.
Al-Ḥasan said: take many believing friends, for a man among them will intercede for his relative and his friend; and when the disbelievers see that, they say: ﴿فَمَا لَنَا مِنْ شافِعِينَ. وَلاَ صَدِيقٍ حَمِيمٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَعْلَمُ خَآئِنَةَ ٱلأَعْيُنِ وَمَا تُخْفِي ٱلصُّدُورُ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: it is the man who looks at a woman; when his companions look at him he lowers his gaze, and when he sees them inattentive he steals a look, and when they look at him he lowers his gaze; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, knows of him that he would love to look at her private parts.
And Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the sudden glance, and he commanded me to lower my gaze."

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآثَاراً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: it is their walking and their leaving marks in the land.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ بِآيَاتِنَا وَسُلْطَانٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾.
﴿بِآيَاتِنَا﴾, i.e. with the signs that indicate his messengership, such as the staff and the like.
﴿وَسُلْطَانٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾, i.e. and a clarifying proof.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t: Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that they rejected the signs, which created beings are incapable of [producing], by saying: a lying sorcerer — ﴿فَقَالُواْ سَاحِرٌ كَـذَّابٌ﴾.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ بِٱلْحَقِّ مِنْ عِندِنَا قَالُواْ ٱقْتُلُوۤاْ أَبْنَآءَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مَعَهُ وَٱسْتَحْيُواْ نِسَآءَهُمْ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: this was after the first killing.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And the meaning of: ﴿إِنِّيۤ أَخَافُ أَن يُبَدِّلَ دِينَكُـمْ أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: I fear that one of the two things will happen: either he will do away with your religion altogether, or he will win [people] over, and so cause corruption against you and wage war on you.
And it is read ﴿وأَنْ يُظْهِرَ فِي الأَرْضِ الفَسَاد﴾, i.e. I fear both things together.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مُّؤْمِنٌ مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إِيمَانَهُ﴾.
The meaning may be: "And a believing man, concealing his faith from the family of Pharaoh, said", by way of fronting and postponing.
And the meaning may be: "And a believing man of the family of Pharaoh, concealing his faith, said: ﴿أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلاً أَنْ يَقُولَ رَبِّيَ اللهُ﴾?", i.e. because he says.
﴿وَإِن يَكُ كَاذِباً فَعَلَيْهِ كَذِبُهُ﴾, i.e. nothing from him will harm you.
This is a difficult verse [Translator's note: the difficulty concerns the continuation ﴿وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقاً يُصِبْكُمْ بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِي يَعِدُكُمْ﴾], because everything a prophet promises comes to pass, so is this not a place for "all"?
There are several answers to it:
a- Among them: that "baʿḍ" (some) is in the sense of "kull" (all); this is the position of Abū ʿUbayda, and he recited:
* "أَوْ يَرْتَبِطْ بَعْضَ النُّفُوسِ حِمَامُهَا" *
(…or until its fated death seizes some soul.)
And this is a view to be avoided, because it entails the nullification of clear expression.
b- Abū Isḥāq said: in this there is binding the opponent in debate by the argument, by saying: "Do you see, if some of what I threaten you with befalls you, will it not mean your destruction?"
So the meaning is: if nothing but some of what Mūsā promised you befalls you, you will perish. He said: and like it is the poet's saying:
قَدْ يُدْرِكُ المُتَأَنِّي بَعْضَ حَاجَتِهِ * وَقَدْ يَكُونُ مَع المُسْتَعْجِلِ الزَّلَلُ
(The patient one may attain some of his need, and with the hasty one there may be slipping.)
That is: the least of the patient man's states is that he attains some of his need.
c- And it is said: there is no negation of the whole in His saying ﴿يُصِبْكُمْ بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِي يَعِدُكُمْ﴾.
d- And it is said: the prophets, may Allah bless them, pray against their peoples, saying: O Allah, make the earth swallow them; O Allah, destroy them — in various kinds of supplication — and some of that befalls them.
e- And there is a fifth answer in the verse: that Mūsā ﷺ promised them a hastened punishment in this world if they disbelieved, and the punishment of the Hereafter; and only what he promised them in this world reaches them in it, while the punishment of the Hereafter is deferred; so on this [view] some of what he promises them befalls them.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يَهْدِي مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ كَذَّابٌ﴾.
That is, a disbeliever.
And Qatāda said: that is, he transgressed against himself by associating partners [with Allah].
And al-Suddī said: he is the one who sheds blood.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ مَآ أُرِيكُمْ إِلاَّ مَآ أَرَىٰ وَمَآ أَهْدِيكُمْ إِلاَّ سَبِيلَ ٱلرَّشَادِ﴾.
It is narrated of Muʿādh ibn Jabal that he read ﴿سَبِيلَ الرَّشَّادِ﴾ with doubling of the shīn, and said: the path of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is, according to most linguists of Arabic, a solecism (laḥn), because one only says arshada yurshidu, and "faʿʿāl" is not formed from "afʿala"; it is formed only from the triliteral; and if you intend intensiveness from the quadriliteral, you say "mifʿāl".
Abū Jaʿfar said: it may be that ﴿رَشَّادٌ﴾ is in the sense of yurshidu (one who guides), not as being derived from it, but as one says laʾʾāl (pearl-seller) from luʾluʾ: it has its meaning but is not formed regularly from it.
And it may be that rashshād is from rashada, yarshudu, i.e. one possessing right guidance, as the poet said:
* "كِلينِي لِهَمٍّ يَا أُمَيْمَةُ نَاصِبِ" *
(Leave me, O Umayma, to a tormenting care [nāṣib, i.e. "possessing torment"].)

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِيۤ آمَنَ يٰقَوْمِ إِنِّيۤ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ مِّثْلَ يَوْمِ ٱلأَحْزَابِ﴾.
Qatāda said: they are the people of Nūḥ, ʿĀd and Thamūd.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيٰقَوْمِ إِنِّيۤ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلتَّنَادِ﴾.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk read: ﴿يَوْمَ التَّنَادِّ﴾ with doubling of the dāl.
The grammarians said: this is a solecism, because it is from nadda, yaniddu, when one goes off headlong in flight, as the poet said:
وَبَرْكٍ هُجُودٍ قَدْ أَثَارَتْ مَخَافَتِي * نَوَادِيَهَا أَسْعَى بِعَضْبٍ مُجَرَّدِ
(Many a herd of kneeling camels asleep, whose strays my dreaded approach has stirred, as I go with a drawn sharp sword.)
He said: and this has no meaning regarding the Resurrection.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a mistake, and the reading with it is good. Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khālid, who said: (On the Day of Resurrection a neck of fire will appear to people, and they will turn in flight from it until it surrounds them; and when it has surrounded them, they will say: Where is the escape? Then they will start weeping until the tears run out, and it becomes blood; then the eyes of the disbelievers will stare fixedly, and that is His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ مُقْنِعِي رُءُوسِهِمْ لاَ يَرْتَدُّ إلَيْهِمْ طَرْفُهُمْ﴾.)
And it is narrated that when they are ordered to the Fire, they turn in flight from it.
And if there were nothing to argue for the reading except His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ مُدْبِرِينَ مَا لَكُمْ مِنَ اللهِ مِنْ عَاصِمٍ﴾, it would suffice.
As for the meaning without doubling: Qatāda said concerning His saying ﴿إنِّيۤ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلتَّنَادِ﴾:
He said: the day on which every people is called by their deeds, and the people of the Garden call out to the people of the Fire.
And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khālid said: (When people are gathered on the Day of Resurrection, they call out to one another, until a neck of fire appears to them, and they turn in flight.)

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
Then He the Exalted said: ﴿مَا لَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِنْ عَاصِمٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, of any helper.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَآءَكُـمْ يُوسُفُ مِن قَبْلُ بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾.
That is, before Mūsā; ﴿بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾, i.e. with the miraculous signs.
﴿فَمَا زِلْتُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِّمَّا جَآءَكُـمْ بِهِ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا هَلَكَ قُلْتُمْ لَن يَبْعَثَ ٱللَّهُ مِن بَعْدِهِ رَسُولاً﴾.
That is: you thought that the proof would not be established against you after him. ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ مُّرْتَابٌ﴾, i.e. with the like of this going astray, Allah sends astray one who is a transgressor and a doubter.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِيۤ آيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ سُلْطَانٍ أَتَاهُمْ﴾.
[It is] as a badal (substitute) for ﴿مَنْ﴾.
And the meaning of ﴿كَبُرَ مَقْتاً﴾ is: the disputing is greatly hateful.
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ﴿عَلَى قَلْبِ كُلِّ مُتَكَبِّرٍ جَبَّارٍ﴾.
And the meaning of this reading is like the meaning of the first, as one says: "I speak to So-and-so on the day of every Friday" and "every Friday-day."
As for the tanwīn [i.e. «قَلْبٍ مُتَكَبِّرٍ»], one says "an arrogant heart", i.e. its owner is arrogant.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ فَرْعَوْنُ يٰهَامَانُ ٱبْنِ لِي صَرْحاً﴾.
That is, a palace; and every great building is a ṣarḥ.
﴿لَّعَـلِّيۤ أَبْلُغُ ٱلأَسْبَابَ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, the gates.
And al-sabab in the language is what leads to a thing; so the meaning is: so that I may reach what leads to the heavens.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَـذَلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِفِرْعَوْنَ سُوۤءُ عَمَلِهِ وَصُدَّ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾.
And it is read ﴿وصُدَّ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾, and this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd.
And it is narrated from Ibn Abī Isḥāq: ﴿وصَدَّ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the best of them is ﴿وصَدَّ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾, as He the Exalted said: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللهِ﴾.
And Abū ʿUbayd's statement in his choice is nothing, because for whoever reads it with ḍamma, the meaning according to him — as Abū Ḥātim mentioned — is: "and Satan turned him from the way" [Translator's note: the text has a stray closing brace here], as He said: ﴿وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ أعْمَالَهُمْ فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ — the straight [way].
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كَـيْدُ فِرْعَوْنَ إِلاَّ فِي تَبَابٍ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: that is, in loss.
Abū Jaʿfar said: from this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدَا أبِي لَهَبٍ﴾.
And His saying: ﴿وَمَا زَادُوهُمْ غَيْرَ تَتْبِيبٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَنْ عَمِـلَ سَـيِّئَةً فَلاَ يُجْزَىٰ إِلاَّ مِثْلَهَا﴾.
Qatāda said: meaning associating partners [with Allah] (shirk).

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيٰقَوْمِ مَا لِيۤ أَدْعُوكُـمْ إِلَى ٱلنَّجَاةِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: to faith in Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ جَرَمَ أَنَّمَا تَدْعُونَنِيۤ إِلَيْهِ لَيْسَ لَهُ دَعْوَةٌ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا وَلاَ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: meaning the idols.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Khalīl said: the meaning of ﴿لاَ جَرَمَ﴾ is "truly"; jarama al-shayʾu means it became true (ḥaqqa); and he recited:
وَلَقَدْ طَعَنْتُ أَبَا عُيَيْنَةَ طَعْنَةً * جَرَمَتْ فَزَارَةَ بَعْدَهَا أنْ يَغْضَبُوا
(I struck Abū ʿUyayna such a thrust that it made it due for Fazāra after it to be angry.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: as for "lā" entering upon "jarama", it is to indicate that it is a reply to [preceding] speech, and that it is not a fresh start.
So the meaning is: the falsity of what you call me to has become established, i.e. it has no answering of a call that benefits.
And His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ هُمْ أَصْحَابُ ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: they are the shedders of blood; and so said ʿAṭāʾ and Mujāhid.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَوقَاهُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِ مَا مَكَـرُواْ﴾.
Qatāda said: he was a man of the Copts, and Allah saved him along with the Children of Israel.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلنَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا غُدُوّاً وَعَشِيّاً﴾.
It is asked: how are they exposed to it morning and evening when they are among its inhabitants?
The answer to this is what ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: he said: the souls of the family of Pharaoh are in the bellies of black birds; they are exposed to the Fire twice every day, and it is said: this is your abode.
And Shuʿba narrated from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, who said: I heard Maymūn ibn Maysara say: when Abū Hurayra entered upon the morning he would call out: "We have entered the morning, praise be to Allah, and the family of Pharaoh have been exposed to the Fire"; and when he entered upon the evening he would call out: "We have entered the evening, praise be to Allah, and the family of Pharaoh have been exposed to the Fire." And no one heard Abū Hurayra but he sought refuge in Allah from the Fire.
And Mujāhid said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿ٱلنَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا غُدُوّاً وَعَشِيّاً﴾: he said: of the days of this world.
Al-Farrāʾ said: in the Resurrection there is no morning and no evening, but the equivalent span of that.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the exegesis is contrary to what al-Farrāʾ said, for the exegesis holds that this exposure is only in the days of this world.
And the meaning, too, clearly shows that it is so, because He said, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿ٱلنَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا غُدُوّاً وَعَشِيّاً﴾, then indicated that this is before the Day of Resurrection by His saying ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدْخِلُوۤاْ آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ أَشَدَّ ٱلْعَذَابِ﴾; so this indicated that the first is in the position of the punishment of the grave.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلأَشْهَادُ﴾.
Maʿmar said, from Qatāda: the angels.
Abū Jaʿfar said: its singular is shāhid, as one says ṣāḥib and aṣḥāb.
And it may be the plural of shahīd, like sharīf and ashrāf.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِن فِي صُدُورِهِمْ إِلاَّ كِبْرٌ مَّـا هُم بِبَالِغِيهِ﴾.
It is like His saying ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القرْيَةَ﴾: the meaning is: they will not attain what they intend by it, because the arrogance is something they have already engaged in; so this poses no difficulty.
And it has been said: the arrogance here is [seeking] superiority over the Prophet ﷺ, and that was their intention, and they did not attain it; as for their intention in the first [view], it is disputing about the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, so as to nullify them, and they did not attain that.
And it is said: only "the Jews" are meant by this; they were arrogant and held back, and said: [we wait] until the Antichrist (al-Dajjāl) comes out, and we will be with him; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that this group of the Jews will not reach the Dajjāl. And the proponent of this view cited as evidence His saying ﴿فَاسْتَعِذْ باللهِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِي سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ﴾.
Yusayʿ al-Kindī narrated from al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: Supplication is worship; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited ﴿وَقَالَ رَبُّكُـمُ ٱدْعُونِيۤ أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِي سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿دَاخِرِينَ﴾: abased.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذِ ٱلأَغْلاَلُ فِيۤ أَعْنَاقِهِمْ وٱلسَّلاَسِلَ يُسْحَبُونَ﴾.
And it has been read ﴿وَالسَّلاَسِلُ يُسْحَبُونَ﴾.
And in the reading of Ubayy: ﴿بِالسَّلاَسِلِ يُسْحَبُونَ﴾.
And al-Farrāʾ permitted ﴿وَالسَّلاَسِلِ يُسْحَبُونَ﴾ [in the genitive].
Abū Jaʿfar said: whoever reads ﴿والسَّلاَسلَ يَسْحَبُونَ﴾ [accusative, with active yasḥabūna], the meaning according to him is: they drag the chains; and this is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: and that is harder on them: they are made to drag them and cannot bear it.
And whoever reads ﴿والسَّلاَسِلُ يُسْحَبُونَ﴾ [nominative], the full stop (al-tamām) according to him is at ﴿والسَّلاَسِلُ﴾; then he starts afresh and says ﴿يُسْحَبُونَ فِي الحَمِيمِ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: "wa-l-salāsili" in the genitive is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is: their necks are in the fetters and the chains; just as the poet's saying is construed according to the meaning:
قَدْ سَالَمَ الحَيَّاتُ مِنْهُ القَدَمَا * الأُفْعُوَانَ والشُّجَاعَ الشَّجْعَمَا
(The snakes have made peace with his foot — the viper and the bold, huge serpent.)
[Translator's note: in the verse, «الأفعوانَ» is accusative although «الحيّاتُ» is nominative, because in meaning the foot and the snakes each make peace with the other.]

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ فِي ٱلنَّارِ يُسْجَرُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, the Fire is kindled with them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says sajartu al-shayʾa, i.e. I filled it; and from it is ﴿وَالبَحْرِ المَسْجُورِ﴾.
So the meaning on this [view] is: the Fire is filled with them; and the poet said, describing a mountain goat:
إذَا شَاءَ طَالَعَ مَسْجُورَةً * تَرَى حَوْلَهَا النَّبعَ والسَّاسَمَا
(When he wishes, he comes upon a brimming [spring], around which you see the nabʿ and sāsam trees.)
That is, a filled spring.

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكُمْ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَفْرَحُونَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
He made this clear by His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿فَرِحُوا بمَا عِنْدَهُمْ مِنَ العِلْمِ﴾.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَبِمَا كُنتُمْ تَمْرَحُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, you were insolent and exultant.

nahhas-meani:79-79.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلأَنْعَامَ لِتَرْكَـبُواْ مِنْهَا وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ﴾.
That is, the camels.
Qatāda said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَلِتَبْلُغُوا عَلَيْهَا حَاجَةً فِي صُدُورِكُمْ﴾: travel from one land to another.
And Mujāhid said: whatever need it may be.

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ فَرِحُواْ بِمَا عِندَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ﴾.
That is, they were content with it.
Mujāhid said: they said: we know better than you; we will not be resurrected, nor will we live after death.
Mujāhid said: ﴿وَحَاقَ بِهِم مَّا كَانُواْ بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾.
That is, the truth that the messengers brought.

nahhas-meani:85-85.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمْ يَكُ يَنفَعُهُمْ إِيمَانُهُمْ لَمَّا رَأَوْاْ بَأْسَنَا سُنَّتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ فِي عِبَادِهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, when they saw the punishment they believed, but their faith did not benefit them.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَخَسِرَ هُنَالِكَ ٱلْكَافِرُونَ﴾.
And they had been losers before that; [it is said "there"] because their loss became evident in that the punishment overtook them and their faith was not accepted.

safi-cedvel:59-60.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis (tawkīd); (لا) the lā of generic negation; (فيها) attached (mutaʿalliq) to the khabar (predicate) of lā; (الواو) a conjunction; (لكنّ ... لا يؤمنون) like ولكنّ ... لا يعلمون [Note: in verse (57) of this surah].
Clause: «إنّ الساعة لآتية ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «لا ريب فيها ... » is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of (إنّ).
And the clause: «لكنّ أكثر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إنّ الساعة لآتية.
And the clause: «لا يؤمنون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of لكنّ.
(60) (الواو) a conjunction; (أستجب) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the apodosis of a command; (لكم) attached to (أستجب); (عن عبادتي) attached to (يستكبرون); (السين) a particle of futurity; (داخرين) an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
And the clause: «قال ربّكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إنّ الساعة لآتية.
And the clause: «ادعوني ... » is in the position of accusative as the content of what was said (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «أستجب لكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of an implied condition, not joined by fāʾ, i.e. "if you call upon Me, I will answer you".
And the clause: «إنّ الذين يستكبرون ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: or it is a causal clause for what precedes, since "calling upon" (duʿāʾ) is made to include the meaning of "worship" (ʿibāda)].
And the clause: «يستكبرون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause: «سيدخلون ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative usage (majāz) and conformity (mushākala): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَقالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ».
It is a majāz mursal (loose figure) whose link is causality, because calling upon Allah (duʿāʾ) is the cause of worship. In the saying أستجب لكم there is mushākala (conformity), because the reward follows upon it. We have taken the speech as figurative because of the indication in His later words «إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبادَتِي», and this figure is supported by
the hadith of al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: «Supplication is worship»
