That is because the pattern faʿula with ḍamma on the ʿayn may be built from what may be wondered at, and runs in the course of «نِعْم» and «بئس» in all rulings. As to its agent, six views. First: it is a pronoun returning to the state, muḍāf to «الذين», as explained earlier. Second: it is a pronoun returning to their dispute, understood from «يُجادلون», as also explained. Third: it is the «كاف» in «كذلك». al-Zamakhsharī said: "The agent of «كَبُرَ» is His saying «كذلك», i.e. 'the like of that dispute has become great in detestation', and «ويَطْبع اللَّهُ» is a resumptive speech." The Shaykh rejected it: it dissociates the speech and adopts an unsound school. As for the dissociation, what appears in the Qurʾān as «كذلك نَطْبَعُ» or «يَطْبع» occurs only linked to one another, so likewise this. As for adopting an unsound school, he made the «كاف» a noun, and it is a noun only in necessity, contrary to al-Akhfash.
Fourth: the agent is omitted; al-Zamakhsharī transmitted it. He said: "Whoever said «كَبُرَ مَقْتاً عند الله جِدالُهم» has omitted the agent, and the agent cannot be omitted." I say: the one who said that is al-Ḥawfī, but he did not mean thereby to explain the iʿrāb; he meant to explain the meaning, which is the meaning of what I said before, that the agent is a pronoun returning to their dispute understood from its verb. al-Ḥawfī stated the original, which is the overt noun, and what he meant is a pronoun returning to it.
Fifth: the agent is a pronoun returning to what follows it, the tamyīz, like «نِعْمَ رَجُلاً زيدٌ» and «بئس غلاماً عمروٌ». Sixth: it is a pronoun returning to «مَنْ» in His saying {مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ}. He returned the pronoun of «كَبُرَ» in the singular by the wording of it; then he has observed the wording of «مَنْ» first in {مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ كَذَّابٌ}, then its meaning second in His saying {الذين يُجَادِلُونَ} to the end, then its wording third in His saying «كَبُر». All this if you parse «الذين» as following «مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ» as an adjective, explication or badal.
You know that the clause «كَبُرَ مَقْتاً» has two views. One: nominative, if we make it a khabar of a mubtadaʾ. Second: it has no position, if you do not make it a khabar but a resumptive clause. His saying «عندَ الله» is attached to «كَبُرَ»; and it was mentioned that it may also be a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or an agent, and both are weak. Third, and it is the sound one: it is governed by «يَطْبَعُ», i.e. "like that sealing, Allah seals." As for «يطبعُ اللَّهُ», two views, the clearer being that it is resumptive; the second, that it is the khabar of the relative, as all this was explained earlier.
His saying: «قَلْبِ متكبِّرٍ»: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Dhakwān read «قلب» with tanwīn, describing the heart with arrogance and tyranny, because both arise from it, even if the whole [person] is meant, as it is described with sin in His saying {فَإِنَّهُ آثِمٌ قَلْبُهُ} [al-Baqara: 283]. The others read «قلب» annexed to what follows, i.e. "on every heart of an arrogant person." al-Zamakhsharī implied a muḍāf in the first reading, i.e. "on every possessor of an arrogant heart", making the attribute belong to the owner of the heart. The Shaykh said: "There is no necessity calling for believing in the omission." I say: rather there is a necessity for it, namely the agreement of the two readings, since the described then becomes the same in both readings, the owner of the heart; unlike not implying it, in which the described in one is the heart and in the other its owner.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {أَسْبَابَ السماوات}: Two views. One: it follows the preceding «الأسباب» as a badal or ʿaṭf bayān. Two: it is accusative by an implied "I mean". The first is better, since the original is the absence of implication.
His saying: «فَأَطَّلِعَ»: The majority read it in the nominative, conjoined to «أَبْلُغُ», so it enters the sphere of hope. Ḥafṣ and others read it in the accusative. Three views. One: it is the answer to the command in His saying «ابْنِ لي», so it is accusative by an implied «أَنْ» after the «فاء» in its answer, according to the rule of the Basrans, as in the saying:
3933 - يا ناقُ سِيْري عَنَقاً فَسِيحا ... إلى سليمانَ فَنَسْتريحا
(O she-camel, go at a wide swift pace to Sulaymān, so that we may rest.)
This best accords with the school of the Basrans. Second: it is accusative. The Shaykh said: "As a conjunction on supposition, since the khabar of «لعلَّ» has often come paired with «أنْ», often in verse and rarely in prose. Whoever put it in the accusative supposed that the nominative verb occurring as khabar is accusative by «أنْ», and conjunction on supposition is frequent, although it is not regular." End of quotation. Third: it is accusative as the answer to hope in «لعلَّ», which is a Kufan school whose adherents cited this reading and the reading of ʿĀṣim {وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يزكى أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنفَعَهُ} [ʿAbasa: 3-4], with «فتنفَعَه» accusative as an answer to «لعلَّه». al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, saying: "likening hope to wish." The Basrans refuse that, and parse the two readings as above.
In Sūrat ʿAbasa it may be the answer to the question in His saying «وما يُدريك», since it follows from it in meaning. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Ibn Jubāra al-Hudhalī said: "As the answer to wish," and there is some question about that, since there is no wish in the wording, only hope. People have distinguished between wish and hope: hope occurs only with the possible, unlike wish, which occurs with it and with the impossible, as in the saying:
3934 - لَيْتَ الشبابَ هو الرَّجيعُ على الفتى ... والشيبُ كان هو البَدِئُ الأولُ
(Would that youth were what returns to the young man, and grey hair were what came first.)
«زَيَّنَ لفرعونَ» was read in the active, the agent being Satan. The disagreement over {وَصُدَّ عَنِ السبيل} has preceded in al-Raʿd; whoever made it active omitted the object, i.e. "he turned his people from the way." Ibn Wassāb read «وصِدَّ» with kasra on the ṣād, as though he transferred the vowel of the first dāl to the first radical after supposing its vowel taken away. This has preceded in the case of «رِدَّ», and that the three dialects permissible in «قيل» and «بِيع» are allowed in it. Ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakra read «وصَدٌّ» with fatḥa on the ṣād and ḍamma with tanwīn on the dāl, making it a maṣdar conjoined to «سوءُ عملِه», i.e. "Satan made the evil of his deed and the barring attractive to him." «التَّباب» is loss; this has preceded at His saying {غَيْرَ تَتْبِيبٍ} [Hūd: 101]. The disagreement has also preceded at His saying {يَدْخُلُونَ الجنة} in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ [verse 40].

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {وياقوم}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why did he bring the «واو» in the third vocative and not the second? I say: because the second enters upon speech that is an explanation of the general and an interpretation of it, so what enters upon it was given its ruling in the impermissibility of the entry of the «واو». As for the third, it enters upon speech that is not of that standing."
His saying: {وتدعونني إِلَى النار}: This clause is resumptive; he reports this of them after his question about his own calling. The implied form may be: "and what is the matter with you that you call me to the Fire," which is the apparent view. It is weak that the clause be a ḥāl, i.e. "What is the matter with you, that I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire?"

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying: {تَدْعُونَنِي}: This clause is a badal from the first «تَدْعونني» by way of explication of it. He used a verbal clause in His saying «تَدْعُونني» to show that their calling is false and without permanence, and a nominal clause in His saying «وأنا أَدْعوكم» to show the permanence of his calling and its strength.
The disagreement over {لاَ جَرَمَ} [Ghāfir: 43] has already preceded. al-Zamakhsharī said here: "It was reported from the Arabs «لا جُرْمَ أنه يفعل كذا» with ḍamma on the jīm and sukūn on the rāʾ in the sense of «لا بُدَّ», and fuʿl and faʿal are two brothers, like «رُشْد» and «رَشَد», «عُدْم» and «عَدَم»."

semin-durr:44-44.t: His saying: {وَأُفَوِّضُ}: This is resumptive. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a ḥāl from the agent of «أَقول».

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {النار}: The majority read it in the nominative. Three views. One: it is a badal from «سوءُ العذاب». Two: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it, that is the evil of the punishment, is the Fire," because it is the answer to an implied question; and «يُعْرَضُون», on these two views, may be a ḥāl from «النار» and may be a ḥāl from «آل فرعون». Three: it is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is «يُعْرَضون». «النارَ» was also read in the accusative. Two views. One: it is accusative by an implied verb which «يُعْرَضون» interprets in meaning, i.e. "they burn in the Fire, being exposed to it," like His saying {والظالمين أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ} [al-Insān: 31]. Two: it is accusative in the sense of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ); al-Zamakhsharī said this. On the first, «يُعْرَضُون» has no position, being an interpreter; on the second, it is a ḥāl as above.
His saying: «ويومَ تقومُ»: Three views, the clearest being that it is governed by an implied saying, and that implied saying is the one in which the imperative clause «أدخِلوا» is quoted, the implied form being: "and it will be said, on the day the Hour is established: Cause to enter." Two: it is accusative by «أدخِلوا», i.e. "cause to enter on the day the Hour is established." On these two views the pause is complete at His saying «وعَشِيَّاً». Three: it is conjoined to the two adverbials before it, so it is governed by «يُعْرَضُون». On this the pause is at His saying «الساعة», and «أَدْخِلوا» is governed by an implied saying, i.e. "it will be said to them such and such."
al-Kisāʾī, Ḥamza, Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read «أدْخِلُوا» with the hamza of cutting, an imperative from «أَدْخَلَ», so «آلَ فرعون» is the first object and «أشدَّ العذاب» the second object. The others read «ادْخُلوا» with the hamza of joining, from «دَخَلَ يَدْخُلُ». So «آلَ فرعونَ» is a vocative whose particle of address has been omitted, and «أشدَّ» is accusative by it, either as an adverbial or as a direct object, i.e. "Enter, O family of Pharaoh, into the severest punishment."

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying: {وَإِذْ يَتَحَآجُّونَ}: As to the operator in «إذ», three views. One: it is conjoined to «غُدُوَّاً», so it is governed by «يُعْرَضون», i.e. "they are exposed to the Fire at all these times"; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. Two: it is conjoined to His saying {إِذِ القلوب لَدَى الحناجر} [Ghāfir: 18]; al-Ṭabarī said this. There is some question about it because of the distance between them, and because the apparent view is that the pronoun in «يَتَحاجُّون» returns to the family of Pharaoh. Three: it is accusative by an implied "Remember", which is clear.
His saying: «تَبَعاً»: Three views. One: it is a collective noun for «تابع» (follower), like «خادِم» and «خَدَم», «غائِب» and «غَيَبَ», «أَديم» and «أَدَم». Two: it is a maṣdar standing in the place of the active participle, i.e. «تابِعين». Three: it is also a maṣdar, but with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «ذوي تَبَع».
His saying: «نصيباً»: Three views. One: it is accusative by an implied verb that His saying «مُغْنُون» indicates, the implied form being "Will you ward off from us a share." Two: «مُغْنون» is given the sense of «حامِلين» (bearing). Three: it is accusative as a maṣdar. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "As «شيءٌ» was thus. Do you not see His saying {لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلاَ أَوْلاَدُهُمْ مِّنَ الله شَيْئاً} [Āl ʿImrān: 116]? «شيْئاً» is in the place of «غَناء» (avail), so likewise «نصيباً»." «من النار» is an adjective of «نَصيباً».

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {إِنَّا كُلٌّ}: The majority read «كلٌ» in the nominative. Its nominative is as a mubtadaʾ, «فيها» is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «إنَّ». This is like His saying in Āl ʿImrān {قُلْ إِنَّ الأمر كُلُّهُ للَّهِ} in the reading of Abū ʿAmr. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read it in the accusative, with three views. One: it is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the noun of «إنَّ». al-Zamakhsharī said: "An emphasis of the noun of «إنَّ», which is definite; and the tanwīn is a compensation for the muḍāf ilayhi; he means: 'we, all of us, are in it'." End of quotation. That is, «فيها» is then the khabar. Ibn ʿAṭiyya also held that it is an emphasis. Ibn Mālik rejected this view and said in his Tasḥīl: "The intention of its annexation does not suffice, contrary to al-Zamakhsharī." I say: this is not the school of al-Zamakhsharī alone; it is also transmitted from the Kufans. Two: it is accusative as ḥāl. Ibn Mālik said: "The view I accept is that «كلاً» in the stated reading is accusative as a ḥāl from the nominative pronoun in «فيها», and «فيها» is the operator, and it has been fronted before it despite its non-flexibility, as it was fronted in the reading of whoever read {والسماوات مَطْوِيَّاتٍ بِيَمِينِهِ}, and like the saying of al-Nābigha:
3935 - رَهْطُ ابنِ كُوْزٍ مُحقِبيْ أَدْراعِهم ... فيهمْ ورَهْطُ ربيعةَ بنِ حُذار
(The clan of Ibn Kūz, carrying their coats of mail behind them, among them, and the clan of Rabīʿa ibn Ḥudhār.)
and the saying of one of the Ṭayyiʾites:
3936 - دعا فَأَجَبْنَا وَهْو بادِيَ ذلَّةٍ ... لديكمْ وكان النصرُ غيرَ بعيدِ
(He called and we answered, while he showed humility before you, and victory was not far.)
meaning with «باديَ» in the accusative." This is the school of al-Akhfash, but al-Zamakhsharī forbade it, saying: "If you ask: can «كلاً» be a ḥāl governed by «فيها»? I say: no, because the adverbial does not operate on a fronted ḥāl as it operates on a fronted adverbial. You say «كلَّ يوم لك ثوبٌ», but you do not say «قائماً في الدار زيد»." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "What he forbade, al-Akhfash permitted when the ḥāl is in the middle, as in «زيدٌ قائماً في الدار» and «زيدٌ قائماً عندك»; and the example he gave does not match what is in the verse, because in the verse the subject of the predication, which is the noun of «إنَّ», came first, and the ḥāl came in the middle, if we say it is a ḥāl, with its operator delayed. As for his example, 'you do not say «قائماً في الدار زيد»', both the predicate and the subject are delayed in it. Some have mentioned that the prohibition in that is by consensus of the grammarians."
I say: al-Zamakhsharī's prohibition is correct because he proceeds according to the school of the majority, and as for his illustration with what he mentioned, it does not harm him, because it is in a place of prohibition, so his not permitting it is sound.
Three: «كلاً» is a badal from «نا» in «إنَّا», for «كلاً» has been followed by operators, as if it were said "Indeed all are in it."
And since they have interpreted the saying:
2937 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . حَوْلاً أَكْتعاً ...
[and the saying:]
2938 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . وحَوْلاً أَجْمعا ...
as a badal despite the non-flexibility of «أكتع» and «أجمع», it is all the more fitting and proper in «كل». Moreover the well-known thing is the definiteness of «كل» when it is cut off. It is related, as common and widespread: «مررتُ بكلٍ قائماً وببعض جالساً», and some ascribe it to Sībawayh. The indefiniteness of «كل» and its accusative as ḥāl is extremely irregular, as in «مررت بهم كلاً», i.e. all together. If it is said: this involves a total badal from a pronoun of the present person, which is not permissible, there are two answers. One: the Kufans and al-Akhfash allow that, and they recited the saying:
3939 - أنا سيفُ العشيرةِ فاعْرِفوني ... حُمَيْداً قد تَذَّرَّيْتُ السَّناما
(I am the sword of the clan, so know me: Ḥumayd; I have climbed to the hump's summit.)
where «حُميداً» is a badal from the yā' of «اعرِفوني»; the Basrans interpreted it as accusative by ikhtiṣāṣ. Two: that what we have here is not the place of disagreement, because it indicates inclusion and comprehensiveness. They have said that whenever the badal indicates that, it is permissible, and they recited:
3940 - فما بَرِحَتْ أقدامنا في مكانِنا ... ثلاثتِنا حتى أُزِيْرُوا المنَائيا
(Our feet did not leave our place, the three of us, until they were made to visit the deaths.)
and like it His saying the Exalted {تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيداً لأَوَّلِنَا وَآخِرِنَا} [al-Māʾida: 114]. They said «ثلاثتنا» is a badal from «نا» in «مكاننا» because of its indication of inclusion, and likewise «لأوَّلنا وآخِرنا» is a badal from «نا» in «لنا»; so for that to be permissible in «كل», which is the origin in comprehensiveness and inclusion, is a fortiori. This is the speech of the Shaykh on the third view, and there is some question about it, because al-Mubarrad and Makkī stated explicitly that the badal in this verse is not permissible, so how can it be claimed that there is no disagreement over the badal, this being the case? It should not be said that in the verse there is a fourth view: that «كلاً» is an adjective of the noun of «إنَّ», for al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ stated that explicitly, saying: it is an adjective of the noun of «إنَّ», because the Kufans use the name "adjective" for emphasis and do not mean the real adjective. Among those who stated explicitly what I have said regarding the stated interpretation is Makkī, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, and because al-Kisāʾī permitted describing only the pronoun of the absent person, not the speaker or the addressee.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {يَوْماً مِّنَ العذاب}: There are two views about «يوماً». One: it is an adverbial of «يُخَفِّفْ», and the object of «يُخَفِّفْ» is omitted, i.e. "lighten for us something of the punishment in a day." According to the view of al-Akhfash, «مِنْ» may be redundant, so «العذاب» would be the object, i.e. "lighten for us on the day of punishment." Two: it is a direct object, but the day is not lightened; what is lightened is what is contained in it, so the implied form is "lighten the punishment of a day." That is unsettled given His saying «من العذاب», and saying that it is a confirming adjective like a ḥāl is more unsettled still. The apparent view is that «مِن العذاب» is the object of «يُخَفِّف», «مِنْ» is partitive, and «يوماً» is an adverbial. They asked that some of the punishment be lightened for them, not all of it, on some day, not every day or a particular day.

semin-durr:51-51.t: His saying: {وَيَوْمَ يَقُومُ الأشهاد}: The majority read «يقوم» with yā' below. Abū ʿAmr in the narration of al-Minqarī from him, Ibn Hurmuz and Ismāʿīl read it with tā' above, for the feminine of the group. «الأشهادُ» may be the plural of «شهيد», like «شَريف» and «أَشْراف», which agrees with His saying {فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جِئْنَا مِن كُلِّ أمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ} [al-Nisāʾ: 41]; or the plural of «شاهِد», like «صاحِب» and «أصحاب», which agrees with His saying {إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِداً} [al-Aḥzāb: 45].

semin-durr:52-52.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ}: a badal from the preceding «يوم», or an explication of it, or it is accusative by an implied "I mean". The disagreement over His saying «يَنْفَع الظالمين» with tā' and yā' has already preceded at the end of al-Rūm.

semin-durr:54-54.t: His saying: {هُدًى وذكرى}: Two views on both. One: they are both objects of purpose, i.e. "for the sake of guidance and remembrance." Two: they are both maṣdars in the position of ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَفِيعُ الدَّرَجَاتِ ذُو الْعَرْشِ يُلْقِي الرُّوحَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ عَلَى مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ لِيُنْذِرَ يَوْمَ التَّلَاقِ (١٥)).
His saying (رَفِيعُ الدَّرَجَاتِ): the implied wording may be "He is رَفِيعُ الدَّرَجَاتِ"; then «ذُو» is a naʿt (adjective), and «يُلْقِي» is resumptive. It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being ذُو الْعَرْشِ, or يُلْقِي.
And (مِنْ أَمْرِهِ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الرُّوحَ, or attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يُلْقِي».

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ هُمْ بَارِزُونَ لَا يَخْفَى عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْهُمْ شَيْءٌ لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ لَا ظُلْمَ الْيَوْمَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ (١٧))
His saying (يَوْمَ هُمْ): «يَوْمَ» is a badal (substitute) of (يَوْمَ التَّلَاقِ). The implied wording may also be "remember the day" (اذْكُرْ يَوْمَ), or it may be an adverb of time for التَّلَاقِي (the meeting). «هُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «بَارِزُونَ» is its khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of the genitive (jarr) by «يَوْمَ» being put in construct with it.
And (لَا يَخْفَى): it may be a further khabar, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «بَارِزُونَ», or resumptive. (الْيَوْمَ): an adverb of time; what governs it is «لِمَنْ», or whatever the preposition is attached to. It is also said: it is an adverb of time for الْمُلْكُ. (لِلَّهِ): i.e. "it is لِلَّهِ (Allah's)". It is also said: the pause is on الْمُلْكُ; then a new sentence begins, saying: "it is — today — لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ", i.e. the day is settled as belonging to Allah. The next (الْيَوْمَ) is an adverb of time for «تُجْزَى». And the last (الْيَوْمَ) is the khabar of «لَا», i.e. "there is no injustice existing today".

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَنْذِرْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْآزِفَةِ إِذِ الْقُلُوبُ لَدَى الْحَنَاجِرِ كَاظِمِينَ مَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ وَلَا شَفِيعٍ يُطَاعُ (١٨)).
(إِذِ) is a badal (substitute) of يَوْمِ الْآزِفَةِ.
And (كَاظِمِينَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الْقُلُوبُ, because what is meant is their owners.
It is also said: it is a ḥāl of the pronoun in «لَدَى». It is also said: it is a ḥāl of the pronoun in «أَنْذِرْهُمْ». (وَلَا شَفِيعٍ يُطَاعُ): «يُطَاعُ» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of شَفِيعٍ according to the wording, or in the position of the nominative according to the position [of شَفِيعٍ].

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ ذَرُونِي أَقْتُلْ مُوسَى وَلْيَدْعُ رَبَّهُ إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ يُبَدِّلَ دِينَكُمْ أَوْ أَنْ يُظْهِرَ فِي الْأَرْضِ الْفَسَادَ (٢٦)).
His saying (أَوْ أَنْ يُظْهِرَ): it is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "I fear both things".
It is also read «أَوْ أَنْ يُظْهِرَ», i.e. "I fear one of the two", and whichever of them happened would be feared. [Translator's note: so in the text — both the lemma and the variant are written «أَوْ أَنْ يُظْهِرَ». The explanation "I fear both things" fits the reading with wāw (وَأَنْ يُظْهِرَ), while "one of the two" fits the reading with أَوْ.]

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مُؤْمِنٌ مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إِيمَانَهُ أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَنْ يَقُولَ رَبِّيَ اللَّهُ وَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَإِنْ يَكُ كَاذِبًا فَعَلَيْهِ كَذِبُهُ وَإِنْ يَكُ صَادِقًا يُصِبْكُمْ بَعْضُ الَّذِي يَعِدُكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ كَذَّابٌ (٢٨)).
His saying (مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ): it is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of مُؤْمِنٌ.
It is also said: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَكْتُمُ», i.e. he conceals it from the family of Pharaoh. (أَنْ يَقُولَ): i.e. "for saying" (لِأَنْ يَقُولَ).
(وَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا قَوْمِ لَكُمُ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ ظَاهِرِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَمَنْ يَنْصُرُنَا مِنْ بَأْسِ اللَّهِ إِنْ جَاءَنَا قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ مَا أُرِيكُمْ إِلَّا مَا أَرَى وَمَا أَهْدِيكُمْ إِلَّا سَبِيلَ الرَّشَادِ (٢٩)).
His saying (ظَاهِرِينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the plural pronoun in «لَكُمْ».
And (أُرِيكُمْ) is transitive to two objects, the second being «مَا أَرَى»; it is from al-raʾy in the sense of belief (iʿtiqād).
(سَبِيلَ الرَّشَادِ): the majority read it without doubling, and it is a noun standing for the maṣdar (verbal noun), either al-rushd (right guidance) or al-irshād (guiding). It was also read with the shīn doubled (الرَّشَّادِ), and it is the one [Translator's note: the text has «الَّذِينَ» ("those who"), evidently for «الَّذِي» ("the one who")] from whom guiding or right guidance is abundant.

ukberi-tibyan:32-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَا قَوْمِ إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَوْمَ التَّنَادِ (٣٢) يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ مُدْبِرِينَ مَا لَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ عَاصِمٍ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ هَادٍ (٣٣)).
His saying (يَوْمَ التَّنَادِ): the majority read it without doubling. Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him, read it with the dāl doubled (التَّنَادِّ); it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «تَنَادَّ الْقَوْمُ», said when the people scatter; i.e. the day when people's ways diverge.
And (يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ) is a badal (substitute) of the day before it. And (مَا لَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ) is in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي آيَاتِ اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ سُلْطَانٍ أَتَاهُمْ كَبُرَ مَقْتًا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَعِنْدَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كَذَلِكَ يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ قَلْبِ مُتَكَبِّرٍ جَبَّارٍ (٣٥)).
His saying (الَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ): there are several views on it:
The first: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are الَّذِينَ…", and «هُمْ» refers back to His saying (مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ), because that is plural in meaning. The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ, the khabar being «يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ», with the referring pronoun omitted, i.e. "upon every heart of an arrogant one among them". And (كَذَلِكَ) is then the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is thus", and what lies between the two is a well-placed parenthetical (muʿtariḍ musaddad).
The third: that the khabar is «كَبُرَ مَقْتًا», i.e. "their saying is greatly hateful".
The fourth: that the khabar is omitted, i.e. "are obstinate", or the like.
The fifth: that it is accusative by implying أَعْنِي ("I mean").
His saying (عَلَى كُلِّ قَلْبِ): it is read with tanwīn (قَلْبٍ), and (مُتَكَبِّرٍ) is then a naʿt (adjective) of it, the owner of the heart being meant. It is also read as a genitive construct; and the construct of «كُلِّ» with الْقَلْبِ is meant to make the heart general, so that the sealing covers every heart; in meaning it is like the reading of whoever read: عَلَى قَلْبِ كُلِّ مُتَكَبِّرٍ.

ukberi-tibyan:36-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يَا هَامَانُ ابْنِ لِي صَرْحًا لَعَلِّي أَبْلُغُ الْأَسْبَابَ (٣٦) أَسْبَابَ السَّمَاوَاتِ فَأَطَّلِعَ إِلَى إِلَهِ مُوسَى وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّهُ كَاذِبًا وَكَذَلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِفِرْعَوْنَ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ وَصُدَّ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ وَمَا كَيْدُ فِرْعَوْنَ إِلَّا فِي تَبَابٍ (٣٧)).
His saying (أَسْبَابَ السَّمَاوَاتِ): it is a badal (substitute) of what precedes it.
(فَأَطَّلِعَ): in the nominative, conjoined to أَبْلُغُ; and in the accusative as the answer to the command, i.e. "if you build for me, I shall look". Some said: it is the answer to لَعَلِّي, since that carries the meaning of wishing (al-tamannī).

ukberi-tibyan:41-42.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَا قَوْمِ مَا لِي أَدْعُوكُمْ إِلَى النَّجَاةِ وَتَدْعُونَنِي إِلَى النَّارِ (٤١) تَدْعُونَنِي لِأَكْفُرَ بِاللَّهِ وَأُشْرِكَ بِهِ مَا لَيْسَ لِي بِهِ عِلْمٌ وَأَنَا أَدْعُوكُمْ إِلَى الْعَزِيزِ الْغَفَّارِ (٤٢)).
His saying (تَدْعُونَنِي): the clause and what is connected with it is a badal (substitute) of, or an explanation of, the first تَدْعُونَنِي.

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَسَتَذْكُرُونَ مَا أَقُولُ لَكُمْ وَأُفَوِّضُ أَمْرِي إِلَى اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ (٤٤)).
His saying (وَأُفَوِّضُ أَمْرِي إِلَى اللَّهِ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «أَقُولُ».

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (النَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا غُدُوًّا وَعَشِيًّا وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ أَدْخِلُوا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ أَشَدَّ الْعَذَابِ (٤٦)).
His saying (النَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا): there are two views on it. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «يُعْرَضُونَ» is its khabar (predicate). The second: that it is a badal (substitute) of «سُوءُ الْعَذَابِ».
It is also read in the accusative (النَّارَ), by an implied verb that «يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا» explains, its implied form being "they will roast in the fire", or the like; on this view «يُعْرَضُونَ» has no grammatical position. On the badal view, its position is that of a ḥāl (circumstantial), either of النَّارُ or of آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ.
(أَدْخِلُوا): it is read with a connecting hamza (ادْخُلُوا), i.e. it is said to the family of Pharaoh; on this the implied wording is "O family of Pharaoh". It is also read with a disjunctive hamza and kasra on the khāʾ (أَدْخِلُوا), i.e. Allah the Exalted says [it] to the angels.

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ يَتَحَاجُّونَ فِي النَّارِ فَيَقُولُ الضُّعَفَاءُ لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا إِنَّا كُنَّا لَكُمْ تَبَعًا فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُغْنُونَ عَنَّا نَصِيبًا مِنَ النَّارِ (٤٧)).
His saying (وَإِذْ يَتَحَاجُّونَ): it may be conjoined to «غُدُوًّا», or the implied wording may be "and remember". And (تَبَعًا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of the active participle. And (نَصِيبًا) is accusative by a verb indicated by مُغْنُونَ, its implied form being "will you ward off from us" or "hold back from us". It may also be in the position of the maṣdar, just as شَيْءٌ is so; do you not see His saying (لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا)? There شَيْئًا is in the place of "availing" (غَنَاءٍ); so likewise نَصِيبًا.

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ فِي النَّارِ لِخَزَنَةِ جَهَنَّمَ ادْعُوَا رَبَّكُمْ يُخَفِّفْ عَنَّا يَوْمًا مِنَ الْعَذَابِ (٤٩)).
His saying (يُخَفِّفْ عَنَّا يَوْمًا): it may be an adverb of time (ẓarf), i.e. "lighten for us, in a day, something of the punishment"; so the object is omitted. On the view of al-Akhfash, «مِنْ» may be redundant (zāʾida). It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "the punishment of a day", like His saying (وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا), i.e. the punishment of a day.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ لَا يَنْفَعُ الظَّالِمِينَ مَعْذِرَتُهُمْ وَلَهُمُ اللَّعْنَةُ وَلَهُمْ سُوءُ الدَّارِ (٥٢)).
His saying (لَا يَنْفَعُ): it is a badal (substitute) of «يَوْمَ يَقُومُ». [Translator's note: so in the text; what is a badal is evidently يَوْمَ (يَوْمَ لَا يَنْفَعُ), substituted for وَيَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْأَشْهَادُ in the preceding verse.]

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمَى وَالْبَصِيرُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَلَا الْمُسِيءُ قَلِيلًا مَا تَتَذَكَّرُونَ (٥٨)).
His saying (وَلَا الْمُسِيءُ): «لَا» is redundant (zāʾida).

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِالْكِتَابِ وَبِمَا أَرْسَلْنَا بِهِ رُسُلَنَا فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ إِذِ الْأَغْلَالُ فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ وَالسَّلَاسِلُ يُسْحَبُونَ (٧١)).
His saying (إِذِ الْأَغْلَالُ): «إِذْ» is an adverb of past time, and what is meant by it here is the future, because of His saying (فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ). I have mentioned this at His saying (وَلَوْ تَرَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا إِذْ يَرَوْنَ الْعَذَابَ).
And (السَّلَاسِلُ), in the nominative: it may be conjoined to الْأَغْلَالُ, the khabar (predicate) being «فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ»; or it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar omitted, i.e. "and the chains are on their necks", omitted because the first indicates it. On this view «يُسْحَبُونَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in the preposition phrase, or resumptive. Or the khabar may be «يُسْحَبُونَ», with the referring pronoun omitted, i.e. "they are dragged by them".
It was also read in the accusative (وَالسَّلَاسِلَ), with يَسْحَبُونَ with fatḥa on the yāʾ; the object here is placed before the verb.

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلًا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَصَصْنَا عَلَيْكَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ لَمْ نَقْصُصْ عَلَيْكَ وَمَا كَانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِآيَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ قُضِيَ بِالْحَقِّ وَخَسِرَ هُنَالِكَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ (٧٨)).
His saying (مِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَصَصْنَا): مِنْهُمْ may be what puts مَنْ in the nominative, since it has been made a naʿt (adjective) of رُسُلًا; or it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), the clause being a naʿt of رُسُلًا; or it may be resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:81-81.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ فَأَيَّ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ تُنْكِرُونَ (٨١)).
(فَأَيَّ) is accusative (manṣūb) by «تُنْكِرُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:83-83.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَرِحُوا بِمَا عِنْدَهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ وَحَاقَ بِهِمْ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ (٨٣)).
His saying (بِمَا عِنْدَهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ): «مِنْ» here has the sense of substitution (al-badal), i.e. "in place of knowledge"; and it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «مَا», or of the pronoun in the adverbial phrase.

ukberi-tibyan:85-85.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمْ يَكُ يَنْفَعُهُمْ إِيمَانُهُمْ لَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنَا سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ فِي عِبَادِهِ وَخَسِرَ هُنَالِكَ الْكَافِرُونَ (٨٥)).
His saying (سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ): it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "We dealt with them according to the practice of Allah" (سَنَنَّا بِهِمْ سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ). And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (حم (١) تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتَابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ (٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حم تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتَابِ): it is like (الم تَنْزِيلُ).

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (غَافِرِ الذَّنْبِ وَقَابِلِ التَّوْبِ شَدِيدِ الْعِقَابِ ذِي الطَّوْلِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ إِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ (٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (غَافِرِ الذَّنْبِ وَقَابِلِ التَّوْبِ): both of them are a naʿt (adjective) of what precedes, and the annexation is pure (maḥḍa) [Translator's note: i.e. it makes them definite].
As for (شَدِيدِ الْعِقَابِ), it is indefinite, because the implied form is «شَدِيدٌ عِقَابُهُ» ("severe is His punishment"); so it is a badal (substitute). It is not permitted that «شَدِيدِ» be in the sense of مُشَدَّد, as أَذِين came in the sense of مُؤَذِّن ("announcer"), so that the annexation would be pure and it would become definite, and so be a naʿt as well. As for (ذِي الطَّوْلِ): it is a naʿt as well. (لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ): it may be a naʿt, and it may be resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَكَذَلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّهُمْ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنَّهُمْ): it is like the one in [Sūrat] Yūnus. [Translator's note: i.e. Yūnus 10:33, «كَذَلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ فَسَقُوا أَنَّهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ».]

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ الْعَرْشَ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهُ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ وَيُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا رَبَّنَا وَسِعْتَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ رَحْمَةً وَعِلْمًا فَاغْفِرْ لِلَّذِينَ تَابُوا وَاتَّبَعُوا سَبِيلَكَ وَقِهِمْ عَذَابَ الْجَحِيمِ (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يُسَبِّحُونَ» is its khabar (predicate).
(رَبَّنَا): i.e. "saying (يَقُولُونَ)", and this omitted [verb] is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And (رَحْمَةً وَعِلْمًا): a tamyīz (specification); the original is «وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ رَحْمَتُكَ وَعِلْمُكَ» ("Your mercy and Your knowledge encompassed everything").

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (رَبَّنَا وَأَدْخِلْهُمْ جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ الَّتِي وَعَدْتَهُمْ وَمَنْ صَلَحَ مِنْ آبَائِهِمْ وَأَزْوَاجِهِمْ وَذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ (٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَنْ صَلَحَ): in the position of the accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the pronoun in «أَدْخِلْهُمْ», i.e. "and admit whoever is righteous (وَأَدْخِلْ مَنْ صَلَحَ)".
It has also been said: it is conjoined to the pronoun in «وَعَدْتَهُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُنَادَوْنَ لَمَقْتُ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ مَقْتِكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ إِذْ تُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى الْإِيمَانِ فَتَكْفُرُونَ (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ مَقْتِكُمْ): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its fāʿil (agent), and (أَنْفُسَكُمْ) is accusative (manṣūb) by it. And «إِذْ» is an adverb (ẓarf) of an omitted verb, its implied form being «مَقَتَكُمْ إِذْ تَدْعُونَ» ("He detested you when you were called"). [Translator's note: the printed text vocalises the verb here as تَدْعُونَ ("you call"), and below as دَعَوْا; the Quranic wording is تُدْعَوْنَ ("you are called"), and the sense intended is evidently the passive.] It is not permitted that «مَقْتُ اللَّهِ» governs it, because it is a maṣdar about which a khabar (predicate) has [already] been given, namely His saying «أَكْبَرُ مِنْ»; nor «مَقْتِكُمْ», because they did not detest themselves when they were called to faith; they only detested themselves in the Fire, and at that time they are not called to faith.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ذَلِكُمْ بِأَنَّهُ إِذَا دُعِيَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ كَفَرْتُمْ وَإِنْ يُشْرَكْ بِهِ تُؤْمِنُوا فَالْحُكْمُ لِلَّهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْكَبِيرِ (١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَحْدَهُ): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from اللَّه, i.e. "called upon alone (دُعِيَ مُفْرَدًا)".
Yūnus said: it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), its implied form being «دُعِيَ حِيَالُهُ وَحْدَهُ» [Translator's note: as printed; i.e. "called upon by Himself, alone"]. It is a maṣdar with its augment omitted, and its verb is «أَوْحَدْتُهُ إِيحَادًا» ("I singled him out").

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يُنادَوْنَ لَمَقْتُ اللَّهِ أكْبَرُ مِن مَقْتِكم أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ — its meaning is: "Those who disbelieved will be called out to, when they are in the state of punishment: Allah's loathing of you in the world, when you were called to faith and you disbelieved, is greater than your loathing of yourselves when you were punished in the Fire."

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿قالُوا رَبَّنا أمَتَّنا اثْنَتَيْنِ وأحْيَيْتَنا اثْنَتَيْنِ فاعْتَرَفْنا بِذُنُوبِنا﴾, that is: You have shown us of the signs what necessitates that we must confess. And they said concerning "أمَتَّنا اثْنَتَيْنِ وأحْيَيْتَنا اثْنَتَيْنِ": that is, You created us dead, then You gave us life, then You caused us to die afterwards, then You resurrected us after death. And it has come in some commentaries that one of the two lives and one of the two deaths is that one is brought to life in the grave and then dies; that fits "أحْيَيْتَنا" and "أمَتَّنا" better, but the first is more common in the commentary.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُلْقِي الرُّوحَ مِن أمْرِهِ عَلى مَن يَشاءُ مِن عِبادِهِ﴾ — it has come in the commentary that "الرُّوح" is revelation; it has come that "الرُّوح" is the Quran; and it has come that "الرُّوح" is the matter of prophethood, so that the meaning would be: "You cast the spirit, or the matter of prophethood, upon whom You will, upon whom You single out for the message". ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ يَوْمَ التَّلاقِ﴾, that is: so that the Prophet ﷺ may warn of the Day of Meeting by what is revealed to him. It is also permissible that it be "so that Allah may warn of the Day of Meeting", but the better — and Allah knows best — is that it be "so that the Prophet ﷺ may warn", and the proof of that is that it has been read: "لِتُنْذِرَ يَوْمَ التَّلاقِ" with the tāʾ. "يَوْمَ التَّلاقِي" with the yāʾ retained is also permissible, and the omission is permissible and good, because it is the end of a verse. The meaning of "التَّلاقِي" is: the day on which the people of the earth and the people of heaven meet. The interpretation of "الرُّوح" in what we have explained is that by it is the life of people, because everyone who is guided is alive and everyone who is astray is like the dead. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أمْواتٌ غَيْرُ أحْياءٍ وما يَشْعُرُونَ أيّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 21], and He said: ﴿أوَمَن كانَ مَيْتًا فَأحْيَيْناهُ وجَعَلْنا لَهُ نُورًا يَمْشِي بِهِ في النّاسِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 122]. This is permissible in people's speech: a speaker says to someone who does not understand from him what is for his own good: "You are dead."

zajjaj:18-18.t:
﴿وَأنْذِرْهم يَوْمَ الآزِفَةِ﴾ — the meaning of "أنْذِرْهم" is: make them fear; and "الآزِفَة" is the Day of Resurrection, so it has come in the commentary. It was called "آزِفَة" only because it is near, even if people consider its span far off. One says: "قَدْ أزِفَ الأمْرُ" (the matter has drawn near), when it comes close.
And His saying: ﴿إذِ القُلُوبُ لَدى الحَناجِرِ كاظِمِينَ﴾ — "كاظِمِينَ" is made accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the ḥāl is construed according to the meaning, because hearts are not described as "كاظِمَة" (suppressing [grief]); rather, those who suppress are the owners of the hearts. The meaning is: "when the hearts of people are at the throats while they are suppressing [their grief]". It has come in the commentary that the heart rises from terror and sticks to the throat, so it neither returns to its place nor comes out so that one might find relief from the distress of one's grief. ﴿ما لِلظّالِمِينَ مِن حَمِيمٍ ولا شَفِيعٍ يُطاعُ﴾ — "يُطاعُ" is an attribute of "شَفِيعٍ", that is: "nor any intercessor who is obeyed".

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿يَعْلَمُ خائِنَةَ الأعْيُنِ﴾: when a looker looks with a treacherous look, Allah knows it. If he looks a first look without intending treachery, that is not a sin; but if he looks again with the intention of treachery in looking, Allah knows that. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, but He mentioned knowledge here so that it would be known that the requital will certainly take place.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أرْسَلْنا مُوسى بِآياتِنا﴾, that is: with Our signs which indicate the soundness of his prophethood — the staff, the bringing out of his hand white without any harm, and the like of that. ﴿وَسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾, that is: "a manifest proof".

zajjaj:24-24.t: ﴿إلى فِرْعَوْنَ وهامانَ وقارُونَ﴾ — these names are in the position of the genitive, but they take fatḥa because they are diptotes (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), since they are definite and they are foreign. ﴿فَقالُوا ساحِرٌ كَذّابٌ﴾ — the meaning is: "they said: he is a sorcerer, a liar". They made the matter of the signs, which created beings are incapable of, into sorcery.

zajjaj:25-25.t: ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَهم بِالحَقِّ مِن عِنْدِنا قالُوا اقْتُلُوا أبْناءَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ واسْتَحْيُوا نِساءَهُمْ﴾ — it had been said to Pharaoh that his kingdom would cease because of a boy to be born, so it was said: do this, so that the newborn will not escape. ﴿وَما كَيْدُ الكافِرِينَ إلا في ضَلالٍ﴾, that is: it comes to nothing, and Allah brings upon it what He wills.

zajjaj:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿أوْ أنْ يُظْهِرَ في الأرْضِ الفَسادَ﴾ — the codices of the people of Iraq are like this, and in the codex of the people of the Hijaz: "وَأنْ يُظْهِرَ" without alif. "وَأنْ يَظْهَرَ" is also permissible. The meaning of "أوْ" is the occurrence of one of two things; so the meaning with "أوْ" is that Pharaoh said: "I fear that he will change your religion or cause corruption" — he made obedience to Allah the Exalted the corruption — so the meaning would be: "I fear that he will nullify your religion altogether, and if he does not nullify it, he will introduce corruption into it". And whoever reads "وأنْ", the meaning will be: "I fear the nullification of your religion, and the corruption along with it".

zajjaj:28-28.t:
﴿وَقالَ رَجُلٌ مُؤْمِنٌ مِن آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إيمانَهُ﴾ — it has come in the commentary that this man — I mean the believer of Pharaoh's family — was called "Simʿān", and it was said his name was "Ḥabīb". "مِن آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ" may be an attribute of the man, and "يَكْتُمُ إيمانَهُ" then has something omitted with it, the meaning being: "concealing his faith from them". Or "يَكْتُمُ" may be an attribute of "رَجُلٌ", so that the meaning would be: "and a believing man said, concealing his faith from Pharaoh's family". ﴿أتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلا أنْ يَقُولَ رَبِّيَ اللَّهُ﴾ — the meaning is: "because he says: my Lord is Allah". ﴿وَقَدْ جاءَكم بِالبَيِّناتِ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾, that is: with what indicates his truthfulness among the signs of prophethood. ﴿وَإنْ يَكُ كاذِبًا فَعَلَيْهِ كَذِبُهُ﴾, that is: it will not harm you.
﴿وَإنْ يَكُ صادِقًا يُصِبْكم بَعْضُ الَّذِي يَعِدُكُمْ﴾ — this is one of the subtle questions, because when a prophet ﷺ makes a promise, the promise comes about in its entirety; not part of it comes about. So the question here is: how was it permissible for him to say "بَعْضُ الَّذِي يَعِدُكم" (some of what he promises you), when the proper wording would be "كُلُّ الَّذِي يَعِدُكم" (all of what he promises you)? This is a mode of argument in which the debater goes about establishing the proof with the least of what the matter involves, and there is no denial in this that all of it will strike. Like this is the poet's saying:
قَدْ يُدْرِكُ المُتَأنِّي بَعْضَ حاجَتِهِ ∗∗∗ وقَدْ يَكُونُ مَعَ المُسْتَعْجِلِ الزَّلَلُ
(The patient one may attain some of his need, and with the hasty one there may be slipping.)
He mentioned "some" only to establish "all" for him — not that "some" is "all" — but rather the speaker, when he says: the least that the patient one gets is attaining part of the need, and the least that the hasty one gets is slipping, has made clear the superiority of the patient one over the hasty one in a way the opponent cannot reject. It is as though the believer of Pharaoh's family said to them: "The least that will be, if he is truthful, is that some of what he promises you will strike you, and in some of that is your destruction." This is its interpretation, and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:29-29.t: ﴿يا قَوْمِ لَكُمُ المُلْكُ اليَوْمَ ظاهِرِينَ في الأرْضِ﴾ — this is the report of the saying of the believer of Pharaoh's family. Allah let them know that the kingdom is theirs while they are dominant over all people; then He let them know that Allah's might is not repelled by any repeller, and no helper can help against it, so he said: ﴿فَمَن يَنْصُرُنا مِن بَأْسِ اللَّهِ إنْ جاءَنا﴾

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿غافِرِ الذَّنْبِ وقابِلِ التَّوْبِ﴾ is in the sense of attributes of Allah. As for the genitive of ﴿شَدِيدِ العِقابِ﴾, it is as a badal (substitute), because it is one of the expressions by which an indefinite noun is described.
And His saying: ﴿ذِي الطَّوْلِ﴾ means "possessor of wealth, bounty and power". You say: "So-and-so has ṭawl over so-and-so" (لِفُلانٍ عَلى فُلانٍ طَوْلٌ), when he has a favour over him.

zajjaj:30-30.t:
﴿مِثْلَ يَوْمِ الأحْزابِ﴾, that is: like the day of party after party. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «يَوْمِ حَزْبِ حِزْبٍ», apparently for «حِزْبٍ حِزْبٍ»; translated as "party after party".] "الأحْزاب" here are the people of Nūḥ, ʿĀd, Thamūd, and those who were destroyed after them and before them.
And the meaning of ﴿مِثْلَ دَأْبِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وعادٍ وثَمُودَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 31] is "like the custom of ..."; and it has come in the commentary: "like the state of the people of Nūḥ", that is: "I fear for you that you persist in your disbelief and then there befalls you what befell the former nations who denied their messengers".

zajjaj:32-32.t:
﴿يَوْمَ التَّنادِ﴾ — "التَّنادِ" with kasra on the dāl. Al-Ḥasan read: "يَوْمَ التَّنادِي" with the yāʾ retained, and most readings have "التَّنادِ". Ibn ʿAbbās read: "يَوْمَ التَّنادِّ" with the dāl doubled. The original is "التَّنادِي"; retaining the yāʾ is the proper way, and dropping it is good and fine, because the kasra indicates the yāʾ, and it is the head of a verse, and the endings of these verses are on dāl. The meaning of "يَوْمَ التَّنادِي" is: "the day on which the people of the Garden call out to the people of the Fire: We have found what our Lord promised us to be true; and the people of the Fire call out to the people of the Garden: Pour some water upon us". It is also permissible — and Allah knows best — that "يَوْمَ التَّنادِ" be the day on which every people is called by its leader. Whoever reads "يَوْمَ التَّنادِّ" with the dāl doubled takes it from their saying "نَدَّ فُلانٌ" and "نَدَّ البَعِيرُ" (so-and-so / the camel bolted), when he runs off headlong; and among what indicates this is His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ مُدْبِرِينَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 33].
And His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ المَرْءُ مِن أخِيهِ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 34] ﴿وَأُمِّهِ وأبِيهِ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 35]. And it has come in the commentary that they will be ordered off to the Fire and will flee, and no protector will protect them from the Fire.

zajjaj:34-34.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جاءَكم يُوسُفُ مِن قَبْلُ بِالبَيِّناتِ﴾, that is: with the miraculous signs. ﴿حَتّى إذا هَلَكَ قُلْتُمْ لَنْ يَبْعَثَ اللَّهُ مِن بَعْدِهِ رَسُولا﴾, that is: you persisted in your disbelief and thought that He would not renew the obligation of proof upon you. ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَن هو مُسْرِفٌ مُرْتابٌ﴾, that is: like that misguidance, Allah leads astray whoever is a transgressor and a doubter. "مُسْرِفٌ" here is: a disbeliever, and "مُرْتابٌ": one doubting the matter of Allah and His prophets.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
﴿الَّذِينَ يُجادِلُونَ في آياتِ اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ سُلْطانٍ أتاهُمْ﴾ — "الَّذِينَ" is in the position of the accusative, referring back to "مَن", that is: "thus Allah leads astray those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any proof that has come to them". It is also permissible that the position of "الَّذِينَ" be nominative, in the sense: "whoever is a transgressor and a doubter — they are those who dispute".
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَبُرَ مَقْتًا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وعِنْدَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾, that is: "their disputing is greatly loathsome with Allah and with those who believe". ﴿كَذَلِكَ يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ قَلْبِ مُتَكَبِّرٍ جَبّارٍ﴾ — and it is read: "عَلى كُلِّ قَلْبٍ مُتَكَبِّرٍ" (with tanwīn on قَلْب). The first is the proper way, because the arrogant one is the person; but it is also possible for you to say "قَلْبٌ مُتَكَبِّرٌ" (an arrogant heart), that is, its owner is arrogant.

zajjaj:36-36.t: ﴿وَقالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يا هامانُ ابْنِ لِي صَرْحًا﴾ — "الصَّرْح" is the palace, and every great building is a ṣarḥ. ﴿لَعَلِّي أبْلُغُ الأسْبابَ﴾ — it has come in the commentary: "the gates of heaven". "الأسْباب" in the language is whatever is connected to a thing; and likewise a rope is called "سَبَب", because things are connected by it. It has also come in the commentary: "the ways of the heavens". So the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "that I may reach what will lead me to the heavens". And "فَأطَّلِعُ" is read with the nominative and the accusative.

zajjaj:37-37.t: ﴿وَإنِّي لأظُنُّهُ كاذِبًا﴾ — this is the saying of Pharaoh. He is saying: even if I claimed that I would look upon the god of Moses, I said this on the basis of Moses's claim, not because I am certain of that. It is related that Hāmān baked bricks for building the tower, and that the first to bake bricks was Hāmān. ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِفِرْعَوْنَ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ﴾ — the position of the kāf is accusative; the meaning is: "the evil of his deed was made attractive to Pharaoh" in the way we have described. ﴿وَصُدَّ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾, that is: he was turned away from the straight path — that is, the straight one — by his disbelief. [Translator's note: the source glosses «المُسْتَقِيمِ» with its feminine «المُسْتَقِيمَةِ», since سَبِيل may be masculine or feminine.] ﴿وَما كَيْدُ فِرْعَوْنَ إلا في تَبابٍ﴾: only in loss. One says: "تَبَّتْ يَداهُ", that is: his two hands have lost.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
﴿وَقالَ الَّذِي آمَنَ يا قَوْمِ اتَّبِعُونِ أهْدِكم سَبِيلَ الرَّشادِ﴾, meaning the path of heading straight to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and I will bring you out of Pharaoh's path. So "أهْدِكم" is jussive (majzūm), as the answer to the imperative; the meaning is: "if you follow me, I will guide you". ﴿لا جَرَمَ أنَّما تَدْعُونَنِي إلَيْهِ لَيْسَ لَهُ دَعْوَةٌ في الدُّنْيا ولا في الآخِرَةِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 43], meaning that it has no answering of a call in this world nor in the Hereafter. Sībawayh said: I asked al-Khalīl about His saying: ﴿لا جَرَمَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 43], and he said: "لا جَرَمَ" is a rejoinder to [previous] speech, and the meaning is: "it is necessary that the Fire is theirs, and it is true that the Fire is theirs". And he recited:
وَلَقَدْ طَعَنْتُ أبا عُيَيْنَةَ طَعْنَةً ∗∗∗ جَرَمَتْ فَزارَةَ بَعْدَها أنْ يَغْضَبُوا
(I struck Abū ʿUyayna a thrust which, after it, made it due for Fazāra to be angry.)
The meaning is: "it earned them anger and made them deserving of anger". So the meaning of "لا جَرَمَ أنَّما تَدْعُونَنِي إلَيْهِ" is: "it has become necessary that what you call me to has no call", that is: "the nullity of its call has become necessary". ﴿وَأنَّ مَرَدَّنا إلى اللَّهِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 43]: our return to Allah has become necessary; and likewise ﴿وَأنَّ المُسْرِفِينَ هم أصْحابُ النّارِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 43].

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ما يُجادِلُ في آياتِ اللَّهِ إلا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ — the meaning is: "in repelling the signs of Allah with falsehood, so as to refute the truth with it, ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾." And the meaning of ﴿فَلا يَغْرُرْكَ تَقَلُّبُهم في البِلادِ﴾ is: let not their safety after their disbelief deceive you, such that they go about as they please, for the end of their disbelief is punishment and destruction.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سُوءُ العَذابِ﴾ ﴿النّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْها﴾ [Ghāfir: 46] — "النّار" is a badal (substitute) from His saying "سُوءُ العَذابِ". It is also permissible that it be nominative by implying an explanation of "سُوءُ العَذابِ", as though someone said: "What is it?", and the answer was: "It is the Fire, to which they are exposed".
If someone says: how are they exposed to it when they are among the people of the Fire? It has come in the commentary that their souls are in the bellies of black birds, exposed to the Fire morning and evening until the Day of Resurrection. Do you not see that after it is ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السّاعَةُ أدْخِلُوا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ أشَدَّ العَذابِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 46]? And it is read: "اُدْخُلُوا" (enter!), in the sense of a command to them to enter, as though: "and on the day the Hour is established He will say: Enter, O family of Pharaoh, the severest punishment". And it was read: "أدْخِلُوا" (make enter!), as a command to the angels to make them enter the severest punishment.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
Then He made clear how that is, and made known that the nations which denied before them were destroyed, by His saying: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهم قَوْمُ نُوحٍ والأحْزابُ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ﴾, meaning ʿĀd, Thamūd, the people of Lūṭ, and the nations that were destroyed between these. ﴿وَهَمَّتْ كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ بِرَسُولِهِمْ لِيَأْخُذُوهُ﴾, that is: to gain power over him and kill him. ﴿وَجادَلُوا بِالباطِلِ لِيُدْحِضُوا بِهِ الحَقَّ﴾, that is: to repel the truth with it.
﴿فَأخَذْتُهُمْ﴾, that is: I made their recompense for intending to seize the messengers that I seized them and punished them. ﴿فَكَيْفَ كانَ عِقابِ﴾, that is: they pass by the places in which the peoples were destroyed and see the traces of destruction.

zajjaj:51-51.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُومُ الأشْهادُ﴾, that is: the angels. Its singular is "شاهِدٌ", like "صاحِبٌ" and "أصْحابٌ".

zajjaj:56-56.t: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُجادِلُونَ في آياتِ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: they dispute in repelling the signs of Allah, without any authority that has come to them, that is: without any proof that has come to them. ﴿إنْ في صُدُورِهِمْ إلا كِبْرٌ ما هم بِبالِغِيهِ﴾, that is: "they will not attain their aim in it", and their aim is repelling the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. What indicates this meaning is "يُجادِلُونَ في آياتِ اللَّهِ", because the pride they have already brought about, so this cannot be confused with [meaning] "attaining the pride". And it has come in the commentary that the Jews are meant by it, and that the pride which they will not attain is expecting the matter of the Dajjāl: they were proud, waiting and expecting the emergence of the Dajjāl, so Allah made known that this group which disputes will not live to see the emergence of the Dajjāl. And what supports the saying of whoever said this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, right after this: ﴿فاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ﴾

zajjaj:6-6.t:
﴿وَكَذَلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ عَلى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾, that is: and like that the word of your Lord came true, meaning by it His saying: ﴿لأمْلأنَّ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ [Hūd: 119].
﴿أنَّهم أصْحابُ النّارِ﴾ — and "إنَّهُمْ" (with kasra) is also permissible.

zajjaj:60-60.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ داخِرِينَ﴾ — its meaning is: humiliated.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, told of the merit of the believers, saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ العَرْشَ ومَن حَوْلَهُ﴾, meaning the angels, ﴿يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ ويُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ ويَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾. So the believer is one for whom the angels brought near seek forgiveness. And it means: ﴿رَبَّنا وسِعْتَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ رَحْمَةً وعِلْمًا فاغْفِرْ لِلَّذِينَ تابُوا واتَّبَعُوا سَبِيلَكَ﴾ — the meaning is: "they say: Our Lord, You encompass all things", that is, the angels say it.
And His saying: ﴿رَحْمَةً وعِلْمًا﴾ is accusative (manṣūb) as tamyīz (specification). ﴿فاغْفِرْ لِلَّذِينَ تابُوا واتَّبَعُوا سَبِيلَكَ﴾, that is: they kept to the path of guidance to which You called.

zajjaj:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿إذِ الأغْلالُ في أعْناقِهِمْ والسَّلاسِلُ﴾ — this is permissible in three ways: "والسَّلاسِلَ" with the accusative, "والسَّلاسِلِ" with the genitive [and "والسَّلاسِلُ" with the nominative]. Whoever reads the nominative conjoins it to "الأغْلالُ"; whoever reads the genitive, the meaning is: "when the shackles are on their necks and [they are] in the chains"; and whoever reads the accusative, giving fatḥa to the lām, reads: "والسَّلاسِلَ يَسْحَبُونَ" (and the chains they drag). [Translator's note: the source names three ways but lists only two before explaining the third (the nominative); the bracketed words supply it.]

zajjaj:75-75.t: ﴿ذَلِكم بِما كُنْتُمْ تَفْرَحُونَ﴾ (the verse). What indicates it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَتْهم رُسُلُهم بِالبَيِّناتِ فَرِحُوا بِما عِنْدَهم مِنَ العِلْمِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 83], that is: that punishment which has befallen you is because you used to rejoice in the falsehood you were in. And "تَمْرَحُونَ", that is: you were insolent, exultant and mocking.

zajjaj:78-78.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أرْسَلْنا رُسُلا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِنهم مَن قَصَصْنا عَلَيْكَ﴾ — it has come in the commentary that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent eight thousand prophets, four thousand of them from the Children of Israel and four thousand from the rest of mankind. And it has come from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said — concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمِنهم مَن لَمْ نَقْصُصْ عَلَيْكَ﴾ — "Allah sent a black prophet, and he is among those whose story is not mentioned in the Quran."

zajjaj:79-79.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الأنْعامَ لِتَرْكَبُوا مِنها ومِنها تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ — "الأنْعام" here are the camels.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَن صَلَحَ مِن آبائِهِمْ وأزْواجِهِمْ وذُرِّيّاتِهِمْ﴾ — "مَن" is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the hāʾ and mīm (the pronoun "-hum") in His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا وأدْخِلْهم جَنّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾, that is: "and admit whoever is righteous". It is also valid for it to be conjoined to the hāʾ and mīm in His saying: ﴿وَعَدْتَهُمْ﴾, so that the meaning would be: "You promised them and You promised whoever is righteous among their fathers".

zajjaj:85-85.t: ﴿فَلَمْ يَكُ يَنْفَعُهم إيمانُهم لَمّا رَأوْا بَأْسَنا﴾ — He is saying: "when they saw the punishment with their own eyes". ﴿سُنَّتَ اللَّهِ﴾ is in the sense of: "Allah laid down this practice (sunna) among all the nations: their faith does not benefit them when they see the punishment". ﴿وَخَسِرَ هُنالِكَ الكافِرُونَ﴾, and likewise: ﴿وَخَسِرَ هُنالِكَ المُبْطِلُونَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 78]. "المُبْطِلُونَ" and "الكافِرُونَ" are losers at that time, and at every time they are losers, but He, Exalted is He, made their loss clear to them when they saw the punishment.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Muʾmin
﷽
﴿حم﴾ ﴿تَنْـزِيلُ الكِتابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ العَزِيزِ العَلِيمِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 2]: the Ḥawāmīm [the sūras beginning with Ḥā Mīm] are all Meccan, revealed in Mecca. The Prophet ﷺ said: «"The likeness of the Ḥawāmīm in the Qur'an is like that of the ḥibara cloaks (striped Yemeni garments) among clothes."» Ibn Masʿūd said: "The Ḥawāmīm are the brocade of the Qur'an."
It has come in the exegesis from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, that there are three views on "حـم". He said: "(حـم) is the greatest name of Allah"; he said: "(حـم) is an oath"; and he said: "(حـم) are the letters of al-Raḥmān, separated." The meaning is: "الـر", "حـم" and "نُونْ" together are equivalent to "اَلرَّحْمَنُ". We have explained the i'rab of the letters of the alphabet at the beginning of al-Baqara.
The reading of it is of two kinds: "حَـمْ", with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, and "حِـمْ", with kasra on the ḥāʾ. As for the mīm, it is quiescent (sākin) in the reading of all the readers except ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, for he read "حَـمَ والكِتابِ" «[Translator's note: «حم والكتاب» is the opening of al-Zukhruf and al-Dukhān, not of this sūra; translated as written.]», with fatḥa on the mīm. This is of two kinds. One of them is that he makes "حَـمَ" a name of the sūra, so he puts it in the accusative without tanwīn, because it is on the pattern of foreign names such as "هابِيلَ" (Abel) and "قابِيلَ" (Cain), and the meaning is "recite Ḥā Mīm (اُتْلُ حَـمَ)". The better [view] is that he gave it fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, where he made it a name of the sūra, and that it is the reproduction (ḥikāya) of letters of the alphabet.
